# Serene Pub — canonical nomenclature

The authoritative vocabulary for Serene Pub's systems: what each term means, which word wins
where two collided, and how to name new things so this does not decay.

**This is a living document and it is tracked deliberately.** Design plans and development
notes are kept out of this repository; nomenclature is the exception, because it is a contract
rather than a plan — contributors, modders and documentation all have to agree on what a word
means, and that agreement has to version alongside the code it describes.

Cite it from documentation and from code comments. **Where the code contradicts it, the code
is wrong** — say so in the comment rather than quietly inventing a third word.

## Maintaining it

- A change that renames a concept updates this file **in the same change**, not afterwards.
- New terms follow §24. Grep first; if the word collides, either pick another or rename the
  other use in the same change.
- A term drawn on a new screen uses its icon from §22; a new icon association is recorded
  there in the same change, and a term that has none goes under _needs an icon_ rather than
  borrowing a neighbour's.
- Mark anything impermanent per **R6** — ⏳ transitional or 🚧 provisional — so it can be
  pruned rather than accumulate.
- The change ledger (§25) tracks renames that are agreed but not yet applied. An entry
  leaves the ledger when the rename lands.

---

## 1. Governing rules

**R1 — One word, one meaning.** Where a word is already load-bearing in one place, the _other_
use renames. Not both.

**R2 — Prefer distinctive words for new concepts.** Every dangerous collision in this codebase
is a generic word — _source, role, key, binding, weight, grant, world_. Every safe one is
distinctive — _gazetteer, receipt, candidate, departed_. An odd word can never be confused
with anything else. Choose the odd one.

**R3 — Qualify, never abbreviate to the bare noun.** _Entry type_, _node definition_, _node kind_ — never bare `type`.
_Signal weight_, _mechanism weight_, _entry weight_ — never `weight`.

**R4 — Casual words must not become type names.** Internal ids stay precise and ugly
(`core:query/world-lore@1`); casual speech says _the world lore query_. `retrievalMode` and
`retrievalStrategy` were two different things one word apart, both since removed — that is the
failure this rule prevents.

**R5 — Reconcile vocabularies at boundaries; never merge them.** Two systems may legitimately
use different words for overlapping sets. Translate at the seam and keep both honest. Merging
them is how six of eight retrieval sources were silently dropped.

**R6 — Mark vocabulary that is not permanent, so the canon can be pruned rather than accrete.**
Three kinds, and they expire differently:

- ⏳ **Transitional** — real today, expires on a known event. _Parity_, _open_, _departed_ die
  when 0.6 ships and the legacy path goes. Delete them then; do not maintain them.
- 🚧 **Provisional** — designed but not built, so the words may still move on contact with
  implementation. The **Knowledge** vocabulary is provisional today.
- ⏸ **Paused** — built, then switched off by the owner; expires when it is either revived or retired.

A canon that never loses words stops describing the system and starts describing its history.
Anything unmarked is permanent and should be treated as expensive to change.

---

## 2. Identifier grammar

```
<namespace>:<kind>/<name>@<major>       core:query/world-lore@1
```

- **namespace** — `core` for first-party; a plugin's own otherwise.
- **kind** — `spec`; the five node kinds `inlet`, `query`, `task`, `oracle`, `outlet` (§4);
  `entry`, `shape`, `policy`, `vec`, `var`, `genre`, `script`, `extract`, `notification` (app-side:
  `core:notification/<slug>@1`, declared with `defineNotificationKind`, §25). The other registries
  (`event`, `slot`, `sheet`, `stat-shape`, `template`, `verdict`, …) use the same shape.
- **name** — kebab-case, singular.
- **major** — the pin. Version lives _in the id_, so every call site names it.

**Spec documents** carry a semver (`core:spec/chat-respond` at `1.21.0`) because they are published
documents; **types** carry an integer major because they are pinned contracts.

**Spec ids — genre first** (ruled 2026-10-05, C4). A core pipeline that serves one genre is
`core:spec/<genre>-<what>` (`chat-respond`, `lair-build-room`, `adventure-turn-order`); one that
serves every genre is `core:spec/<what>` (`summarize-scene`, `builtin-delete`, `set-annex-field`).
`<genre>` is the genre id's own name (`core:genre/chat` → `chat-`), and the same job keeps the same
`<what>` in every genre (`-create`, `-respond`, `-answer-form`, `-turn-order`). **The prefix is
load-bearing**: retiring a genre culls its pipelines by `core:spec/<genre>-*` (`retiredGenres.ts`),
so a genre pipeline without it outlives its genre, and a shared pipeline's id never starts with a
genre's name. A plugin's ids live in its own namespace (`showcase.whodunit:spec/respond`), where its
genre is already said. Ids are internal (R4); people see the **pipeline name**, below.

**Pipeline names** (ruled 2026-10-05, C2). A pipeline's display name (`CORE_SPECS[].name`, rewritten
into `pipeline_specs.name` at every boot) says what the pipeline does, with **no genre qualifier**:
_Reply_, _Create session_, _Answer a form_, _Turn order_, _Narrate_ — never _Lair turn_,
_Turn order (Chat)_ or _Summarize: scene_. Wherever pipelines of several genres are listed, the
genre is shown beside the name (Admin › Pipelines' **Genre** column and filter), so four genres' _Reply_ never need their names to tell them apart.

## 3. The groups

| Group           | Owns                                                       |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Pipeline**    | spec execution — nodes, ports, the executor, receipts      |
| **Catalog**     | declared types and published specs                         |
| **Config**      | values, scopes, overrides, notices                         |
| **Retrieval**   | finding and ranking what goes in the prompt                |
| **Content**     | lorebooks, entries, bindings                               |
| **Session**     | messages, channels, cast, scenes                           |
| **Connections** | adapters, capabilities, sampling                           |
| **Indexing**    | the embedding and annotation lanes                         |
| **Extensions**  | plugins, hooks, scripts                                    |
| **Measurement** | parity, corpora, the A/B tool                              |
| **Knowledge**   | presence, perspective, temporality _(designed, not built)_ |
| **Media**       | images, attachments, thumbnails                            |
| **Graph**       | narrative nodes and relationships                          |
| **Shell**       | the rail, sidebar views, widths, Jump — §26                |
| **Rulesets** 🚧 | rulesets and what they define — §24 (proposed), §28 (the interface's words) |

## 4. Pipeline

| Term                         | Means                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **spec** 📘                            | A published pipeline document. Versioned by semver.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **picture pipeline** 🚧 | **Named 2026-10-12 (DESIGN-image-generation §0; row added by §16 follow-up D3).** A spec whose outlet produces **media** — today **Image** (`core:spec/chat-generate-image`), **Portrait** (`core:spec/character-portrait`), **Scene** (`core:spec/chat-illustrate-scene`, `core:spec/adventure-illustrate-scene`) and **Sprite set fill** (`core:spec/sprite-set-fill`). A description of what a spec does, not a type: nothing stores or checks it. Casual: _the Portrait pipeline_. ⚠ Not a _mode_ (SillyTavern's image-generation modes are a boundary word, R5): there is no mode switch — each purpose is its own spec with its own slots. Not a **loadout** (the model a step runs on, §10), and not a **workflow** (a ComfyUI graph, §10). |
| **node** 📘                            | One step in a spec.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **node kind**                          | The closed effect classes, **ruled 2026-09-14**: **inlet** 📘 (run entry) · **query** 📘 (reads) · **task** 📘 (pure transform) · **oracle** 📘 (calls out to an external nondeterministic source — a model, TTS, image gen, embeddings, a human) · **outlet** 📘 (the only effect-capable kind: writes, attaches, emits — the run leaves into the world here). A sixth, **entry**, is the lorebook entry-type family riding the same registry and is not a pipeline kind. ⚠ Not a "type" — see **node definition** (§5). **Landed in code 2026-09-16** (plans/30 §U3, migration 0134): `Kind` in `descriptors.ts`, `pipeline_nodes.kind`, the builder verbs `.inlet() .query() .task() .oracle() .outlet()`, `TaskCtx`/`OracleCtx`/`OutletCtx`, and every definition id (`core:inlet/…`, `core:oracle/…`, `core:outlet/…` — the kind is part of the id grammar, 01 §3a). Every stored document was rewritten and republished once. _fan-out_ was never a kind — parallelism is the **gather** clause.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **port** 📘                            | A node's declared input or output.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **slot**                     | A declared parameter address a config value can fill. ⚠ Unqualified, _slot_ is always this one. The stats vocabulary's is an **attribute slot** and is always said in full (§9). Its SDK registry says the qualified word in every exported name (`defineAttributeSlot`, `getAttributeSlot`, `attributeSlots()`), so nothing in an import list collides with the pipeline `slot()` address helper. The **slot kinds** are a closed set: `connection · sampling · prompts · template · parameters · wire · variables · scripts · settings`. A `params` slot's fields are **shared** or **own** (2026-09-16, R-7 P2 refined): a field the definition marks `shared: true` resolves at the owner a `slot.params({ node })` reference names and renders once, on the owner; an unmarked field is the node's own through the same reference — resolved at its own address, rendered on its own step.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **settings slot**            | **Ruled 2026-09-15 (R-9), built 2026-09-16.** The one slot kind **the substrate declares** and no author may (the name is reserved; `register` refuses it): `enabled` on every `optional` definition, `review` on every definition whose `effects` gate (default = its `reviewDefault`), and `mode` on every **gather** clause. Projected onto the registry row by `snapshotRegistry` (`settingsSlotFor`) and declared for a clause by `clauseSettingsSlotFor` — a clause has no row, so the SDK is its declaration's home. **Not hashed** (`authoredSlots`): it is derived from `optional`/`effects`, which are. Addresses unchanged: `<nodeKey>.settings.enabled` / `.review`, `<clauseId>.settings.mode`. ⚠ Not a _substrate key_ — that was the word for these while nothing declared them (plans/29 §7 R-9); retired.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **script point**                       | **Interior point** (18 §4e): a declared **seam** inside a binding: a named moment in its work where a user chain may run (`ctx.scripts.applyText(key, text)`), declared on the definition as `scriptPoints: [{ key, accepts, label, description? }]`. Since R-11 (built 2026-09-16) a point **declares what it accepts** — script kind ids, hashed like a port hook's `accepts` — and the executor hands that list to the applier; the bare-string spelling (`'each-draft'`) is **refused** at `register()` — retired without an alias (2026-09-27) — and `scriptPointsOf` is the one reader of the declared list. Its **seam address** is its key. ⚠ Not a port-hook seam — that is a `scripts` slot's (port, phase), addressed `in:<port>` / `out:<port>`, which the substrate applies at; a point is the binding's to invoke.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **seam**                             | **Named 2026-10-10 (PLAN-script-placement-and-catalogue D1).** A place a script chain may run: a **port hook** (a `scripts` slot's port and phase) or a **script point**. Declared on the definition, never stored; `seamsOf(definition)` is the one reader, in run order (`in:` seams, then points, then `out:` seams). _(was: **hook site**, §23; the type `ScriptHookSite` keeps its name this release ⏳)_ ⚠ R5's _translate at the seam_ and other prose uses of _seam_ for a boundary between two systems are plain English, not this term. |
| **seam address**                     | **Named 2026-10-10 (D1).** The one spelling of a seam in labels, receipts and the catalogue: `in:<port>` (a slot with `phase: 'before'`) · `out:<port>` (`phase: 'after'`) · `<pointKey>` (a script point). Type `SeamAddress`; `ScriptHookSite.at`. ⚠ Not a storage address: chains stay stored at `config[nodeKey][slotName]['']` and `config[nodeKey].scripts[point]`. UI label: _Scripts · before text_ / _after text_ / _at each draft_. |
| **script map**                       | **Named 2026-10-10 (D3, R-Q1).** The read-only, run-order view of every seam in a pipeline and the chain attached to each (plus a connection's stop guards on `text/stop` seams), the **Scripts** tab beside **Configure** in the admin pipeline workspace. Computed from declarations + config; nothing stored. |
| **unplaced** (a chain)               | **Named 2026-10-10 (D4, R-Q4).** A stored chain whose seam no longer resolves on its definition. Marked, never culled: UI _no longer here_; listed under **Unplaced** in the script map and the Admin › Scripts **Use** filter; the executor skips it with a note, and **halts** the run when it holds a `text/stop` script. ⚠ Never _orphaned_, which is the config-address word for a value whose option is gone (and is culled). |
| **executor**                 | Runs a spec against scope data.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **run**                      | **One spec execution.**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **turn**                     | **One exchange with the user.** May contain several runs — respond, narrate, summarize. ⚠ _Not_ a synonym for run.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **step**                     | A node as placed in a pipeline, and each run of it (widened 2026-09-30, owner ruling Q9 — the settings, the **streaming step**, the **step status** and the **step label** all name a node as placed). ⚠ Not a **node definition**: one definition is placed as many steps. |
| **receipt** 📘                         | The durable record of a run: nodes, outcomes, decisions, diagnostics.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **halt**                     | A run that stopped deliberately. **Not a failure.**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **preview**                  | A run that stops before generating; nothing is sent, nothing is saved. Since 2026-09-15 a preview is a **dry run** — see below — so the outlets before the halt run and commit nothing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **dry run**                  | **Ruled 2026-09-15 (09-B B4, R-21 (1)).** A run whose outlets perform no writes: `ctx.commit` returns a **synthetic id** (`dry:<nodeKey>`) and reaches no host, the receipt's node row says `dry`, and the event the write would have caused is recorded flagged `dry` rather than emitted. `RunOptions.dry`; every preview is one. ⚠ Not a **preview** — a preview also halts; a dry run may go to the end.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **placeholder**              | **Ruled 2026-09-15 (R-17).** The reply row a pipeline creates for itself at an outlet straight after the inlet (`create-message` with `generating: true`; node key `placeholder`), empty and generating, filled by the spec's last outlet (`update-message`, key `save`). The create → update pair on that one row is **one live row** (F7, restated W1 2026-09-23; was _one primary row_). The trigger inserts nothing. ⚠ In prose _placeholder_ is this row; the `{{char:N}}` cast placeholder is a **tag** (§8).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **live row**                 | **Ruled 2026-09-15 (R-21 (2)).** The row the most recent live-row outlet committed in a run — the placeholder, on a reply — as the executor tells the host on every oracle call (`RunFacts.liveRow`). Where core routes an oracle's stream (the oracle stays blind to messages), and what Stop finalises. Declared per outlet (`Descriptor.liveRow`), and opened only by a write still being written — `generating` fed, or a claimed `row` (`LIVE_ROW_PORTS`, `opensLiveRow`, W1 2026-09-23); a complete message from the same outlet is an ordinary write. At most one per run (F7). `seed-greetings` writes N rows and is nobody's live row.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **derelict reply**           | **Built 2026-09-30 (plan lorebooks-consolidation A9 leftover).** A message row still generating whose run died with the process that ran it (a crash, a kill). Boot's `replies` startup task settles it (`sessions/derelictReplies.ts`: `settleDerelictReplies`, `reconcileDerelictReplies`) the way a failed run settles its row — the text that arrived stays, `error.message` is `DERELICT_REPLY_SENTENCE` (_The server restarted before this reply finished._) — and hands its session to the embedding queue. Only rows last written before the process started. ⚠ Not a **stopped** reply (a person pressed Stop: `generationOutcome: 'stopped'`), and never _stranded_ — that word is the story calendar's (dates a calendar has no room for). |
| **one road**                 | **Ruled 2026-09-15 (09-B B4).** Every reply runs end to end — inlet → placeholder → … → oracle → save — through `utils/runReply.ts`. ⚠ **Retired:** the _adapter road_ / _preview-halt road_ (`generateResponse`: halt at the payload, the connection adapter sends and streams into the trigger's row) and the _second road_ (`runReplyToCompletion` with `fillMessageId`). Never reintroduce a trigger-side message insert.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **run kind**                 | **2026-09-16 (U1 review, W3).** What a registered run is FOR, as the message's own Stop reads it: **reply** (a turn filling a message row — `runReply`), **action** (a contributed function a person triggered — `sessions:triggerFunction`: a render, a summary), **maintenance** (nothing a person watches from the composer; reserved, nothing registers one yet). `RunHandle.kind` (`RunKind`). **Pr-6 sprint 2 (2026-10-25):** the SDK now owns the union — `RUN_KINDS` / `RunKind` (`sdk/src/status.ts`: reply · action · routine · maintenance), which the app's `runRegistry` re-exports — and every `sessions:runStatus` frame carries it (`RunStatusFrame.kind`, `StatusRelayOptions.kind`; the kind is the registry's, `runKindOf`, else the trigger family's, `runKindOfFamily`); the page's `generating` (`generatingOf`) counts only `reply` and `action`, never `routine` or `maintenance`. Stop is **row-scoped**: `cancelSession` stops a run whose live row is among the released rows, or a reply that has no row yet — never a session-mate's render. ⚠ Not a **node kind**, not a **stop kind**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **gather branch**            | One member chain of a **gather** clause (`gather.worldLore.read`). ⚠ Not a "lane".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **host service**             | Something a node may call out to (a database read, a model call).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **handler** 📘                         | The function a node definition is bound to. Reads an `input` and returns a result; owns no I/O of its own. ⚠ Never "the binding" — see §8.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **structural compatibility** | A handler may be bound to **any node definition that supplies everything it reads**. Nothing is said about the other direction: a definition may supply names the handler ignores. That asymmetry is what lets one handler serve several definitions — it is written against the **intersection** of what they supply. Checked by the compiler for core (`InputOf<C>`, `SharedInput<[A, B]>`) and as data everywhere the compiler cannot reach (`structuralCompat`) — a plugin binding another plugin's handler, the admin-side orchestrator. ⚠ Not "type compatibility": nothing is compared by name or by nominal identity.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **scope data**               | The data a run reads, derived from a session. _(was: `world`)_                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **clause**                   | **Ruled 2026-09-15** (_was_ **block**, the container sense). A container of nodes with a repetition or branching rule of its own: **gather** (several chains collected — _was_ `async`; `mode: sequential\|parallel` is a setting, and by the equivalence law it is unobservable), **each** (once per item — _was_ `map`), **loop** (until a predicate says stop), **junction** (the branches whose predicates fired, any subset, optional default — _was_ `route`). Not a node — a clause publishes under its own id and its members are addressed through it, and **nodes and clauses share one address space**: a clause id may not equal a node key (the builder refuses it). **Landed in code 2026-09-16** with the kinds: `pipeline_clauses` (was `pipeline_blocks`), `ClauseKind`, `.gather() .each() .loop() .junction()`, `BuiltClause`, `clauseId`/`clauseKind`/`clauseChain`, a junction's `branches` (was `routes`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **tool**                     | A **named, read-only function a model may ask for by name.** Canonically an extension's sandboxed hook; core ships four. A tool is not a node: it is dispatched by `core:oracle/run-tool@1`, which is. ⚠ Never a synonym for a node, a hook or a script — a hook is _how_ a tool is usually implemented, not what the word means.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **advertisement**            | What the model is told about its tools, in one of two forms: the **prompt door** (written into the context, for models that never heard of tools) or the **native door** (handed to the API's own tool field). One `advertise-tools` node publishes both.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **tool loop**                | A `loop` clause whose predicate is "the model asked for a tool" — generate, read the answer back, run the tool, prompt again with the result. **The bounded agentic turn.** Its ceiling is mandatory. The reference spec (`core:spec/tool-loop`, exported by core-catalog as an example and test fixture; not seeded since 2026-10-05) keys it `tools` (landed 2026-09-16; was `agent` — _agent_ is the Adventure roles' word, §9), and the query that lists what the install offers is keyed `available` so `$.tools` names one thing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **iteration**                | One pass of an `each` or `loop` clause's body. Numbered from 0, and the number is on every step's receipt row (`iteration`) — which is what makes "the third pass timed out" answerable.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **carry**                    | What one iteration of a loop can read of the ones before it: the clause's own accumulating output (`$.tools.values`), and nothing else. An iteration never sees another's intermediate node values.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **ceiling**                  | A repeating block's declared `max`. Hitting it is recorded (`stopped: 'ceiling'`) rather than inferred, because a truncated loop otherwise looks exactly like a finished one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **verdict**                  | **Ruled 2026-09-17 (01 §13; plans/31 V4).** The **one function that judges a rule**: a declaration — `core:verdict/<slug>`, the law it comes from (`R-20`, `F39`), the **doors** that hear it, a `judge` over one input, and a failing input the conformance kit feeds through every door (C27) — registered with the SDK's `defineVerdict` and enumerated by `verdicts()`. Seven are core's: `i18n` (R-20) · `enablement` (U5e) · `audience` (R-15) · `settings-travel` (F39) · `provisional` (R-2) · `effects-line` (F41) · `staleness` (U5f). The verdict **owns the sentence**; a door quotes it and composes nothing. The judge's answer is a **verdict result** (`VerdictResult`: `ok`, or the `sentence` and the `fix`), never itself "the verdict". ⚠ Not a **decision** (§7, selection's answer on a candidate), not Whodunit's _Verdict_ spec (the game's finding, §9), not Battleship's **call verdict** (a shot's answer), and not the capability answer `satisfies()` returns (`capabilities.ts` `Verdict`, ⏳ the type name predates the ruling and is the reason the registered shape is `VerdictDecl`). ⏳ The app's `audienceVerdict()` / `enablementVerdict()` (`sessionActions.ts`) and the types `EnabledWhenVerdict` · `AudienceVerdict` · `EnablementVerdict` name the _answer_ and are the app's **doors** — renamed when V5 builds the app host, not before. |
| **door**                     | **Ruled 2026-09-17 (01 §13; plans/31 V4).** Where a rule is **heard** — the closed list `Door` in `sdk/src/verdicts.ts`: **construction** (an author building a document or declaration: the builder, `genre()`, `announce.build()`) · **registry** (`register()`, the `define*` doors, a host reading its registry against what it can run) · **validate** (`validate()`) · **publish** (a host's `saveDocument`, the packager, an install) · **run** (the executor) · **fire** (a host's action fire) · **write** (a host's message write) · **list** (a listing or affordance — the action list, a client drawing a control grey or a form collapsed). A verdict declares every door that hears it, host doors included; C27 holds a host to the ones it has and names the rest. _A door that re-derives a rule is a defect._ ⚠ Not the **prompt door** / **native door** (§4 _advertisement_, how a model is told about tools), not the **structured door** (§10, how a step asks for JSON), and not a UI _door_ into a lorebook lens (§22) — each of those is a qualified compound and stays; the bare noun is this one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **streaming step** · **step status**   | **Built 2026-09-27 (lair pass B3/B18).** Declared on a node's `expose`: `stream: true` marks the **oracle** whose prose streams into the **live row** — at most one per _execution path_ (exclusive junction branches may each have one), never JSON, never inside `each` / `loop` (the `validate()` law _streaming step_); `status` is the node's **step status**, the progress line shown from its start and winning over the handler's own `ctx.status`. The host reads `streamingSteps(doc)` and `stepStatuses(doc)`. ⚠ Renamed from _streaming stage_ · _stage status_ 2026-09-28 (§23): **stage** is the reading column only.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **step label** · **step purpose** | **Built 2026-09-30 (config grouping, owner rulings Q5).** Declared on a node's `expose` beside the step status, both optional display text (R-20), hashed with the document — a spec that sets neither hashes as before. `label` is the **step label**: the step's own name wherever the settings name it — the heading of the **settings group** its model call leads (§6), its legend among Advanced settings — winning over the step status and the node definition's `i18n.name`; any step may carry one. `purpose` is the **step purpose**: one or two sentences under that heading, saying what the call is for, allowed only on a _model call_ — an oracle whose definition declares a `connection` slot (SDK `isModelCall`; law _step purpose_, refused at construction and by `validate()`). An `assemble` step's `connection` slot names the model its prompt is formatted for; it calls none. ⚠ Not the **step status** (progress prose shown while the step runs). |
| **scenes first** 🚧 | **Ruled 2026-11-10 (owner direction, verbatim: "We want to make sure we are encouraging pipelines/modders to be targeting scenes first for granular history updates, then history entries second, optimally compiling from scenes to history entries.").** **Purpose:** history is compiled, not written. Pipelines put story events into scenes (a story line, or a **scene note** through `note-scene@1`), and a person's Compile files a day's scenes under the day's one history entry (§8 **one history entry per date**). A direct history write is the second choice and lands on the day's entry (**a pipeline's history write**, below). Compile stays a person's press (lead default S3). Taught by the outlet contract (`contracts/src/outlets.ts`: _History is compiled, not written_), the SDK guides (_Story events: scenes first_) and INTEGRATING §1l; checked by `W_WRITES_HISTORY` and **C40**. **Not:** a lock: a history write still works, and every refusal is in words (P1). |
| **Bench or bring back a seat** (`core:outlet/set-seat-bench@1`, contracts export `setSeatBench`) 🚧 | **Built 2026-11-10/11 (owner rulings; PROPOSAL-benched-seats-2026-11-10, lane bench-L3).** An outlet: in-ports `seat` (`seated-member:<id>` · `player-seat:<id>` · `character:<id>`) · `benched` (JSON boolean), out `main` · `seat` · `seats`; `effects: write`, `reviewDefault: off`, `review: { fields: [] }`. It benches a seat or brings it back through `setSeatBench` (§9 **benched seat**); it adds no message. Allowed only where the genre declares `writes.seats` (absent = off). UI name _Bench or bring back a seat_. Refused in words: _This session's genre ('‹name›') does not bench or bring back seats._ (`seatWriteRefusal`); host halts _there was no benched true or false, so no seat was benched_ · _'‹given›' is not a seat in this session, so nothing was benched_. Taken back with its turn (a `seat-bench` **session imprint**, §9). ⚠ Not **Note it in the scene**'s scene notes; not a person's Bench button. |
| **Note it in the scene** (`core:outlet/note-scene@1`, SDK `noteScene`) 🚧 | **Built 2026-11-10 (owner ★S4; contract lane hist-C, host lane hist-B2).** An outlet: in-ports `text` · `scene` · `sources`, out `main`, `effects: 'write'`. It appends a **scene note** (§8) to the run channel's open scene, or a named one; it adds no message and never writes history. UI label 🚧 (★C-1) _Note it in the scene_, which avoids _Notes_ (**Session notes**, §24). Refused in words: _a note needs text._ · _this genre keeps no scenes._ · lore writes Off (the existing sentence) · _there is no scene ‹x›._ · _that scene belongs to another session._ · _no scene is open to note; open one first (propose-scene-cue@1)._ · _‹node› has no session to note a scene in — …_ |
| **a pipeline's history write** · `fileOntoHistoryDay` · _filed onto ‹date›'s entry_ 🚧 | **Built 2026-11-10 (owner ★H1 reuse; lead default S1 append; fourth-round ruling "The session's story 'now'"; lanes hist-B1, hist-G).** `create-lore-entry@1` with a history entry type goes through `fileOntoHistoryDay` (`runtime/host.ts`). The date is the write's `fields` year, else the session's story now taken literally (★G-3). Then `assertDateLands` → `historyDayOwnerRefusal` → `historyEntryOfDate(create: true)`, and the day entry's content gains the write as a paragraph through the imprinted `changeLoreEntry`, so a retake reverts it and removes an entry the write made (stamped `provenance: "pipeline"`). `match` is ignored; when the day's entry already existed the receipt says _filed onto ‹date›'s entry_. Refused 🚧: _‹node›: a history date needs a year. Give this write a year in its fields, or leave the date out to use the story's day._ (a month or day with no year) · _‹node›: history needs a date. Give this write a year in its fields, or give the story a dated history entry first._ (no year and no story now) · rule C's sentence on or before a fork date. A history re-date through `update-lore-entry@1` gets the lock, `assertDateLands`, `assertHistoryDateFree(exceptId)` and `assertRedateKeepsLines`, only when the date changes. The chat tool `write_entry` refuses history: _History comes from scenes: capture the moment and compile it, or write world lore._ **Not:** a second entry for the day, ever. |
| **`W_WRITES_HISTORY`** · **C40** (`historyWriteFindings`) · `declaredNodeParams` 🚧 | **Built 2026-11-10 (lead default S6: a warning, not an error; lanes hist-C, hist-D1).** `W_WRITES_HISTORY` is the packager's warning (`cli/src/compiler.ts`) on a `create-lore-entry` node whose resolved entry type is `core:entry/history`: _writes history entries directly — history is compiled from scenes_. A document with a `summarize-request` inlet is exempt: its save is previewed. Conformance law **C40** (_scenes first_, `conformance/src/index.ts`) runs the same predicate (`historyWriteFindings`) over the shipped catalogue. Both read node params through `declaredNodeParams(doc, nodeKey)` (`sdk/src/document.ts`, exported), which C39 now shares. **Not:** an error: the package still builds. |
| `update-cast-member@1`'s **cast state** (`nodeState` · `nodeVisibility` in `changes`) · `NODE_VISIBILITIES` 🚧 | **Built 2026-11-10 (plan item 5; contract lane hist-C, host lane hist-B2).** _Change a cast member_ may set `nodeState` (checked against `CAST_STATE_WORDS`: active · deceased · missing · departed) and `nodeVisibility` (normal · legendary · hidden; `NODE_VISIBILITIES` in `runtime/castMember.ts`), dated and tied to the turn like its other changes; `{ follow: true }` is refused for both. Refused: _'‹value›' is not a cast state; …_ · _'‹value›' is not a cast visibility; …_ |


### Registrations, routines and cadences 🚧 (built 2026-10-20/21)

The layering restructure's words (PROPOSAL-layering-restructure §6, rulings R1–R48; built by lanes 1–9). Each was grepped across both repositories before it was ruled; every one is 🚧 until SDK 1.0 (0.7). Members read only the interface words in the last column of each row's sentence; the rest is code and admin canon.

| Term | Means |
| --- | --- |
| **registration** 🚧 📘 | _This trigger runs this pipeline._ `RegistrationDecl { key, trigger, pipeline, when?, values?, order?, mode?, allowStacking?, caps?, label? }`, made with `register(trigger, pipeline, opts)` from declared objects (an event, an **action handle**, a **cadence**; the spec or `use('…')`). Lives in **the genre's defaults**, a preset's changes, or a session's rows — the app's `registrations` table (0108: `scope_kind` genre · preset · session, `origin` genre · preset · `package:<id>` · admin · upgrade · owner · pub · routine-state; a **registering**, **change** or **drop** row). Replaces the pipeline sense of _binding_ (§23). ⚠ Not _registering a node definition_ (the registry's sense, `describe*Definition`; descriptors.ts's private `registrationFindings` map is that one): say "registers a definition" there, "a registration" here. |
| **registration key** 🚧 | DERIVED, never typed: `<trigger key>→<pipeline key>` (`registrationKeyOf`, `triggerKeyOf`, `REGISTRATION_KEY_JOIN` = `→`) — core ids contribute bare names (`message-respond→story-respond`, `every-n-turns→story-sweep`), other packages keep their namespace (`message-respond→acme.dice:roll`). Unchanged by a cadence's options or a `when` (A8), so session values and the queue survive an edit; changing the trigger or the pipeline is another registration. Admin instance-wide edits are genre-scope change rows keyed **`admin:<key>`**. |
| **trigger family** 🚧 | **event** · **action** · **routine** (`TriggerFamily`, `TRIGGER_FAMILIES`; open — Live is to be a fourth, R47); recorded on every run (`pipeline_runs.trigger_family`, receipt `triggerFamily`, `registrationKey`). ⚠ Bare _trigger_ stays retired (§23, 2026-09-28): always "trigger family", or the trigger's own noun. |
| **event pipeline** · **action pipeline** · **routine** 🚧 📘 | The three kinds of pipeline (R7): one fires when what it listens to fires; one when a person invokes its action; a **routine** when its **cadence** says so (owner's word, 2026-10-20). A routine enters through **`core:inlet/routine@1`** (`C.routine`; ports `session`, `routine` — where it resides, `RoutineFiring` — `cause`, `ruleset`, and one per entity kind), carries no opinionated data (R9), exists only inside sessions, acts with the session owner's authority (A14: receipt _routine ‹name›, for ‹owner›_), and never wakes itself or another (R19). ⚠ Not a **task** (a node kind, §4) and not the retired **background task** (§23). |
| **cadence** 🚧 📘 | When a routine is due (R5, R16): `CadenceRef { id, options }` — `core:cadence/<name>@1`: `every-n-turns` · `after-each-turn` · `after-each-round` · `after-each-scene` · `when-idle` · `on-event` · `when-value` · `system-cron` · `timeline-cron` · `schedule` · `every-n-rounds` (`coreCadences`; builders `everyNTurns`, `everyNRounds`, `afterEachTurn`, …); a plugin's through the script kind **`core:script:cadence/due@1`** (`definePluginCadence`). Answers due-or-not (`cadenceDue`), passes no data; evaluated only at the moments it **wakes on**. Members never read the word (_When it runs: Every 5 turns_, `cadenceWords`); admins see **Cadence**. The one cadence choice an owner makes: a routine on after-each-turn / after-each-round may run on the other (**When it runs**, R52; `TURN_OR_ROUND_CADENCES`, a session change row's `trigger_ref`, key unchanged). ⚠ The plugin schedule tick's payload field `cadence: 'hourly'` (§25, 2026-10-02) is a value of that hook, not this concept. |
| **System Cron** · **Timeline Cron** · **Schedule** 🚧 | The crons (R10, R15, R20): real time on the 5-minute grid (minutes in multiples of 5); story time on the session's story clock (at least one minute, never seconds); set moments — once, daily, weekly, monthly, annually — on either clock (`clock: 'system' \| 'story'`). ⚠ _Timeline Cron_ is the owner's ruled display name (R10) and the one place the word stands near the clock: the clock is the **story clock** (§9), the option value `'story'` (`'timeline'` retired, §23), and bare _timeline_ stays banned (§9). |
| **jump ceiling** 🚧 | `maxJump` on a story-time cron (R19), label **Skip when the clock jumps more than …**; a skipped move is an **inspector line** (_Skipped: the clock jumped 3 days (more than 12 hours)_). A long jump otherwise fires each due cron once (R17). |
| **routine mode** 🚧 | **Off** · **Review** · **Full** (`RoutineMode`; R37) — the lorebook write-mode triple on purpose. Anyone with the session's settings picks it; the preset sets the default; a routine left Off stays listed (R8). |
| **Allow stacking** 🚧 | `allowStacking`, off by default (R18): off, a firing that finds the same routine **waiting** is refused (_Skipped: already waiting_, `ALREADY_WAITING`); one arriving while it **runs** still queues one. An admin's (R36). |
| **cron caps** 🚧 | The two limits on system-clock routines (R11): **idle cron timeout** and **most cron runs in a row** — `system_settings.cron_idle_timeout_minutes` (4320) · `cron_max_runs_in_row` (12), the same on `user_settings` (nullable, ≤ system), a routine's own `caps` (≤ both; `capsOf`, `EffectiveCaps`, `capsPause`). UI **Background routines** (_Stop after nobody has played for (minutes)_, _Most runs in a row_; `userSettings:updateRoutineCaps`, `systemSettings:updateRoutineCaps`); a paused routine says _Paused: no one has played for 3 days_ / _Paused after 12 runs in a row_. |
| **interaction** 🚧 | What resets the cron counts and resumes a session's system-clock routines (R11, R21): a member's line, an action a person fires, a form answer, a settings change, **Run now** (`noteInteraction`, `InteractionKind` line · action · form · setting · run-now). After a restart a session's system-clock routines are **paused since restart** (`PAUSED_SINCE_RESTART`) until one; a **resumed** session counts from it. |
| **routine queue** 🚧 | Per session, one routine at a time, in order, only once every action and event run (and what it set off) has resolved (R13, R14; `RoutineQueue`, a **firing**); across sessions the model queue serves interactive work, then events, then routines (A13, R26: `LLM_PRIORITY` 0 · 1 · 2, `priorityOfFamily`, `withRunFamily`). |
| **Run now** 🚧 | The session owner fires an enabled routine by hand from the composer's **Routines** menu (R39; `sessions:runRoutine`); counts as an interaction, queues like any firing. |
| **session moments** 🚧 | The host-raised events routines wake on: `core:event/turn-ended@1` · `round-ended@1` · `scene-opened@1` · `scene-closed@1` · `story-clock-moved@1` (off the ledger, `OFF_LEDGER`), and the host-only **system tick** on the 5-minute grid (managed service `routines`). Every line on a **lane** **takes a turn** of that lane (R51) when it is not a greeting, goal or system row, nor written by a routine (⚠ not the Messages widget's **turn line**), recorded with its speaker in the **turn tally** (`sessions.metadata.turnTally`, `routines/turnTally.ts`: `TurnTallyV1`, `LaneTally`, `tallyTurn`, `NARRATOR_SPEAKER` = `narrator`); a **round** (R52, the story's lane `main`) ends once every **active speaker** — the turn order's candidates and the speakers its prepared entries name, plus every person who spoke this round — has had a turn. `turn-ended` carries `lane` · `turn` · `round` · `turnsBy`; `round-ended` `round` · `speakers`; core's turn cadences count the story's lane. Published as `session.turn` · `session.round` · `session.lastSpeaker` · `session.turnsBy` (`sessionOf(genre).turn` …, cadence and ruleset scripts' `session`). ⚠ Not the ruleset handler's **round** (`rulesets/rounds.ts`, one reply from the story's side — what a timed piece counts): an R1 collision, flagged. **Seat changes of a turn (lane s4-follow-c, 2026-11-09, owner "Yes, a read genres opt into"):** a genre that declares 🚧 `SessionShape.turnSeatChanges: true` (off in core, P1) gets 🚧 `turnSeatChanges: TurnSeatChange[]` on `turn-ended` and on `RoutineCause` — the seats added, removed or changed (switched on/off, portrayal moved; a reorder is not a change) since the previous turn-taking line of the same lane landed, netted per seat, envoys left out. 🚧 `TurnSeatChange { ref, seatKind, castMemberId, change: 'added' \| 'removed' \| 'changed' }` (@experimental). Derived from the `session_changes` ledger the one seat writer records into (`seatChangesOfTurn`, `sessionReadsSeatChanges`, `turnLineWhere`; `latestLandingId` · `latestChangeIdAtOrBefore` · `SeatEventRow` · `seatEventRowsBetween` in `messages/sessionChanges.ts`; ⏳ `TurnSeatChangeRead`). ⚠ Not `CastChangePayload`, not the host's `SeatChange` (§9 seat writer), not Dungeon Crawler's `plan.seatChanges` (slot writes). |
| **carried entities** · **entity kind** 🚧 | What a trigger hands a pipeline, read as `carries` in code (R4): `EventDef.carries`, `ACTION_CARRIES`, `CadenceDef.carries` (`cadenceCarries`); kinds `session` · `message` · `speaker` · `actor` · `cast-member` · `subject` · `user` · `slot` · `clock` · `scene` · `form` (`EntityKind`, open; `entityWord`). Listed on the generated page **Events and what they carry** (`/docs/sdk/events`, A1). ⚠ The entity kind **subject** (what `sprites-attached` and `media-offered` carry) is not the retired **subject of a binding** (§23). |
| **registration fit** 🚧 | A pipeline **fits** a trigger when every entity its steps read (`entitiesRead`, `inletEntitiesOf`) is carried (R4); `fitOf(pipeline, trigger)` answers in words (_Story reply reads the speaker; scene-opened carries none._). Re-judged on install, update and publish (A11). ⚠ Not **ruleset fit** (§25, 2026-10-19, a genre's rating of a ruleset): say "registration fit" where both could be meant. |
| **suits** 🚧 | The events a pipeline is made for — a picker's hint, never a lock (`.inlet(k, node, { suits })`, `SpecDocument.suits`, `suitsOf`; UI _Made for this_). Replaces the inlet lock (§23). |
| **emits** 🚧 | A pipeline's top-level list of the events it may record (R6, `SpecDocument.emits`, `.emits(...)`), so a preset can register on them; a cycle among them is refused at registration (A12, `emitCycles`). ⚠ A NODE still never declares emits (F8). |
| **action handle** 🚧 | An action as an object a registration names: `spec.actions.<key>` (`ActionHandle`, `actionHandlesOf`; `CompiledSpec<A>`), never `'<spec>#<key>'` typed by hand. |
| **the genre's defaults** 🚧 | A genre's default registrations and setting values (`GenreDecl.defaults` `{ registrations, settings }`, stated with `withGenreDefaults`, read with `genreDefaultsOf`) — and its default preset, the one marked `default: true` (R22). Core's: `coreGenres()`, `storyRegistrations()` … ⚠ Not a session layout's **base** (§23) and not a pipeline's **declared defaults** (`.defaults()`, §6). |
| **presets as changes** 🚧 | A preset is ONE set of changes on its genre's defaults (R2, R3): `register` · `drop` · `change [{ of, … }]` (registration objects in; keys stored, `PresetDecl.registrations`), `settings` (`SettingValue`s), `requires` with version ranges (A16, `satisfiesRange`). Never on another preset: `PRESET_PARENT_KEYS` refused, `presetLevelFindings` judges a stored one (C37). Merged by `effectiveRegistrations(genreDefaults, presetChanges, sessionRows)`. Admin UI: _What this preset runs_ — **The genre's** · **Changed here** · **Added here**, **Drop** / **Restore**, **Add a pipeline**, **Only when…**, **Clone**. |
| **the door** (registration door) 🚧 | The one validator every origin calls (§11-2): the SDK's `registrationFindings` (fit, cadence options, routine fields, values never naming a connection, exposed plumbing, duplicates warn, cycles refuse) wrapped by the app's `registrationDoor` with host facts (`doorSentence`, `presetChangesRefusal`, `envoyFindingsOf`, `presetRequirementFindings`). |
| **broken registration** 🚧 | One that stopped fitting after a change (A11; `refitRegistrations`, `refitAfterChange`, `brokenReason`, `BREAKING_LAWS` fit · values · envoys): set aside, and the layer below answers, with a notice. ⚠ Not a **stale** layout or config value. |
| **duties** 🚧 | A pipeline's per-duty switches, read at the routine's mode: `core:task/reply-duties@1` (_What the reply reads_: Read the lorebook, Read the scene), `reckoning-duties@1`, `sweep-duties@1` — each card titled by its routine's name (_Note what changed_, _Look back over the story_, the Lair keeper's _Keep the books_; `ReckoningRoutineTerms.dutiesTitle`, S7, 2026-10-23; was _What the reckoning keeps_ / _What the sweep files_, §23) → `modes` · `any` (`sessionDutiesOf`, `LOREBOOK_DUTIES`, forced Off without a lorebook). 🚧 A duty may read **ceded** (G1, S2): while the reply carries changes at Full, the reckoning's _Keep the sheets_ and _Track conditions_ read Off (`CEDES_TO_REPLY_CHANGES`, `main.ceded` = `off: replies carry changes`) — ⚠ not a switch the owner turned off. |
| **the reckoning** · **the sweep** · **Picture each new scene** · **Remember things** 🚧 | Core's routines: `core:spec/story-reckoning` (UI _Note what changed_, after each round — or after each turn, the owner's **When it runs** choice, R52), `core:spec/story-sweep` (UI _Look back over the story_, every 5 turns), `core:spec/story-illustrate-new-scene` (on scene opened, Off; ⚠ not `story-illustrate-scene`, the **Scene** action), `core:spec/assistant-memory` (Chat, every 5 turns, Off). ⚠ _sweep_ keeps its open R1 collision with §10/§20 (★, 2026-10-19); members read only the UI names. |
