## 7. Retrieval

| Term                      | Means                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **mechanism**             | _How_ something was found: **keyword** · **semantic** · **entity** · **structural**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **band**                  | _What kind_ of content, and its budget share: `worldLore`, `characterLore`, `history`, `messages`, `relationships`. The type is `RetrievalBand` — qualified, because `Band` is taken; see §10. _(was: `SourceKind`)_                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **source**                | The **vector index's** vocabulary: `message`, `worldLore`, `historyEntry`, `narrativeNode`, … Reconciled to bands at the seam, never merged.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **signal**                | One scored component within a mechanism.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **candidate**             | Something that might reach the prompt, carrying signals.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **decision**              | Selection's verdict on a candidate: included or not, with a reason.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **retrieval marker**      | The mark a list row carries for the newest run's **decision** about it: ● fired, ○ considered, nothing when no mechanism reported on it. A reading of a decision, never a fourth outcome.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **block**                 | **One message** in the assembled prompt — §15. What assembly places _inside_ one is an **allocation**, never a block.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **admission**             | Whether a candidate is _considered at all_.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **eligibility**           | Whether a candidate _may_ be selected — a hard gate, distinct from score.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **evidence**              | Non-keyword grounds for admission.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **share**                 | A band's slice of the budget. **Declared on the source** since 2026-09-16 (R-7 P5): each retrieval definition's own `params.share`, a relative number the ranker normalises (`shareNormalisation`). Never the `share` control type any more — that divided one value over members, and there is no one value.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **minimum**               | A guaranteed least count for a band — `minEntries`, the label _Always keep at least_. The conversation's alone (R6); declared on `session-history`. _(was: **floor**, ruled 2026-09-16 — that word is the action model's, §9; the identifiers `minEntries` and `reserved_minimum` already said it.)_                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **threshold**             | A score cutoff below which a candidate is not considered — `thresholdMin` / `adaptiveThreshold`'s `max(threshold, topScore × fraction)` clause (`semantic.ts`). _(was: **floor**, ruled 2026-09-16 — a third sense distinct from both the action model's word and the retrieval **minimum**; never *floor* or *minimum*.)_                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **cap**                   | A ceiling on a band — `maxEntries`, declared on the source; absent means none (`relationship-search`, whose own ceiling is the band's).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **band intent**           | **Built 2026-09-16 (R-7 P5).** What one source says about its own place in the window — `{ band, intent: { share, maxEntries, minEntries, priority } }` — published as ONE element at the head of its candidates list and read off by the ranker (`BandIntent` in the SDK). ⚠ An element, not a wrapper: the list stays a flat array so every consumer and both `candidates/*` script kinds keep their contract, and an empty source still has a share. ⚠ Not "metadata" in code — the ruling's word for it in prose (16 §5a); the type is the intent.                                        |
| **band priority**         | A band intent's `priority`: `low · normal · high · always`. `normal` is no ordering at all; `high`/`low` sort the band's entries ahead of or behind the others when the ranker sweeps leftover room; `always` takes every entry the window can hold ahead of the scored fill (`reserved_priority`) — **up to the band's `maxEntries`** (U3b review S1): a priority is a promise about the band, a pin about one entry, and only the pin steps over the cap. ⚠ Not the per-entry **priority** an author sets on a lorebook entry (a score bonus), which keeps the bare word in that vocabulary. |
| **band-namespaced field**            | A band intent's field on a definition that produces MORE THAN ONE band through one port and so declares several intents in one `params` slot: `<band><Field>` — `worldLoreShare`, `historyMaxEntries`, `characterLorePriority` (`bandIntentFieldsOf` in the contracts). `lorebook-triggers@1`, and `entity-search@1`'s `recalledLinesShare` (lore on `main`, recalled lines on `messages`, 2026-09-27); a lane declares the bare `share` / `maxEntries` / `priority` because it speaks for one band. Same labels, same defaults, one table (`LORE_BANDS`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **recalled line** · **docs excerpt** | **Built 2026-09-27/28.** Two **declared bands** (§15), each its own band rather than one of the five. A **recalled line** (`recalledLines`, `core:var/recalled-lines@1`: `{ speaker, turn, text }`, oldest first) is an older transcript line `entity-search@1` found again, published on its `messages` out-port only (`Descriptor.bandPorts`) and named through the host read `recalled_lines`; nothing places it unless a template does (shipped layout **Lines**). A **docs excerpt** (`docsExcerpts`, `core:var/docs-excerpts@1`, keyed "Page › Section") is a documentation section `core:query/docs-search@1` found for the guide genre (`searchDocs`, `runtime/docsRetrieval.ts`). ⚠ A recalled line is not _recall_ the measurement (precision/recall) — the qualifier keeps them apart (R3); a docs excerpt is not **world lore**. |
| **gazetteer**             | The known-name vocabulary: titles, aliases, cast names, nicknames.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **mention**               | A span of conversation text that may name something.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **link**                  | A resolved mention → entry or character.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **runaway pattern**       | **Built 2026-09-30 (plan lorebooks-consolidation S3).** A regex key whose time to match can grow without bound — a repeat nested in a repeat the next round could also match (`(a+)+`), a repeated choice whose options can match the same text (`(a|ab)*`), or one over `PATTERN_MAX_LENGTH` (1,024) characters. `runawayPatternOf` (`shared/entries/runawayPattern.ts`) is the one judgement: `entries:create` / `entries:update` / an entry amendment refuse one (`assertNoRunawayPatterns`, only what the write introduces, judged across the row and every amendment of it), an import reads its entry as a literal, and the scan never runs one. Every other regex key runs under a time bound (`ranking/boundedPattern.ts`: 25 ms a key); one **pattern budget** of 200 ms a scan (`patternBudget()`, shared by every window and recursion pass of one `keywordQuery`) and 250 ms an event-loop task across scans (`PATTERN_TASK_BUDGET_MS`). A key's **pattern debt** — its runs past `PATTERN_SLOW_MS` (5 ms), a trip counted at the whole bound, cleared by any fast run — skips it until restart at `PATTERN_DEBT_MS` (50 ms): a single trip is retried at once, and a key slow on every run is caught though it never trips. Past the three shape rules, two more refusals: `tooIntricate` (judging it would pass `JUDGE_WORK_LIMIT`) and `unreadable` (it compiles, but the parser cannot read it). What a scan did not run is `diagnostics.patternsNotRun` `{ id, source, key, why }` on the receipt. ⚠ A heuristic, not a proof: it refuses some safe patterns and misses polynomial ones, which is why the bound is not optional. |

**The flow, every noun distinct:** a **mechanism** produces **candidates** carrying
**signals**; ranking **scores** them; selection turns them into **decisions** within a
**band's** budget; assembly turns those into **allocations** and renders them into
**blocks**; the **receipt** records it.

**Resolved collisions**

- ⚠ **`source`** → the _index_ vocabulary. The ranker's budget grouping is a **band**. This is
  the collision that silently dropped six of eight sources at ranking.
- ⚠ **`band`** → the _retrieval_ concept in prose, but the **type is
  `RetrievalBand`**, because `Band` is already a public SDK export naming a
  _connection capability grade_ (§10). Two live meanings of one bare word is the
  failure R1 exists to stop, so the newer use qualifies. The canon's own name for
  the SDK's is **capability grade**, so the qualifier belongs on that side and can
  be dropped here once that pass runs — §25.
- ⚠ **`weight`** → always qualified: **signal weight** · **mechanism weight** · **entry
  weight** (the per-row multiplier). A band's slice is a **share**, never a weight.
- · **`score`** → the number. The function is `score()`; there is no other kind of score.
- · **`budget`** → the token budget. A band gets a **share** of it.

**Retired:** _arm_ (→ **mechanism**) · _retrieval mode_ · _retrieval strategy_ (both removed —
every mechanism runs and contributes additively).

---

## 8. Content

| Term                | Means                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **lorebook**        | A collection of entries.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **cover image** (of a lorebook) 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-21.** The book's one picture: `lorebooks.cover_media_id` (`coverMediaId`, FK `files.id`, `SET NULL`, migration 0111), a file stored as **lorebook-owned media** (§18) by `storeLorebookCover` and set or cleared through `lorebooks:update`'s `coverFile` (a picture · `null`). Drawn **square** (owner: _"Lorebook images should be square instead of round"_) in the list row and before the name in the header; `lorebookCoverSrc`. Seen by whoever may read a book that wears it (`canViewMedia`). R3: never bare _cover_ in code beyond the column — `coverMedia`, `coverFile`. ⚠ Not a cast member's **face**, not the session card's cover (the lead's portrait — a layout word, not a stored thing). |
| **entry**           | One row of authored world content.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **field role**      | What an entry field _does_ for the engine: title, order, priority, anchor, parent, key, embed text. ⏳ The declaration key is still `roles` — it is hashed into `core:entry/*@1`, so it moves with `@2` and not with a rename. _(was: `role`)_                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **trigger**         | An authored term that fires an entry. The column stays `keys`. **The only sense** (ruled 2026-09-28, R1): what starts a run is an **event** or a fired **action** (§9), never a trigger.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **secondary key**   | A condition key, combined by selective logic.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **selective logic** | `AND ANY` · `AND ALL` · `NOT ANY` · `NOT ALL`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **binding**         | The link from a cast member to a character or persona card. **Content only.** ⏳ Ruled 2026-09-10: a `lorebook_bindings` row is a **cast member** (name, aliases, state, summary, graph node); _binding_ narrows to the card link; the `{{char:N}}` placeholder is a **tag**. UI label **Cast**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **cast member**     | Someone who exists in a lorebook's world, carded or not. The row behind the Cast section. _(was: binding)_ Its stored name (`lorebook_bindings.name`) is its shown name at the book's present on Main, for sort and search only; the vocabulary claims names by the member's base (undated Main) shown name (★cp-names-1, owner 2026-11-08, "Both, via base name"). One writer of it (★s4-fixes-2, P2): 🚧 `writeBackShownName` (`characters/versions.ts`), after a name-touching cast-version write, edit or delete on Main, after the card sync (`utils/characterBindingSync.ts`, which names a row itself only when it has no base version for the write-back to read) and after session Back/Forward takes or restores story-written versions (lane s4-tidy).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **cast tag**        | The `{{char:N}}` a lore text names a **cast member** by — the member row's `binding` column (the canon's "tag" of the **binding** row above, qualified per R3: a bare _tag_ is a **Tag** label, §22). **One spelling, and only it is a tag** (`{{char:N}}` — to the prompt, the editor and every server scan alike; 0.5's `{char:N}` is read only by the 0.5 import, an R5 boundary: `importedCastTagNumber` · `importedCastTagsIn` · `rewriteImportedCastTagsDeep`; 0200 rewrote what was stored, merge logs included), **one member per tag per book** (`lorebook_bindings_binding_unique`, 0201), and **a number is never reissued** (`lorebooks.next_binding_number`; the entry save mints a member only for a number the book has not issued, up to `MAX_TYPED_MEMBER_NUMBER`; `MAX_MEMBER_NUMBER` is the last the counter can issue). Only the `char` prefix is a cast tag — `{{roll:20}}` is a macro. A cast tag **follows its member** (A16, 2026-09-30): a merge rewrites the absorbed member's tags to the survivor's in every lore text column, keeping **undo notes** (`binding_merge_logs.tag_rewrites`), which an undo replays **by position** (the value's **tag positions**), so merges undo in any order; a delete writes the member's name in their place, in the merge logs' saved copies and undo notes too. A **blank member** (`isBlankMember`) is a background member nobody filled in — no card, name, summary, aliases or sprite set, state and visibility at their defaults, no scene, date or parent — what the pre-A16 save minted over a merged member's tag; an undo deletes one nothing points at (`memberIsLinked`: a relationship, scene, lore, child member, dated change, presence, stat row, attribute sheet, pending stat proposal, suggestion or merge log) and moves any other off the returning member's tag. Not every background member is blank. `server/utils/castTags.ts`; client `castTag.ts` draws them. UI: "reference" / "mention" (docs). |
| **card-less** (of a cast member) · `makeMemberCardless` 🚧 | **Built 2026-11-08 (★3, lane s4-cl; plan §34.2).** A member with no linked card (`lorebook_bindings.character_id` null). The one way to get there: 🚧 `makeMemberCardless(tx, memberId, { cause, card? })` (`cast/cardless.ts`); 🚧 `CardlessCause` `unlink` · `card-delete` · `provided-uninstall` · `starter`; 🚧 `CardlessOutcome` (adds 🚧 `facesRepointed`, the versions whose face or likeness moved). It runs each module's writer: words detached (`resolveFollows`; an unlink keeps its from-the-book's-present rule), and the card's sprite sets (🚧 `copySpriteSetsToMember`), gallery (`addToMemberGallery`) and card-layer stats, fill-only (🚧 `copyCardStatsToMember`, `characters/dowry.ts`), copied onto the member. Files go through `fileForOwner`. The face and likeness pictures on every version of the member (retired ones too) are re-owned last: 🚧 `repointCastVersionFiles(tx, memberId, files)` (`characters/versions.ts`) points them in place, with no retire and no new version, at the book owner's own file rows (★s4-cl-1; lane s4-cp, 2026-11-08). A starter copy runs it for every member (🚧 `makeCopyCardless`, `lorebooks/starterKits.ts`, cause `starter`) and moves the copy's `character:<card>` annotation keys to `cast_member:<id>`. It is idempotent. Deleting a card makes every member linked to it card-less, in any book. ⚠ Not **background member** (next row; ★4): a card-less member can be seated and speak, and a carded member can be background. **At boot** (lane s4-rul-f, 2026-11-10): members left linked to a card deleted earlier become card-less the same way (⏳🚧 task `deleted-card-members`). |
| **background member** | **Ruled 2026-11-08 (★4, owner); built by lanes s4-seat and s4-seat-live.** A cast member this session does not seat: no seat **in play** of either table (`session_characters`, `session_personas`) holds it (§9 **a seat in play**); a benched seat's member is background (§9 **benched seat**). A name, a summary and some lore, like the innkeeper everyone mentions but nobody plays. It depends on the session, not on the card: a member with no card who is seated speaks for themselves, and a member with a card who is not seated is background. It decides whose private lore a turn sees: a seated member's lore is its own speaker's, never the narrator's; the narrator gets a background member's. Code: the private-lore gate (`isCharacterLoreEntryVisible`, `prompt/characterLore.ts`) reads 🚧 `seatedMemberIds` on its session (the live `cast_member_id`s of both tables, plus the members whose linked or dated card a live seat holds, so an older member-less seat does not leak its lore to the narrator; built in `asSession`, `runtime/host.ts`), and 🚧 `currentCastMemberId` (the speaker of a card-less seat's turn; set only when `currentCharacterId` is null). Without `seatedMemberIds` the gate keeps its old rule, "no linked card". A departed seat's member is background again (★s4-seat-4, rec keep). 🚧 A deceased member whose seat is still in play reads as seated (owner ★1, 2026-11-10, benched-seats plan; lane bench-L2): the cast state `deceased` alone no longer sends a member's lore to the narrator, and the `nodeState` hydration in `host.ts` is gone (§23). ⚠ Not **card-less** (a member with no linked card). |
| **carrier card** 🚧 | **Built 2026-11-08 (★S4-1, lane s4-st).** A provided book's plugin-stamped card (a genuine `extensions.serenepub.provided` mark with its own uuid), kept as the release carrier so a plugin upgrade's Update offer reaches the book's members. Hidden from every library, picker and search by 🚧 `genuineProvidedMarkSql()` (`plugins/providedMarks.ts`, the SQL twin of `markedCharacter`; the characters list, `jump`, folder counts, the applet library's `library-characters` and the conversations store apply it); a read of one card by id does not. Owns nothing a person edits (★5: existing 0.6 starter-copied cards stay as they are; ★st-2 open on the applet library). Qualified because bare "carrier" names the carrier version of `reparentFromBookPresent`. ⚠ Not a cast member, not a re-imported card whose mark names another uuid, and not a starter lorebook's card (a starter copy makes none). |
| **`canReadCastMember`** · **`canEditCastMember`** 🚧 | **Built 2026-11-08 (lane s4-cp; plan §34.2).** Who may read and who may edit a cast member's own art, one module (`cast/memberAccess.ts`) so the sprite and gallery sockets and the copy rule answer alike. **Read:** whoever may read the member's book (owner, a share recipient, a live provided book, a session's own notes; an administrator unless `{ isAdmin: false }`), or anyone in a session that seats the member. **Edit:** `findOwnedBook` — the book's owner, or a session's own notes for its members; a share recipient, a session guest and an administrator read and never write. A refusal never confirms the member exists. **Copy to my characters** from a member uses the read rule **without** the admin exception (🚧 `mayCopyMember`, `characters/cardFromMember.ts`). ⚠ Not `canViewCharacter` (a card's rule). |
| **reading into**    | The relation between a **session** and the lorebook it has: the session _reads into_ the book. The **book header** (below) says it as its subtitle, the **reading line** (2026-10-10, design A.2): _Read by ‹session›_, where it reads when that is not main at now, and how many entries reached its last turn — or _Not read by a session_, muted. It replaces the rail's `ReadingInto` block (§23). ⚠ A session reads **on its own line, at its story clock** — or at the head of the line when it follows the line's present (owner ruling 3, 2026-09-28; **lorebook reading**, below) — and retrieval resolves amendments there too, so the reading line is also where a reader who has moved the moment or the line is told they are not looking at what the session reads, and the one click back is **Read what it reads** (the session's line, at its clock). A session keeps the book it started with (the **book lock**, §24 Session data vocabulary; ★B-5, 2026-11-08), so no verb reads a book into a session or stops reading one: **Read into this session** / **Stop reading** and the _attach_ identifiers are retired (§23, 2026-11-08); the UI words _Attach_ / _Detach_ were retired before them (§23).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **moment bar** | The lorebook workspace's ONE time surface, along the bottom of every lens (ruled 2026-09-30, "one timeline everywhere"; rebuilt 2026-10-10, design A.1). Left: the **line chip** (`BranchChip`: switch line, Fork, Compare, Rename, Delete; it opens upward from the foot) and the moment in words (`momentWords`: _Reading now_ · _Reading as of ‹date›_). Away from now, beside them, what a save does there (`MOMENT_SAVE_SENTENCE`) and the pool at that moment (`asOfCountSentence`: _12 entries as of this moment, 3 not in the story yet_). Then the scrubber — a tick per dated entry, a chip at the moment — **Go to date…** and **Open timeline** (the Time lens, offered unless it is open). Right: **Make this the present** (away from now, it stores the moment as the line's story clock) and **Return to now**, the only one in the pane. Away from now the whole bar takes the `warning` tint, so the reader can tell from anywhere in the pane that the book is not being read as it stands. Compact, it is one line — line chip · moment words · Return to now — that opens the rest in place (`compact`, `aria-expanded`). A **reader first**: setting the moment never edits a row, but saving WHILE at one offers to file an **amendment** (below). The **Time** lens is the axis drawn large, with lanes. The track steps between the dates the book holds; **Go to date…** (built 2026-09-28, #164) stands the reader at ANY date — checked against the book's calendar, refused never clamped — so an amendment can land where nothing is dated yet. ⚠ Who is in the world at the moment is not the bar's: that is the **roster popover**, a cast fact. Replaces the **World bar** and the **moment banner** (§23). |
| **roster popover** (`RosterPopover`) | **Built 2026-10-10 (design A.1).** Who the world holds at the moment being read, on the line being read: a count that opens one row per **appearance** under _In the world now_ (or _In the world ‹date›_), each opening its member, two of one person said first. A cast fact, so it stands beside the Cast scope's name on the **lens line**, never on the **moment bar**. Replaces the World bar's roster (§23). |
| **book header** · **lens line** | **Built 2026-10-10 (design A.2–A.3).** The two rows over a book's lenses. The **book header** is ONE `PanelNavHeader` at both widths: the book's name as title, the **reading line** as subtitle (**reading into**, above), back always (the book list is off screen at desk too), and ⋯ **Settings** · **Duplicate** · **Export… (paused)** · **Delete this lorebook**. No `DetailHero`: a book's icon tile said nothing. The **lens line** says WHAT on the left — the scope's label and its figure (_Cast · 14_), and under Cast the **roster popover** — and HOW on the right, the **lens track**; it is hidden under **Book settings**, which sets the lenses aside. |
| **lens track** (`LensTrack`) · **lens popout** · **scope popout** (`ScopePopout`) | **Built 2026-10-10 (design A.3–A.4, owner A-Q1, A-Q3).** The **lens track** draws the lens control: a segmented track at the right end of the **lens line**, one 32px icon button per lens in the registry, the chosen one tonal primary with `aria-pressed`, each named in its title with its shortcut (`data-lore-lens-track`). Its UI label is **Show as** (2026-10-11, less-confusing G2): `aria-label="Show as"`, the compact trigger _Show as: ‹lens›_, the docs' **Show as › Time**; _lens_ stays the code word and is never shown. The places lens is labelled **Map**, because **Places** is a view (a scope) in the rail. At compact the book's find row is the filter box, then the **scope popout** — a 40px button wearing the chosen scope's icon, opening `role="radio"` rows (the seven scopes, then the saved scopes, each with its figure, and the Loose ends line after them), the chosen scope said once more as one dismissible chip under the row (`scopeChipLabel`) — then the **lens popout**, the track's compact form (`LensTrack compact`): one button wearing the chosen lens's icon, opening radio rows. ⚠ A lens is never a scope: the track draws, the rail and the scope popout choose. Replaces the **lens row** and the compact scope chips (§23). |
| **`lensesShown`** · **`lensShown`** · `LensTrack`'s **`advancedControls`** prop 🚧 | **Built 2026-11-10 (owner GO; PLAN-advanced-controls-2026-11-10, lane adv-D).** `lensesShown(advanced)` lists all lenses, less **Graph** and **Lives** unless advanced; `lensShown(lens, advanced)` falls back to List; `lensForKey(event, advanced)` gained the parameter; `LensTrack` has a required boolean prop `advanced` (`client/lorebooks/lenses/registry.ts`). With **advanced controls** (§26) off, Graph and Lives leave the track and their Alt+Shift 4 and 6 shortcuts with them; an address naming either draws List, with no redirect. ⚠ The prop is `advancedControls` (renamed from a bare `advanced` 2026-11-10, ★adv-E-2) so it never reads as `advanced: true` on a FieldDecl (ruled 2026-10-19, §5-2), which means _fold this field_; the helpers' parameter is local and keeps the short name. |
| **Views** · **Saved** (the rail's groups) · **Pinned** (a saved scope) · **Book settings** (a route) | **Built 2026-10-10 (design A.2–A.3, owner A-Q2).** A book's **section list** (`LoreRail`) is scopes and only scopes. Head: the filter box. **Views**: the seven scopes with their figures, dimmed while a lens that ignores scope (Lives, Places) is open — choosing one still opens it, in the default lens. **Saved**: the saved scopes (`SAVED_SCOPES`, `savedScopeCounts`), today **Pinned** alone — a row like a scope's, current (`aria-current`) INSTEAD of one, opening Everything narrowed to the pinned entries (`savedScopeRoute`); future saved scopes land here. Foot: one quiet line, _3 loose ends ›_ (`looseEndsLabel`), opening the **Loose ends** queue, which is a chore list and never a row. **Book settings** is a route, `LoreRoute.settings` (`#lore=12/settings`, written `?settings=1`; actions `openSettings` · `closeSettings`), drawn in the lens slot over the route beneath it with the **lens line** hidden; Back and Escape pop it first. |
| **cast member page** (its tabs) | **Built 2026-10-10 (design A.6).** A cast member's page is a `PanelTabStrip`: **Member** (the form, presences, amendments), **Lore** (the member's anchored lore, Add lore, the character-lore editor), **Relationships** (every tie, uncapped), **Timeline** (the scenes they are in: `memberScenes` → `MemberTimeline`). The tab is kept while moving between members and on returning to Cast (`lastMemberTab`). Icons §22. The design's _Ties_ was not adopted: **relationship** is the row's word (§17). An entry's marks **Pinned** (_Always in the prompt_) and **Off** (_Out of every prompt_) are toggles in the entry editor's ⋯, here and in the entry workspace; Advanced is matching only (priority, regex, case, recursion, conditions). |
| **cast amendment**  | A dated overlay on a **cast member** — their name, aliases, state, summary, and **which card represents them**. ⚠ **Not a character amendment** (ruled 2026-09-23, superseding ruling 5's wording): a character CARD is a reusable asset several books may share, so amending it would change that person in every one of them. The person in _this_ story is the `lorebook_bindings` row. `characterId` is an ordinary amendable column, which is what makes "a different card for a different lifecycle" need no mechanism of its own. Table `cast_amendments` (0161 drops `character_amendments`, 0162 creates it). Its fields are **`CAST_AMENDABLE`** (`sockets/amendments.ts`: name, aliases, summary, state, visibility, sprite set, card), refused in words for a state or visibility a member cannot have; `0211_cast_amendment_fields_repair` cut older rows to them (A25, 2026-09-30). |
| **retold** (field) · `RetoldField` · `lorebook_bindings.retold` 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-13 (PLAN-cast-retold-fields, owner rulings 1–2).** A card field a **cast member** tells in their own words: `description` · `personality` · `scenario` · `firstMessage` · `alternateGreetings` · `exampleDialogues` · `face`. The member keeps its own column per field and `retold: Record<RetoldField, boolean>`; `true` reads the member's column, `false`/absent reads the card's through. Switching a field off **keeps** its text (hides, never discards). UI: a **Use from card** switch on each field of the member's form (on = the card's text reads through; off = the member's own, kept set aside when switched back on), the **From the card** note at the top of Profile and Voice, **Take from card** while the switch is off; a card-less member has the fields as its own, no switch (2026-11-10, lane s4-rul-e). The card is a **starter**; editing it reaches every member that still reads that field from it. ⚠ Not an **override** (§6 — a config-scope value), not an **amendment** (a dated overlay; the retold columns and flags are themselves amendable), not _diverged_ or _mirrored_ (there is no copy kept in sync). **★cp-10 (lane s4-follow-a, 2026-11-09):** the fields also include `postHistoryInstructions` · `creatorNotes` · `likeness`, which live on **cast versions only** (no `lorebook_bindings` column; `VERSION_ONLY_MEMBER_KEYS` in `sockets/lorebooks.ts` strips them before a row write), each with **Use from card** on the member form (a card-less member owns all three); 🚧 `LikenessTab` `owner` prop (a member owner reads the member's gallery and sprites). |
| **face** (of a cast member) 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-13 (PLAN-cast-retold-fields, owner ruling 3).** The picture a cast member is drawn with when `retold.face`: `lorebook_bindings.face_media_id` (FK `files.id`, `SET NULL`), picked from the card's gallery or uploaded as **lorebook-owned media** (§18). UI **Change face** · **This book's pictures** · **Upload a picture** · **Use the card's picture**. ⚠ Not a **Portrait** (§18, the picture pipeline), not the card's **avatar** (`characters.avatar_media_id`, the card's own picture, which a member without a retold face reads through). |
| **dated card**      | A card a **cast amendment** draws a member with from a date (its `characterId`). **It is the member's**, on any line and at any date — identity, not a reading: a session seating it seats that member, and seating it never mints a second one. A card draws ONE member, linked or dated: `amendments:create`/`:update` and `lorebooks:updateBinding` refuse a card another member has, naming them. One map, `server/utils/castMemberCards.ts`: **`castMemberCards`** (`CastMemberCards`: `memberOf` card → member, `cardsOf` member → cards, linked first) · **`memberOfCard`** · **`cardTakenBy`**; `LorebookLinks.datedCards`. Every seat → member reader goes through it (`cardMemberAt`, `findOrInsertBinding`, `sessionLinks`, `normalizeOwner`, the graph context, scene mentions, the prompt's absorbed names, side characters, the scene cast list, and the private-lore gate, which reads a member's cards as **`memberCards`** on the binding — the host's lore read puts them there — and names the seated one for co-occurrence). The card check runs under the book's lock (`assertCardFree` in `sockets/amendments.ts`). ⚠ A **deleted** card is never given a member: `findOrInsertBinding` answers null for it when no member has it. ⚠ Not "card swap": **swap** is a pipeline word (§9). Built 2026-09-30 (plan A25). |
| **amendment**       | A **dated overlay** on a subject: "from this date, these fields read differently". Never a version, never an edit — the **base** is untouched and both are true, at different dates. Two tables, `entry_amendments` and `cast_amendments` (a deleted subject must not leave overlays behind, and a polymorphic subject column cannot cascade); one resolver, `asOf`. An amendment IS a date: `year` is `NOT NULL` — except a **held amendment** (below), the one undated kind (`year` nullable; CHECK `entry_amendments_undated_check`). It never carries the entry's own date (`ENTRY_DATE_PARTS` are `NEVER_AMENDED`, A18(b), 2026-09-30): re-dating is editing the entry. ⚠ Not a **child entry** — `schema.ts` called a nested entry's parent "an amendment's base entry" until 2026-09-23, when that use was renamed under R1. ⚠ Not the SDK constitution's numbered _amendments_ (F37–F41), which are laws in a plan. Built 2026-09-23 for entries and for the **cast**. The user-facing word is **dated change** (the Duplicate, overwrite-import and cast-delete copy); an amendment is filed on the **line** being read, and the verb that removes one is **Delete**, with a confirm (2026-09-28).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **held amendment** 🚧 (provisional name, unruled ★B1-1) | **Built 2026-11-11 (lane sense-b1; owner rulings S3 "Only Apply settles", Stage B 1–2 (b) fold).** A session's change to an **entry** of the lorebook it reads, kept in the session's **own book** (**Session notes**) as an `entry_amendments` row until the lorebook's owner applies it. **Purpose / why:** a pipeline's change must not rewrite a book other sessions read; the session sees its own change, nobody else does, and **Apply to the lorebook** is the only door. **Owns:** the change itself: `base` (what each changed field read when the session wrote it), `source_message_id` (the turn that made it, so a swipe, regenerate, Back and delete take it and Forward puts it back), and the session's story date at day grain when it reads at a moment, else none. **A held amendment is exactly an `entry_amendments` row with `base IS NOT NULL`.** It is made whatever the lorebook write mode (Full included); a change to an entry of the session's own notes is written as before. **Does not own:** the lorebook's text (the entry is untouched until Apply); a history day (`create-lore-entry` onto a day writes through under **Full** except for a session whose scenes end by themselves, where it files onto the own book's day, merged at Apply, 🚧 2026-11-12 lane sense-b4, §25 *The flip*; on the own-book route a day is the own book's, 🚧 2026-11-12 lane sense-b3, §25 *The own-book route*); the entry's date (a change that would move a history entry's date is refused). After Apply it is the lorebook's and the turn no longer owns it. 🚧 2026-11-12 (lane sense-b2): Apply also happens **by itself** (scene close, a scene's summary saved, Close out) under the rule in §25 *Apply in full*; a held amendment the lorebook already reads is **done** and is dropped, never applied. ⚠ Not a **line amendment** (a dated change a person or a rule files on a line of the lorebook); not a **session imprint** (a change to a session row); not a **kept imprint** (an entry's note about a reply since replaced); not a ruleset's **held entry** (`HeldEntry`, §9); not a change _held for review_ (**Review changes** proposals). Never the bare word _held_ as a name (R3). The interface says _This session only_ on the session panel's card (never _held amendment_). Placed in §8 beside **amendment**, whose kind it is. |
| **off window**      | "Off from D1 until D2" — a period an entry is not read in, written as TWO amendments (`enabled: false` at the start, `true` at the end) because an amendment only ever sets a value from a date forward. ⚠ **`until` is exclusive**: the end date is the day it is back. | **one history entry per date** · **the day's entry** · **owning line** (of a history day) · `assertHistoryDateFree` · `historyDayOwnerRefusal` · `historyOwnerStep` · `historyEntryOver` · `CASE_HISTORY_OWNERS` 🚧 | **Built 2026-11-10 (owner ★H1 reuse, ★H2 rule C, ★H3; PLAN-history-one-per-date-2026-11-10, lanes hist-A, hist-G).** **Purpose:** a history date names one moment of a line's story, so a day has one history entry, as each line reads it. **Why:** two entries on one date made compile and stat dating disagree (opposite tie-breaks), and a genre could pile undated history onto _Year 1_. **Owns:** `scenes/historyEntryOfDate.ts` owns every history-date check: `assertHistoryDateFree(tx, { lorebookId, branchId, date, exceptId? })` (rule C first, then one per date on the target line; undated rows ignored; archived rows count; the caller holds `lockBookCalendar` and passes only `tx`) and `historyDayOwnerRefusal` (rule C's sentence, or null). The pure `historyOwnerStep(line, date)` (`shared/lorebooks/lineReading.ts`, test table `CASE_HISTORY_OWNERS`) names a day's **owning line** (rule C): a line owns dates strictly after its fork date, an ancestor owns the rest, and a dateless fork owns no dated history. `historyEntryOver(a, b)` (`state/reading.ts`) is the one tie-break: the later date, and of equal dates the lower id, so on a doubled date **the day's entry** is the oldest. Dates compare as the day (`dayOnly`, `compareDates`): partial dates are distinct (lead default). The day-entry paths reuse the day's entry instead of making a second: compile (`historyEntryOfDate(create: true)`, which creates on the owning line), `entries:iterateNext`, a blank session write (the summarize window's **New**), the Time-lens drop, and a pipeline's history write (`fileOntoHistoryDay`, §4). A person's `entries:create`, or re-date through `entries:update` (checked only when the date changes), is refused: _‹line› already has a history entry for ‹date›. Open it, or choose another date._ · _‹line› shares everything up to ‹fork date› with ‹owning line›. Change that day here as an amendment, or choose a later date._ · 🚧 _‹line› follows ‹owning line› with no fork date, so its dated history is ‹owning line›'s. Change that day here as an amendment._ **Not:** a database unique index (none; the check is on the write path and reads across lines). Bulk and system writers (import, attic ETL, starters, the provided-book upgrade, fold, line delete) land rows unchanged, and a doubled date surfaces as a Loose-ends chore (below). Undo and restore are exempt: they put back exact rows. ⚠ A fork's version of a day it doesn't own is an **amendment**, never an entry of its own. |

Fix lines 🚧 (owner ★): _Give one of them another date, or move what it says into the other and delete it._ · _Give it a date after the fork, or delete it._ **Not:** a refusal: the server refuses new writes; these list what is already there. |

Three sources, one card (`Sockets.StarterKits.Card`, id `book:<id>`, `source` `core` · `plugin` · `admin`; the id `primer:<id>` is kept only for API callers that still name a primer, `{ primerId }`): a ruleset's or plugin's **primer**, imported at boot as an immutable **primer row** (§25; ★M2e-1, owner 2026-11-04: an administrator disables it, never deletes it; Freeform's empty Blank is not a kit), and an **admin kit** (a `lorebooks` row of **book kind** `starter_kit`, made by **Save as starter lorebook** or **Clone**, edited in place by the admin who made it). Sockets `starterKits:list` · `starterKits:saveFromBook` · `starterKits:clone` · `starterKits:delete` (GATED family); `starterKit` (`{ primerId }` · `{ lorebookId }`) on `lorebooks:create` and `sessions:create`; one writer, `writePrimerInto`, and one copier, `bookFromKit`. UI **Starter lorebook** (badge), **Start from a starter lorebook**, **Your starter lorebooks**, **Save as starter lorebook**, **Make a lorebook from this kit**, **Delete starter lorebook**, **Admin › Play › Starter lorebooks**. ⚠ Not the **compendium** (owner ruling 9: _"importing entries from a ruleset is different than from a lorebook seed/template"_) and not the Vis Itineris **starting kit** (a class's gear, §25). ⚠ **Renamed 2026-10-22** from *starter kit* (owner: _"starter kits don't really mean anything outside that context"_ — they are lorebooks at the core); the CODE keeps its names — `starterKits:*` events, `lorebooks.kind 'starter_kit'`, `StarterKitPicker`, `starterKitCards` — translated at the UI seam (R5); Admin address `/admin/starter-lorebooks`. Core ships two primers, in registration order: **The Ninth Mile** (`core:primer/ninth-mile@1`, Freeform, listed first; no cast, because its keeper is the **starter character**) and **Brackenvale** (Vis Itineris) — readiness B4, 2026-10-30. |
| **book kind** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-21 (K1, migration 0114).** Which kind of `lorebooks` row a book is: `lorebooks.kind` `'book'` (a **lorebook**, the default) · `'starter_kit'` (a **starter lorebook**). A session's notes are NOT a kind: they stay `session_id` + `overlay_of`. `lorebooks:list` carries `kind`, so the shelf groups the asker's own kits under **Your starter lorebooks**; another person's kit is never on a shelf. ⚠ Qualified (R3): never a bare _kind_ — the workspace's pool already says _kind_ for an entry's section. |
| **lead** (a world-lore category) 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-21 (K1).** A starter lorebook's rumour or hook, stored as a **world lore** entry with `category: "lead"` and one-way `involves` links to what it is about (written by `writePrimerInto` from a primer's leads). A category value, not an entry type: no `core:entry/lead`. |
| **starter character** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-30 (readiness B4, lane K).** The one character Serene Pub ships as text and offers first on the setup wizard's **Pick a character**: Nell Haverly, keeper of The Ninth Mile (`STARTER_CHARACTER` in `shared/characters/starterCharacter.ts`: name, summary, description, personality, a two-paragraph first message, no avatar). **Created only when picked** (`starterCharacterCreate()` → `characters:create`, owned by whoever pressed **Pick**), never seeded. Its card hides while that person owns an unchanged copy (`isStarterCharacterRow`: their own, unshared, not a persona, name and description exactly as shipped; `ownStarterCharacter`) and comes back once the copy is renamed or edited. The step's offers, in order: `CharacterStepOffer` `starter` · `choose` · `create` · `library` · `import` (`characterStepOffers`, `client/wizard/wizardPicks.ts`). UI **Comes with Serene Pub** (chip), **Pick**, **Adding…** (`role="status"`), _Couldn't add this character. Try again._ (inline, `role="alert"`, no toast). ⚠ Not a **starter lorebook** (The Ninth Mile carries no cast, so book and character together make one Nell), and not the sense in which a cast member's card is _a starter_ (**retold**, above): always qualified (R3). |
| **rules list** · `list:<typeId>` (a scope) · `entries:types` 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-22 (PLAN-lorebook-kinds §C, lane C1).** One entryable list of a book's Rules, drawn in the lorebook workspace as entries of its **derived entry type** (`core:entry/vis-itineris.weapons`, stored without `@1`): Vis Itineris's Weapons, Armour, Gear, Consumables, Spells, Feats, Conditions, Creatures; Freeform's Things, Conditions. **UI: the list's own label** (_Weapons_), under a rail group named by the rules (_Vis Itineris_) after **Views**; never _repertoire_ or _piece_ (§28). Its scope is the qualified `list:<typeId>` (R3; `listScope` · `isListScope` · `listScopeType` in `loreRoute.ts`, the seven core scopes unchanged); `entries:types { lorebookId }` → `{ lorebookId, rulesName, types: { typeId, label, repertoireId, piece, libraryRows }[] }`. **Drawn only where it has something in it** (owner ruling 2026-10-21): the book holds entries of it, or the rules' library has rows for it (`drawsRulesList`). Its door is generated (`rulesListDoor`); its editor is `DerivedEntryEditor` (core fields + the list's piece fields + supply); New reads _New entry in ‹list›_. ⚠ Not a **list slot** (§9), and not a **saved scope**. |
| **‹Rules› library** (the chip) · **library row** (`library#<typeId>/<pieceId>`) · **Edit a copy** · `lorebooks:library` · `entries:copyFromLibrary` 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-22 (PLAN-lorebook-kinds §C ruling 10, lane C2).** The rules' shipped catalogue of pieces (SDK **compendium**, §28) shown **under** a book, never in it. **UI: always qualified by the rules** — the chip _Vis Itineris library_ (`PoolFilters.library`, in the chips row of a list the library has pieces for, and of Everything; **off each time the book opens**, owner default), the row badge _Vis Itineris library_, the pool summary _‹n› from the Vis Itineris library_, the empty list's _Show the Vis Itineris library_; never bare _Library_ (§26's rail view), never _compendium_ or _piece_. A **library row** is a `PoolItem` with `fromLibrary: true` in its own key space (`libraryKey`, `client/lorebooks/libraryRows.ts`): read only (`<fieldset disabled>`, the source line above the fields), no row menu, never filed, counted, queued (Loose ends), jumped to or read into a session — `bookPool` never holds one. A piece the book holds a copy of (its `derivedFrom.piece`, on the line being read) is left out. **Edit a copy** is its one action (owner only): `entries:copyFromLibrary { lorebookId, branchId?, typeId, pieceId }` → `{ entry, copied }` copies it as an entry of its rules list (piece = fields, name = title, description = content; `derived_from { compendium, piece, version }`), answering with the line's existing copy (`copied: false`); the editor then opens the copy. A later library version never changes a copy. `lorebooks:library { lorebookId }` → `{ lorebookId, name, source, rows: { typeId, repertoireId, id, version, piece, source? }[] }` (entryable lists only; empty for Freeform). ⚠ Not a **starter lorebook** (a seed for a new book, ruling 9), and not a kind of book. |

**Resolved collisions**

- ⚠ **`role`** → **field role** for entries. _Role_ alone means **authorization**. Messages
  keep **role** (`system`/`user`/`assistant`) — industry standard and never in the same file.
- ⚠ **`key`** → in prose, an entry's is a **trigger**. Bare _key_ means a database key.
- ⚠ **`binding`** → _content_ only. The node-type→implementation map is the **implementation
  registry**. ⏳ Expensive: schema, sockets, SDK. Its own pass.
- · **`field`** → an entry's declared field. A form control is a **control**.
- · **`position`** → ours. SillyTavern's _insertion position_ is deliberately not adopted.

| **seat** · **character seat** · **player seat** 🚧 | **Ruled 2026-10-14 (owner).** A **seat** is a place at the table for anyone who takes turns — the general word, never a type name alone (R3): always one of its two kinds. 2026-11-08):** 🚧 `seatCast({ castMemberId, seatedBy })` seats a member by itself: it must be attached to the session or in its own book or an ancestor's own book (never an overlay row; refusals 🚧 `SEAT_REFUSALS.overlayRow` · `outsideBooks` · `memberGone`, ★s4-seat-2 copy open), the seater is required, `character_id` is the member's linked card or null ⏳ (until S5), a revive is by (session, member), and the merge rule covers card-less seats. 🚧 `seatPlayer({ castMemberId })` seats a member in a player seat; The strategy is a swappable node — a session's choice is its **swap**. Always qualified: **strategy** alone was retrieval's (§23).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

| **earshot** (of an attribute slot)          | 🚧 **Built 2026-09-28 (lair pass R1).** Which prompts may read a slot's value: `AttributeSlotProps.earshot` = `'all'` (the default — every agent a run builds a prompt for) · `'holder'` (only the **holder's own voice**: the prompt written as the cast member who carries the value; every other prompt — the planner, the scene, the state-keeper, another member's voice — is built as if the value were not there). `'holder'` is refused unless `appliesTo` is exactly `['cast']`; `'all'` said aloud is dropped at registration (one declaration, one hash). SDK `SlotEarshot` · `SLOT_EARSHOTS` · `slotEarshot`; carried on `state.slots` rows as `earshot: 'holder'`; enforced for prompts by `withinEarshot(state, speaker)`, where state becomes a prompt (the shared builder and the adventure surfaces' merge), never at the run's read. First user: `core:slot/whisper@1`. A **holder-only** slot or value is one so declared. **Hearing** (built 2026-09-30, plan A28 🔒): one person's reach over the holder-only values in one session — every member's for the session's owner, else the members they portray — because a person's view of a holder-only value follows its **data audience**, `owner` + `character:<holder>` (`holderAudience`), resolved by the audience resolver (`hearingOf`, `state/earshot.ts`). Prompt and person share ONE filter, `heardOnly(state, hears)`; every `state:*` reply carrying values is the caller's view (`stateAsHeard`; `valueHeard` for ledger lines and pending changes), so the Stats widget, `session_state.v1` and a plugin frame show a guest only their own character's whisper (and offer no Whisper box on anyone else's: `describeState` drops the slot from that member's `configs`). A person **changes** such a value only where they hear it: `state:set` and `state:configure` refuse otherwise, and `state:decide` answers a pending change the caller does not hear as _Proposal not found._ A value **computed** from a holder-only one is heard as it is (`earshotSlots`, the fixed point over derived slots, named derivations' `from` and slot rules): holder-only when it reads the value through its own member (`owner.`, the `slot` filter), **owner-only** when it reads it any other way (`state.`, `who.`) — heard by the session's owner alone, taken off every owner it lands on (world, places, members) and out of every prompt. A stored value on a cast member whose slot no declaration names is read as holder-only. ⚠ Not **audience** itself (who may see or act on a declaration or a stored value): earshot is what a prompt hears; the audience a holder-only value is given is what a person sees. Not _heardBy_ (event-map neighbours) or _confide_. |

| **rule** (attribute)                        | **Ruled 2026-09-17 (R11); SDK shape built, gate 🚧.** `{ when, set \| add \| remove }` in **Liquid** expressions on a slot declaration (one per slot for now, stored as a list). Fires **once per change set** at the gate, single pass, in sheet-then-slot order, seeing pre-change state plus the incoming changes; its output joins the same validation, turn lock and receipt as every other change. The genre's own writer, so it **applies**. ⚠ Not a script (§4): a rule is data, hashed with the declaration, receipted per rule. ⚠ Not a **derivation**: `derive` is one Liquid expression per derived slot, graph-ordered, never stored.
