| **turn lock**                               | **Ruled 2026-09-17 (R9); SDK `turnLock.ts` built (`openAnchorFor`, `isAnchorOpen`), gate 🚧.** A write to a session cast owner anchors to that character's **latest** reply and stays open until that character speaks again, however many other speakers take turns between. The world owner anchors to the session's newest message the same way — or, since lair pass R8 (2026-09-28), to a row the run declares (`set-state`'s `worldRow`: the Lair's beats row), and **every row of the newest turn** is open for the world (`TurnMessage.turn`, the creating run). Personas are characters, so the player's turns lock too. Owned by the SDK so the gate, a plugin and the client cannot answer differently. Lorebook-layer edits on the story clock are never turn-locked.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **who** (state keys)                        | **Ruled 2026-09-17 (R16); 🚧.** A sibling of `state.cast`, never inside it: `speaker` · `last` · `previous` · `user` · `owner` · `next` · `active`, each pointing at the same entry the cast map holds. Resolved once at run start beside the **portrayal** and pinned on the receipt. **Absent** means the key is missing. `narrator` and `addressed` were considered and declined (a loaded bag; a guess). ⚠ `state.cast.byId[characterId]` is the second index over the same entries (R17); the id index is built first and the slug index derived, because a slug moves on rename and an id does not.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **action** 📘                                                          | **Ruled 2026-09-15** (plans/29 R-15); venue · audience · quick · slash name **built 2026-09-16 (U5c)** as `ActionDecl` on `contributes.actions[]` and `CORE_ACTIONS` for core's verbs (SDK `actions.ts`); enabled-when **built 2026-09-17 (U5e)** as `ActionDecl.enabledWhen` / `GenreDecl.enabledWhen` over the SDK's `predicates.ts`. Anything a person or an AI-voiced participant invokes: a composer button, a message-menu item, a slash command, a widget control. Declares a **venue**, an **audience**, `quick`, a **description** (required since 2026-09-28, and optionally an **icon alt** — see **action legend**), an **enabled-when** predicate, optionally a **present-when** predicate (`ActionDecl.presentWhen`, 2026-09-27: absent is hidden, not greyed — see **present-when** (of an action)) and, for composer actions, a **slash name**. Its `key`, joined to the spec slug as `<spec slug>#<key>`, is its **identity** — the one key everything routes and stores by (plans/31 V2, ruled 2026-09-17): a binding's subject, a preset's included set, a session's enablement row, a genre's enabled-when default, the fire, a block's `action`, the _new_ mark. There is no second routing key (_function_ is retired, §23); two specs declaring one key are two actions, and one slash name means one of them. ⚠ Not a _pipeline_ (an action starts one) and not an _event_ (an occurrence — core's, or one a package declared and a write recorded). A **built-in** is a state-altering action core implements and always emits with what changed (delete, ghost, swipe, hide, edit, branch, stop); a **floor** is a built-in no genre may remove (stop, branch, edit). Content-producing actions (extend, regenerate, narrate) are declared by the genre and its pipelines.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Actions** (the widget, `actions`) 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-11 (PLAN-core-widgets W8).** Core's widget that draws the session's listed **action**s (`actions.v1`) as buttons that stay up, in three groups read off fields the listing carries: the **turn controls** (the `extra` **venue**), the genre's own (the `composer` venue) and the **foreign** ones (`origin: 'foreign'`: another namespace's, switched on for the genre; UI _Added actions_). A message's actions and a widget's own controls are not drawn. Reads `actions` · `viewer` · `settings` · `locale`; no scopes; `maxInstances: 1`; settings `groups` (`all` · `turn` · `genre` · `foreign`) · `size` (`compact` · `large`, the tile grid) · `showWaiting` (declared, not drawn: no section it reads carries a session's open **form**s). A press is `invoke(identity)`, so a collecting action opens the page's collect modal as its chip does; a greyed button carries the chips' verdict (`paletteRowState`) as its `title`; a newcomer it draws is told to the page as met (`actions-seen`). Plain half `@serene-pub/core-catalog/actions` (`actionsView` · `ActionsView` · `ActionsGroupView` · `ActionsButtonView` · `ActionsGroupKey` · `actionsGroupOf` · `actionsGroups` · `ACTIONS_GROUP_ORDER` · `ACTIONS_GROUP_TITLES` · `ActionsSettings` · `ACTIONS_DEFAULTS` · `readActionsSettings`). ⚠ Not an **action** (one declared thing a person invokes; this draws many), not the composer's **Actions** disclosure (the row above the field, about the line being written, which folds away) and not the **action legend** (which explains; this presses). The groups setting says `foreign`, not the plan's _scripts_ (R1: a **script** is authored code at a hook, §12, and contributes no action). |
| **built-in**                                | **Ruled 2026-09-15, built 2026-09-16 (plans/30 U5b).** A state-altering write core implements and always emits with what changed and what was lost: **delete** · **hide** (a ghost) · **edit** · **swipe** · **branch**, each a core outlet (`core:outlet/delete-message@1` …) run as its own one-node spec (`core:spec/builtin-delete` …, inlet `core:inlet/built-in-request@1`) through `runBuiltIn` (`runtime/builtins.ts`) with run kind `action` — receipted, gate-eligible, its event on the receipt and in the session's **changes**. **Stop** is a built-in with no outlet: the run-level guarantee (R-17) emits `message-stopped` from the finalisation, and the row says `generation_outcome = stopped`. A genre may switch an **opt-in built-in** (delete · hide · swipe) off through `messageVerbs`, never re-implement one. Content-producing actions (regenerate · extend · a swipe's fresh alternative) are **built-in write + declared content**: the genre's pipeline makes the text and the reply's own `update-message` records `message-updated` with the **verb**. ⚠ Not a _floor_ (the subset no genre may remove) and not a _venue_ (where it appears — U5c).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

A promise about the _genre_, not about who may act: branch is owner-only in every genre, and the item rule applies to a floor as to any verb. **The action model's word alone** since 2026-09-16 — the Its **origin** is `core` · `plugin` · `user` (a CHECK, with the triple it implies: core and plugin rows carry a **seed key** and no author, a person's carries an author and none), its **slug** is its stable key within that owner (`default`, `cinematic`; a person's is kebabed from the name), and its **visibility** is `shared` or `private` — shipped rows are always shared. A plugin's row is **withdrawn** (`withdrawn_at`) when the package is disabled or uninstalled, never deleted, because sessions name it as where they **started from**. The slug `default` is reserved to the genre's owner, by grammar (the genre id's namespace against the package's own); that row is the **genre default layout**. `layout_updated_at` moves only when `layout` does — never `updated_at`, which every boot re-force and every rename bumps. UI and docs call it a **layout** (_Your layouts_, _Save as new layout_), never "preset" on screen: that is the **session preset**'s word. The v2 columns `document`, `widget_settings` and `widget_styles` (columns, not the tables of those names) were dropped by brief 2 (`0191_layout_drop_v2_columns`, 2026-09-29). ⚠ Not a **session preset** (§9, the bundle a session is created from). |
| **new-session layout** | **Named 2026-09-28 (brief 5a; owner L4)** _(was: **layout default**)_. The **session layout preset** a person picked for a genre's new sessions. A session they open with no layout of their own **starts from** it; with none set, or once it is deleted, unshared or withdrawn, the session starts from the **genre default layout**. Read only at that first open, so changing it later moves no session. One row per (person, genre) in `user_layout_defaults` — the table keeps its name, translated at the seam (R5); the FK is `ON DELETE SET NULL`. UI, on a card's menu: _Use for new *Genre* sessions_ / _Stop using for new sessions_; on the genre default layout's card _Use for new *Genre* sessions_ CLEARS the choice (`newSessionChoice` → `null`), and the server answers a pin to the genre default layout's id as a clear too — no row is the one way to say it (2026-09-30). Code: `resolveNewSessionLayout(tx, userId, genreId)` (never `…Source`: _source_ is on R2's list), the wire flag `isNewSessionLayout`, the socket `sessions:layoutPreset:setNewSessionLayout { genreId, layoutPresetId \| null }` (`null` clears it, deleting the row; built 2026-09-29, brief 6a — `layoutPresetId`, not `presetId`, for the reason under **started from**); `db/userLayoutDefaults.ts` keeps its name. ⚠ Never "layout default" or "default layout": _default_ already has two senses here, the **genre default layout** and the defaults a genre supplies to **enabled-when**. |
| **genre default layout** | **Named 2026-09-28 (brief 5a).** A genre's `default`-slug **session layout preset**, shipped by the genre's owner: core's for a `core:` genre, the owning plugin's for a plugin genre (which gets no core row). What a session **starts from** when its person has no **new-session layout**, and what **Reset to genre default layout** copies back in. It is an ordinary row, found by (`genre_id`, slug `default`, origin ≠ `user`, not withdrawn), and no longer `layout_preset_id = null`; the wire flag is `isGenreDefault` (was `isDefault`). **Always qualified (R1, R3):** never the bare "genre default", which already means the defaults a genre supplies per function (`GenreDecl.enabledWhen`, **enabled-when**), and never "the default layout" (a person's is their **new-session layout**). UI: the card group _Genre default layout_; the status _Started from the genre default layout_. **2026-11-05 (lane lay-B):** core's genre layouts are `panels` v2 and carry panel titles — Cast, Scenario, Last character, Story, Characters, World, Lore, Last persona, Party, Table talk — and Guide ships one, `GUIDE_LAYOUT` (layout name _Guide_: Messages, Turn line, Composer). |
| **started from** (a session layout's provenance) | **Named 2026-09-28 (brief 5a; owner L2).** Which **session layout preset** this session's layout was last copied from, and when: `session_panel_layouts.layout_preset_id` (TS and wire `startedFromLayoutPresetId`) and `layout_copied_at` (`layoutCopiedAt`). Null after **Start from scratch**, or once that row is deleted (`SET NULL`). Read ONLY to label, to offer **Start again from**, and to mark a source changed since the copy — **never to draw**: it is provenance, not a base, and nothing is layered over a session's layout. Status line: _Started from the genre default layout_ · _Started from "*Name*" (from *Plugin*)_ (core's other layouts: _(from Serene Pub)_) · _Started from your layout "*Name*"_ · _Started from "*Name*" (shared by *Author*)_ · _Your own layout_ (scratch, or the source is gone). **Updated** is the chip on the source's card when its `layout_updated_at` is later than `layout_copied_at` (the `:get` answer's flag `startedFromUpdated`, built 2026-09-29); nothing moves until the person starts again. It is LIVE (brief 6b, 2026-09-30): whatever moves a layout's `layout_updated_at` — **Save changes to**, a plugin update, core's reconcile — pushes **`sessions:panelLayout:startedFromUpdated`** `{ sessionId, startedFromLayoutPresetId, layoutCopiedAt, startedFromUpdated, presets }` (scoped `#<sessionId>`, gated; also answered when the page asks) to every session that started from it and now reads Updated (`sessions/startedFromPush.ts`: `pushStartedFromUpdated`, `afterLayoutReconcile`). The same answer carries OTHER people's lists after sharing, stopping sharing, renaming or deleting a shared layout (**`pushLayoutListChanged`**, to everyone but the actor with a session of its genre open), and the page asks for it on every (re)connect (**`onConnect`**, `client/sockets/interest.svelte.ts`) — a push sent while a socket was down, a restart's boot reconcile included, is otherwise lost; an answer about an older copy than the page holds is dropped (**`olderThanHeld`**, `client/sessionLayout/layoutAsks.ts`) (2026-09-30). Brief 4 (built 2026-09-29) draws it three ways, all inside the editor: the chip, a line under the status (_*Who* has updated "*Name*" since this session copied it._, with **Start again from "*Name*"**, or **Reset to genre default layout** when the source is the genre default layout), and a dot on the _Layouts_ tab / phone button; never a banner on the stage. Words: `client/sessionLayout/startFrom.ts` (`provenanceLine`, `updatedSentence`, `reCopyAsk`). ⚠ Always the LAYOUT's, never the session's: a session is _created from_ a **session preset**, and "started from" is not said of that. Hence `…LayoutPresetId` and not `startedFromPresetId`, because `sessions.preset_id` (`presetId`) is the session preset. ⚠ Replaces the pinned **base** (`layout_preset_id` read as a live reference; `presetBase`, `presetWidgetSettings`, `baseLayout`, `effective*`), retired by brief 3 (built 2026-09-29, §23). |
| **Start from** · **Start again from "*X*"** · **Start from scratch** · **Reset to genre default layout** · **Done** · **Save as new layout** · **Save changes to "*Name*"** (the layout editor's verbs) | **Named 2026-09-28 (brief 5a; owner L2, L3).** The first four REPLACE this session's layout by copying one in, and all four confirm first (built 2026-09-29, brief 4): one Skeleton `alertdialog` (`LayoutConfirmDialog`, words from `startFrom.ts` `copyConfirm`) that says what it replaces — a copy's _Where it brings its own settings or style for a widget, those replace yours. Everything else you've set is kept._ (LB as built: only what the layout CARRIES wins, and a saved layout carries a widget's values only where they differ from its defaults, so a widget it merely places keeps yours; revised 2026-09-29, the brief 4 review), scratch's _Every widget's settings and style go back to their defaults._ (LC) — and that the editor's **Cancel** does not undo a copy; the phone bar's icon-only Reset asks too. A copy's confirm is the primary; scratch's, which only clears, is in `error` (STYLE-GUIDE §2, §6.6). The editor's tab and the phone's button that hold them are _Layouts_, never _Presets_ (the **session preset**'s word). **Start from**: pick a card (groups _Genre default layout_ · _From *Plugin*_, with core's extra layouts under _From Serene Pub_ · _Your layouts_ · _Shared with you_) and copy it in. **Start again from "*X*"**: re-copy what the layout **started from**. **Start from scratch**: an empty layout, every widget at its defaults — this session's widget settings and style pins are cleared, all of them (owner LC as applied 2026-09-29, brief 6a). **Reset to genre default layout**: re-copy the **genre default layout**. All four are ONE socket event, `sessions:panelLayout:startFrom { sessionId, layoutPresetId \| null }` (`null` = scratch), over ONE helper, `copyLayoutIntoSession`. The other three write. **Done** saves the edits to this session's own row only (`sessions:panelLayout:set`). **Save as new layout** writes a new private **session layout preset** from this session's layout, offered to every session of the genre, and makes it what this session **started from** (`sessions:layoutPreset:save`); it packs the settings and style pins of every widget instance the session draws, which the page reports as `drawnWidgetIds` because the floor draws widgets no arrangement names. **Save changes to "*Name*"** re-captures into your own preset the session started from (`sessions:layoutPreset:update`); other sessions that started from it only see **Updated**. It asks first (`saveChangesConfirm`); when THIS session reads the layout as Updated, the question warns that saving replaces those changes and offers _Start again instead_ (the dialog's `alternative`) beside _Save over them_, and the server refuses such a save unless the page sends **`overwriteUpdated`** (`LAYOUT_PRESET_UPDATED_SINCE`, brief 6b). ⚠ _scratch_, never _blank_: elsewhere _blank_ is truly empty (a new component, a new calendar), and an empty session layout draws the built-in floor (owner LC, 2026-09-29: the conversation in the middle unless the genre omits it, and the genre's declared panels where they go by default). ⚠ No _Discard changes_ and no _changed_ badge: there is no base to differ from. The **card menu** (built 2026-09-30, brief 6b: `LayoutCardMenu` over `RowMenu`, items from `startFrom.ts` **`cardMenu`** · `CardMenuAction` · `CardMenuContext`) holds _Use for new *Genre* sessions_ / _Stop using for new sessions_ (`:setNewSessionLayout`; the card new sessions start from — **`newSessionLayoutOf`**: the chosen one, else the genre default layout — wears the star of _set as default_), _Make a copy_ (`:clone`), and on a layout the person manages (**`canManageLayout`**: theirs; an admin's for someone else's SHARED one) _Share with everyone on this server_ / _Stop sharing_ (`:share`, which names the session the editor is open in, of the layout's genre: a guest is a guest ON A SESSION, and a guest there is refused PUBLISHING — ⚠ advisory, since the same person owns any session they make; taking one private needs no more than managing it; the menu draws no share control at all for a guest in that session), _Rename_, _Delete_. |

**The Adventure genre's four agents.** Words for the _roles_ in one multi-agent turn, not for
node kinds or for pipelines: each is a step of `core:spec/adventure-respond`, and each has its
own context node definition so it has its own editable prompt.

| Term             | Means                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **planner**      | The step that decides what happens next and **who speaks**, and writes no prose. A genre with one declares `speakerStrategies: []`: turn-taking is this step's output, never a next-speaker strategy, and no Turn order control renders.          |
| **narrator**     | The step that writes the scene from the plan. Narrates the world and its consequences; never speaks for the cast. ⚠ Distinct from the standard chat's **Narrator Response**, which is a manually fired message rather than a step of a turn. |
| **voice**        | One cast member's turn inside a reply: one generate per speaker the planner named, each knowing only what that character knows. Not a _speaker_: the speaker is whoever is producing a turn, and an adventure turn has several.                     |
| **state-keeper** | The step that reads the finished reply and reports what it made true, as attribute and possession changes. It reports; it does not decide: its output is a **proposal** unless its routine's mode is **Full** (⏳ was the `trustNarrator` field; §23). 🚧 Adventure's may also say how long the scene took — a **clock proposal** (kind `clock`, live scenes ★3; §25). 🚧 **Whose stats it keeps** (`resolve-state-changes@1`'s in-port **`keeps`**, owner ruling 2026-09-30): `'world'` (the world's and its places'), or one participant reference (that member's alone), or a party speaker fact (`{ characterId }` / `{ name }`); a list keeps every item it holds, read flat, an absent item keeping nobody more. A change to any other owner is refused on the receipt. Absent, every owner, as before. 🚧 The Lair's books are its **Keep the books** routine's (`lair-keeper`, after each round, Review by default; 2026-10-21): the world's, the places' and the delvers'; a **character turn** keeps none. |
| **`ViewerV1.advancedControls`** 🚧 | **Built 2026-11-10 (owner GO; PLAN-advanced-controls-2026-11-10, lane adv-F; ruling ★adv-C-1).** `advancedControls?: boolean`, an additive v1 key on the base **viewer** section (`sdk/src/widgets.ts`), filled live by core's `envelopeSections.svelte.ts`: whether this viewer's **advanced controls** (§26) are on. Absent means shown. The `authors-note` widget declares `reads: ['viewer']` and hides its depth, interval and _Sent as_ when it is `false`. **Replaced the plan's `SessionDossier.advancedControls`** (★adv-C-1): there is no dossier field and no new scope. ⚠ Not a permission. |
| **`lockedByAdvanced`** (`SessionLorebookReading`) 🚧 | **Built 2026-11-10 (owner GO; PLAN-advanced-controls-2026-11-10, lane adv-F).** An optional prop: with `readOnly`, an owner who sees the reading read-only only because **advanced controls** are off reads _Turn on advanced controls to change them._ (★adv-B-2). |
| **`ActionListDeps.advancedControls`** 🚧 | **Built 2026-11-10 (owner GO; PLAN-advanced-controls-2026-11-10, lane adv-C).** `advancedControls(): boolean` (`sessionPage/actionList.svelte.ts`): off leaves core's _Branch from here_ out of every venue; a genre action keyed `branch` is never filtered. |

⚠ The four split two ways, and the split is what decides how each is put on the wire. The
planner and the state-keeper are asked a **question**: no speaker, no line to continue, and
the answer's shape carried by whichever **structured door** (§10) the connection opens. The
narrator and the voices take a **turn**: each prompt ends on its own speaker's line, the
narrator's being the Narrator. A question's transcript is **prose only** — a JSON block an
earlier reply left behind is cut on the way into the prompt and never in the stored message,
or the next planner reads its own shape back and the state-keeper answers in the planner's.

**Resolved collisions**

- ⚠ **`character`** → a cast member. A text position is an **offset** or **column** — never
  "character 494" in a system with a character named Vell.
- · **`message`** → a session message. Socket traffic is an **event**; an error carries
  **text**.
- · **cast**, not _participants_.
- ⚠ **entry / edge / attribute slot** are three different things and conflating them is the
  classic modelling trap. A named topic with prose is an **entry**; "this relates to that" is an
  **edge** (a relationship or a possession); "this owner's number changed" is an **attribute
  slot**. See docs/stats-and-states.md.

**Socket interest** — transport vocabulary, used app-wide, recorded here because §9 is where
_event_ is defined. Built 2026-09-14 (phases 1–3 of `~/.claude/plans/socket-interest.md`).

- · **interest** — a client's declared wish to receive one kind of event. Not a _lease_ (a
  model permission, §10), not a _subscription_, not a _watch_.
- · **interest key** — `event` or `event#scope` (`sessions:streamChunk#42`). Never the bare
  `key`. `interestKey()` in `shared/sockets/interest.ts`.
- · **interest registry** — the ONE client module holding every subscriber, counted per key,
  one raw socket listener per event name: `client/sockets/interest.svelte.ts`
  (`declareInterest`, `requestWithInterest`, `useInterest`). Contexts `interest` and
  `adminInterest` wrap it; the second exists only inside `/admin`.
- · **interest set** — the server's per-socket copy of the keys (`socket.interest`), cleared
  on disconnect, never on silence.
- · **interest sync** — the `interest:sync` message: the client's full key list, replacing the
  set. Sent before a request it wants answered, on every key change, every 30 s, and on
  every connect. Self-healing, not a keepalive.
- · **interest gate** — the check in `emitToUser` and `broadcastHelpers`: a **gated event**
  (in `GATED_EVENTS`, empty until a family's last consumer has moved to the registry) is
  emitted per interested socket, or not at all — and a **thunk** passed as its payload runs
  only then, so the cascade's query is never paid for a reply nobody wants.
- · **interest scope** — the `#scope` half of a key, and the only way a push is narrowed to one
  entity. `SCOPED_EVENTS` in the shared module is the ONE table saying where each scoped
  event's scope lives in its payload (`scopeOfPayload`); both sides read it, because a client
  guessing a scope the server does not extract is a silent drop. A bare key means every scope.
  `sessions:get` scopes on `payload.session.id`, not a top-level `sessionId` — the table says so.
- ⚠ **restricted interest** — a key under `RESTRICTED_INTEREST_PREFIXES`, whose whole family
  is admin-only. Refused by the registry for a non-admin and dropped by the server from a
  non-admin's sync. Defence in depth: the handlers' own admin checks remain the boundary. A
  family with one non-admin reader (`activity:`, `connections:`, `systemSettings:`) must
  never be listed, or non-admins go dark on it.
- · **held restricted interest** — a restricted key declared while the user is still
  UNKNOWN (before `users:current` lands, or after a logout). Held, not _refused_: the
  subscriber is kept but the key is in no sync, so an unidentified session names no
  restricted key on the wire. `setInterestUser` empties the hold — an admin declares them for
  real, a non-admin drops them as refused. "Unknown" is not "non-admin" (2026-09-15).

---

## 10. Connections

| Term                        | Means                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **connection**              | A configured way to reach a model. Since 0114 the row is an **endpoint** and the models it reaches are rows of their own — see the three entries below.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **endpoint**                | **What a `connections` row IS** since 0114: where the compute is — base URL, key, wire protocol, the capabilities the _protocol_ can express. The table keeps its name and its ids (every foreign key points at it), so _connection_ and _endpoint_ name the same row; say **endpoint** when the point is that it is not a model.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **connection model**        | One row in `connection_models`: a model reachable **through** an endpoint. Holds the identifier the adapter sends, a display name, and _overrides_ of the endpoint's prompt format, token counter, capabilities and context window. ⚠ Never a **local model** (above) — that is a file on disk this install owns; this is a name an endpoint answers to, which for a managed connection happens to be that file's.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **(endpoint, model) pair**  | What every selection in the app actually is: a **job default** or a pipeline's **connection slot** — the oracle's `connection` slot (control `connection-ref`, value SDK `ConnectionSlotValue` `{ref, modelId}`; its twin is the **sampling slot**) — the only two tiers; a session names no connection (ruled 2026-09-15, §23). **Both halves are required.** A registration naming only the endpoint is _incomplete_ and resolves as _unconfigured_, with a sentence naming the fix — never as some model the endpoint is presumed to mean (ruled 2026-09-15; §23 _default model_). ⚠ The two halves never travel apart: a model belongs to one endpoint, so changing the endpoint _clears_ the model rather than carrying it across.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **default loadout** (as a person reads a transform's default) _(was: **job** · **job default**, retired as user-facing words 2026-10-12, §23; code ⏳: capability default, `job*`)_ | **Amended 2026-10-12** (owner 2026-10-12: _"need to stop using nicknames for the modality defaults; loadouts simplify the concepts for users now."_) Everywhere a person reads, a transform's default is **the ‹X› loadout** — _the Reply loadout_, _the Images loadout_, _the Embeddings loadout_, _the Entities loadout_, _the Narration loadout_ (`shared/loadouts/defaultLoadoutName.ts`: `defaultLoadoutName` · `defaultLoadoutPhrase`; a transform core ships no default loadout for takes its SDK label, _the Vision loadout_). Never _job_, _job default_, _Chat replies_, _chat model_ / _chat default_, _image default_, _capability default_ or _active_ for it (§23). `jobLabel` (both copies) answers the loadout's name. Its setters say **Use in Reply** · **Use in Images** · **Use in Embeddings** · **Use in Entities** (were _Use for chat_ …, _Make active_, a model's _Set as default…_ → **Use in…**); the toast says _Gemma 3 is now in the Reply loadout._ The admin section is **Admin › Models › Loadouts** (URL `/admin/defaults` kept; its rows are named by loadout). ⚠ **What it's for** on a model (_Chat · Image generation · Embeddings · Named entities · Not sure_) describes the MODEL and keeps its words. Was: a **job** is a transform the pub needs a default pair for — chat, images, embeddings, entities, vision, … — and its **job default** is that pair: the instance-wide (endpoint, model) pair registered for it, one row of `connection_defaults`, keyed `(input, output)`, carrying `connection_id` + `connection_model_id` (+ a sampling config). What a run uses when nothing overrides it. Ruled 2026-10-09 (design C.2, owner C-Q2): copy and this canon say **job** now, and _capability default_ is retired in copy (§23); the code keeps its `capability*` names for this sense (`capabilityEntry`, `CapabilityModel`, `capabilityStateWord`, the `capability` props) ⏳ until `connection_defaults` next changes, then renames to `job*` (`jobTile`, `jobLabel` and `chooseJobModel` already are). Chat's job is labelled **Chat replies** where a person picks its model (`jobLabel`: what the pair is FOR; _Chat_ is also a genre); every other job takes the SDK's label. Every way to set one is the same call, **`chooseJobModel`** — the **job picker**'s **Use**, a Models tab's **Use** / **Use for chat**, a model's **Set as default…**, a managed runtime's **Use**, a local ONNX model's **Make active**, Set up chat's first model: one costed confirmation, one write (`connections:setDefault`), one toast (`chosenSentence`). **Admin → Defaults** edits the same rows. ⚠ Not a **capability** (below), which is what a connection or a model CAN do. |
| **needed** (a default loadout) · **Off** | **Amended 2026-10-12:** copy counts loadouts — _1 loadout needs a model_ · _Every loadout this pub needs is filled_ · _The Reply loadout needs a model_ (Needs you). **Built 2026-10-11 (less-confusing C1/C2).** A job is **needed** on this pub when it is chat (every session reply runs on it) or when a step requiring it failed in a real run in the last 7 days (`server/admin/jobUse.ts`, `NeededBecause` `replies` \| `failedRun`). Unset and needed: status **Needed** on Admin › Defaults and one gold **Needs you** item, counted by the Overview's Models card. Unset and not needed: **Off**, in surface tone, with what would use it. ⚠ Not **demanded** (`ComboRow.demanded`): some catalog node requires the job, which is true of image generation on every pub. |
| **service**                 | The vendor: Ollama, OpenAI, KoboldCpp. _(never "provider")_                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **adapter**                 | The code that speaks a service's protocol.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **local model**             | A model **file this install owns**, on disk — one row in `local_models`: a GGUF or safetensors file one row by `filename` alone; an ONNX model one row per (Hub id, **modality**), each with its own cache directory (two partial unique indexes, migration 0144, 2026-11-04). Not a connection and not a service: a connection may _point at_ one by bare filename. Vendor-neutral by construction, because `.gguf` is not KoboldCPP's — llama.cpp opens the same bytes — so no row names an engine; which engines can load one is **derived** from format and modality. **Amended 2026-10-29 (model consolidation, PLAN-model-library §2):** the owner skipped the segregation for this pass, so the row still names no directory and no runtime; which runtimes hold a file is the **model presence** read, worked out on each ask from the folders and stores. An ONNX row's `quantization` holds the **precision** it was downloaded at (lane MA), which its loader reads before the list's default. |
| **model format**            | The **container**: `gguf` · `onnx` · `safetensors`. A property of the bytes, read off the file, so it carries no provenance. ⚠ Says nothing about what the model is _for_ — the curated image models are every one of them `.gguf`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **modality**                | What a model is **for**: `text-gen` · `embeddings` · `image-gen` · `ner` · `tts` (UI label _speech_) · 🚧 `asr` (UI label _transcription_: audio in, text out — the managed audio.cpp's transcription packages, written by its model sync) · 🚧 `matting` (a `local_models` row only — the cut-out's background remover; §25) · … An open vocabulary whose contract is the SDK's connection _shapes_. One word across `connections.modality`, `local_models.modality` and `connection_models.modality` (0172). On an endpoint it is the primary FILING only; on a **connection model** it is what the model serves, and `capabilityRefusal` refuses a transform of another modality — one endpoint can serve several (an Ollama host chats and embeds, the managed KoboldCPP chats and draws). NULL on a connection model means the host said nothing, and is ungated. ⚠ **Not detectable from a file**, which is the half `kind_source`'s trust ordering grades. Icons are the output kind's — §22.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **capability** | What a connection or a model CAN do: its transforms (`text->text`, …) and features (tools, streaming). The word's only sense, in code and copy (design C.2, 2026-10-10); the default pair a transform needs is a **job** (above). |
| **capability grade**        | How well it does it. The grades are `none` · `emulated` · `native`, exported by the SDK as `Band` / `BAND` / `bandOf` / `bandsFor` — ⚠ **nothing to do with a retrieval band** (§7).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **sampling config**         | Temperature, penalties, context window: one `sampling_configs` row, edited in the **Sampling** view (rail) and managed in **Admin → Models → Sampling**; chosen in a **loadout sheet**'s step 3 (_was_ the job sheet's step 2; its **Open in Sampling** goes to the view), in Admin → Pipelines (a model call's pick) and in a session's settings (the session's sampling pick); referenced by a **sampling slot**. The Sampling view left the rail and came back on 2026-10-11 (§23). The only word (ruled 2026-09-30, Q2) — ⚠ never _sampling preset_: **preset** is the session preset's and the author preset's. A ComfyUI loadout's step 3 offers the image configs like any image loadout; a workflow never has configs of its own — its settings are its **workflow variables** (§23 **workflow shape**, reversed 2026-10-12). |
| **sent** / **not sent** · **N of M sent** · **Choose parameters** · **Holds a default** · **Built in** · **Used by** · **Use in loadouts…** _(was: Set as default…)_ | **Amended 2026-10-12 (loadout words):** the ⋯ item and its dialog are **Use in loadouts…** (_Tick the default loadouts that should use ‹config›_); a row reads _6 of 34 sent · in the Reply and Vision loadouts_, the ★ _In the Reply loadout_, **Used by** lists _Reply · loadout_, the toast _The Reply loadout uses Creative now._, deleting says _The Images loadout uses it, so it will use the connection's own defaults…_. **Built 2026-10-10 (design D.1–D.3, owner D-Q1).** The Sampling view's words — in its editor and in Admin → Models → Sampling's change form (the view left the rail and came back on 2026-10-11, §23; the sheet's _Edit parameters…_ editor that carried them meanwhile is retired). A config's parameter is **sent** or **not sent** (its `enabled` set): the editor shows the sent ones, and **Choose parameters** (a toggle, tonal with `aria-pressed` while on) shows every parameter of the shape in place, each with its checkbox, a parameter not sent dimmed and reading _not sent_; nothing saves until **Save**. **N of M sent** counts them on a list row (_6 of 34 sent · default for Chat replies, Vision_, `samplingRowLine`), beside the Parameters heading and on each group's label (`· 4 of 6 sent`). A row's ★ is **Holds a default**: the config is the sampling half of ANY job's default, read from every `connection_defaults` row of its shape, never one canonical transform; its lock is **Built in** (read-only; **Duplicate** to change it). **Used by**, a card on the detail (`samplingConfigs:usedBy`), lists the jobs whose default names the config and the pipelines whose `sampling` slot picks it, each opening where it is changed. **Set as default…** (the detail's ⋯; `SamplingDefaultsDialog`) lists every job of the shape with the config it names today and a checkbox each (**All** ticks every one); **Apply** names this config as the ticked jobs' sampling half (`samplingConfigs:setDefaultFor`), each job keeping its model, and a job already naming it is shown ticked and fixed — taking a default away is Admin › Defaults'. Retired (§23): _Clone to a new config_, _Update as primary_, the _Enabled parameters_ sub-screen, the category level, the trailing `*`, `samplingConfigs:setUserActive`. |
| **logit bias entry** 🚧    | One row of a sampling config's `logitBias` list (SDK `LogitBiasEntry` `{ text, value }`; the field is `format: 'logit-bias'`): the text read by SillyTavern's syntax (`readLogitBiasText`, `shared/utils/logitBias.ts`) as a **word** (trimmed, tokenized with one leading space), **exact** text (`{…}`, verbatim) or token **ids** (`[1, 2]`) — else **empty** (ignored) or **invalid** (shown beside the row with its reason); the value a bias from −100 to 100 (`LOGIT_BIAS_MIN` / `LOGIT_BIAS_MAX`) given to every token of the sequence. Words rather than ids so one list biases the same words on any tokenizer. ⚠ Always qualified: a bare _entry_ is the lorebook's (§8). |
| **structured door**         | Which of three ways a step asks for a JSON answer, chosen from the connection's own capabilities and recorded on the receipt: **schema** (the shape travels, natively or compiled to a grammar), **object** (JSON, shape unsaid), **instruction** (a sentence in the prompt, which every backend can be asked). A property of the REQUEST, never of the prompt somebody wrote.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **wire mode**               | Which _method_ a service is called by for the same capability: **chat** (role-tagged messages) or **completion** (one text prompt). A connection capability like any other, resolved preset → test → hand-set override (ruled 2026-09-07). Never "chat format" — that collides with prompt format below.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **prompt format**           | How blocks become wire text: Vicuna, ChatML, split-chat. ⚠ Meaningful **only in completion wire mode**; in chat mode the roles carry the structure and this must not be offered. The _value_ on a connection; the row it names is a **completion template**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **completion template**     | One row in `completion_templates` — per-role prefix/suffix, stop strings, and a render mode. **Data, never code**: a template that can compute is a template that can be made to do something other than format. Built-ins seed immutable; a variant is a **clone**. `connections.prompt_format` is an FK to its `key`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **render mode**             | `flat` (one completion string) or `role_array` (role-tagged messages). An **explicit column**, because it used to be decided by `/split/i` against the format _name_ — so any admin-authored name containing "split" would have silently rerouted the pipeline. ⚠ `role_array` is `split_chat` only and is **not admin-authorable**; admin templates are flat, which is what keeps them outside the injection surface.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **recommended list**        | The fetched catalogue of local ONNX models — `embeddings.yaml` / `ner.yaml` from `SerenePub/serene-pub-onnx-list`, cached a day under the data dir, with the built-in copy as fallback. Its fields are the model's facts: `tier` (fast · balanced · best), `size` (MB), `dimensions` / `labels`, `max_input_tokens`, `pooling` (mean · cls · last*token), `prefixes`, `tags` (`long-input`, `multilingual`, …), `released`, `license`. Never "catalogue" for the fetched thing — that word is the built-in fallback's. Entries with `last_token` pooling are excluded until the loader can pool that way. ⚠ There are **three** such lists, and the **model finder** reads all of them: these two, plus the shared GGUF YAML (`SerenePub/serene-pub-gguf-list/recommended.yaml`), whose fields are a different set — `recommended_vram` (GB, and the source of a GGUF row's tier chip), `size` (GB), `details.parameter_size` / `.quantization_level` / `.description`. Say \_the GGUF list* or _the ONNX lists_ when which one matters; the FIELDS are not interchangeable. **Amended 2026-10-29 (lane MA):** an ONNX list entry may carry `dtypes` (the **precisions** it comes in; `catalog.dtypes`), offered in the **quant picker**. The finder now reads a fourth list, the **audio list** (§10 Speech), for the **speech scope** and **transcription scope** only. |
| **local model state**       | What a local ONNX connection model's FILES are doing on this machine: `not_downloaded` · `downloading` · `on_disk` · `error`. A fact about the disk, re-checked on every sync, never durable state — and independent of being the default. Rides on `ModelRow.local`. ⚠ Never a **local model** (§10 above): that is the registry row; this is the row's disk state.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ~~**active**~~ (local modality) _(retired as a user-facing word 2026-10-12, §23)_ | **Amended 2026-10-12:** the row the Embeddings or Entities loadout holds is **In use** (chip, headline _In use · loaded_, connection row state _In use_; nothing held: _Loadout unfilled_); **Make active** → **Use in Embeddings** / **Use in Entities**; copy says _the Embeddings loadout holds one model app-wide_. `isActive`, `makeActive`, `onMakeActive` stay as code names ⏳. Was: the job default for `text->embedding` or `text->entities`, called _active_ in the UI because there is exactly one per modality app-wide. Not a flag, not a column — the same `connection_defaults` row every other default is. **Make active** = _Set as default…_ for that one transform.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

Slots do not truncate because nothing in them is free-form, and the eye scans a column of states rather than reading four sentences. ⚠ Not a **model row** (below) — models left the index with the 2026-09-17 ruling, and a row here never lists any.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

| **connection state**        | What a **connection row** says a connection is doing, in five words and exactly one colour each: `ready` (success — it works now) · `idle` (quiet — set up, nothing wrong, not running) · `unfinished` (primary/gold — it is waiting on YOU: a key, a binary, a model, a refresh) · `busy` (warning — something is in flight) · `broken` (error — it was finished and it still failed). ⚠ **Only `broken` is red.** The split exists because a connection created ten seconds ago with no API key rendered exactly like one whose key had been rejected: a fresh install showed two red rows and two **Fix** buttons out of four, reporting as faults the two things nobody had got to. Ask whether it is finished before asking whether it works. **Amended 2026-10-06:** a listed row that serves chat while chat has no default ANYWHERE is `unfinished` — label **Pick a model**, action **Choose** (verb `choose`, opens the connection) — and green **Ready** only once chat is answered somewhere (`RowStatusFacts.defaults`, `RowDefaults { chatSet }`, `rowDefaults(entries)` from the defaults summary the strip reads). A green row beside _Sessions can't reply yet_ was a row claiming readiness on a pub that could not reply. **Amended 2026-10-10 (design C.2): THE one state scale.** A connection, a job's pair, the chat **status strip** and a connection view's status card all take these five states and tones (`CONNECTION_STATES` · `CONNECTION_STATE_TONE` — success · surface · primary · warning · error — · `CONNECTION_STATE_DOT` · `CONNECTION_STATE_TEXT` · `CONNECTION_STATE_LABEL`); the readiness rows, the next step and the chrome's dot read them, and nothing invents a sixth. **Needs attention** (the index's filter and count, `needsAttention`) is `broken ∪ unfinished`, red and gold, which is what the words say. A failed model listing is `broken` (_Couldn't list models_). Retired (§23): the readiness words (`ok` · `pending` · `warning` · `unset`), the chrome's dot words and the next step's own vocabulary. **Amended 2026-10-24 (★R2, L4.1):** a ROW — the index row, the index card, the admin changelist — wears its state as a 6px dot and 13px muted words (`rowStatusClasses`), and only a **blocked** row (`RowStatus.blocked`: broken AND it fills a default loadout, `loadoutsFilledBy`, the admin **Needs you** reading) is drawn red; a broken row nothing relies on keeps the quiet dot. The scale and its five tones are unchanged for the strip, the tiles and the readiness rows. `stateTone` is retired (its three readers read `rowStatusClasses`). ⚠ Two older copies still spell their own: `defaultsSummary.ts`'s `DefaultState` and `managedConnectionView.ts`'s `StatusDot` (follow-up). | **loadout** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-12 (I12; DESIGN-image-generation §11–§14, owner "I like it", word ruled).** The third model layer, after **modality** and **capabilities**: what a kind of work runs on — the **pair** (connection, model), a **sampling config** by reference (it owns no knobs; the 09-02 shape ruling stands) and, when the pair's drawing sheet takes a template payload, a **workflow**. Never prompts, parameters, template, settings or scripts — those say what the STEP means (rule: what changes if you swap the model without touching the step's intent is loadout). Table `loadouts` (0103): `seed_key` (a shipped declaration's id), `slug` (unique per owner), `name`, `description`, `owner` (`core` · plugin id · `pub`), `transform`, the pair, `sampling_config_id`, `workflow_id`, `tier`, `default_for_input`/`_output` (the **default loadout** of that transform, unique per pair), `merged_into`. Ids: `core:loadout/extraction@1` · `acme.rp:loadout/extract@1` · `pub:loadout/<slug>`. A node names one on its oracle's additive **`loadout`** slot (control `loadout-ref`, value `{ id }`, config scope only — `WRITE_MATRIX.loadout`; SDK `slot.loadout(id)`, `p.loadout(node, …)`); resolution per value: the node's explicit slot → its loadout (merges followed) → if **unfilled**, the transform's default loadout (`world.ts` `applyLoadoutLayer`; receipts carry the chain as `loadout`). The transform default IS the default loadout: `connections/capabilityDefaults.ts` reads loadouts only; `connection_defaults` was moved by a boot one-shot (`loadouts/fromConnectionDefaults.ts`). Core's set: `CORE_LOADOUTS` (Reply · Tool calling · Extraction · Scene prompt · **Vision** · Images · Portrait · Sprites · Scene · Narration · Transcription · Spoken reply · Embeddings · Entities); a plugin ships its own in manifest `loadouts[]`, arriving unfilled and unmerged. ⚠ Not a **preset** (three meanings already, R1) and not a **purpose** (a display label, 09-30). Members never see one; a session never picks one. |
| **unfilled** (a loadout) 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-12 (I12).** A loadout whose pair is empty. A node naming it runs on its transform's **default loadout**, whole (pair and sampling together, so neighbouring steps never reload a model for a window). Every shipped loadout arrives unfilled; the wizard fills Reply and Images. UI: _Unfilled — falls back to Reply_. ⚠ Not _Off_ (a job whose **default** loadout has no pair: the job is off, nothing to fall back to) and not an unset slot (a node slot with no value, which reads its loadout). |
| **merged loadout** · **parent loadout** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-12 (I12; §13).** A loadout whose `merged_into` names a parent of the same transform: a run-time redirect — resolution follows the chain to its root, the child's own pair/sampling/workflow are kept but ignored, and the receipt says _extract → Extraction (merged)_. The pub's act (**Merge into…** / **Unmerge** on the loadout sheet); a plugin never merges anything. A cycle is refused when it would be made (`mergeLoadout`). _merge_ stays an ordinary verb elsewhere. ⚠ Not a copy and not inheritance: nothing of the parent is written into the child, and unmerging restores the child exactly. |

Edits are a draft until **Save** / **Create loadout** (§6.14 unsaved changes; closing asks _Discard unsaved changes?_). Header: the title edited in place · slug in mono · owner chip (_Core_ / plugin id / _Yours_) · the **Default for ‹transform›** star (a toggle, sent with Save; locked on for the current default) · the **what runs** line (_KoboldCPP · Nemo 12B · sampling Chat_, or _Unfilled — falls back to Reply_, gold) · description (read-only prose on a shipped one, with **Duplicate to edit**). Always qualified (R3). ⚠ Not a cast member's **presence** (§8) or the Knowledge **presence** (§14), which say where an entity is in the story; a presence holder is not an attribute's holder. |
| **precision** (of a model file) 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-29 (lane MA).** The number format a model's weights are stored in, as a person picks it: an **audio.cpp package**'s (`precision` in the **audio list**: `q8_0` · `bf16` · `f16` · …; `shared/audio/precision.ts`) and an ONNX model's (`dtype` in code and on the wire: `ONNX_DTYPES` `fp32` · `fp16` · `q8` · `q4`, `shared/constants/onnxDtypes.ts`; the chosen one kept in `local_models.quantization`). The person-facing word for _dtype_ (R5: the code keeps `dtype`, the copy says precision). Picked in the **quant picker**. ⚠ A GGUF chat or image model's files are its _quants_ even where the label (`Q8_0`) is the same: say _precision_ only for an audio.cpp package or an ONNX model. Not a number's precision anywhere else. |
| **Get more…** (a runtime's door) 🚧 | **Ruled 2026-10-29 (model consolidation D1; built by lane MB).** The control on a runtime's Models tab (managed KoboldCPP, Ollama, audio.cpp, a local ONNX connection) that opens **Get a model** with that runtime as the destination and the scopes narrowed to what it holds. Replaces the **Get tab** (§23). ⚠ A door into the one finder, never a finder of its own. **Placement as built (lane MV, 2026-10-29):** KoboldCPP and Ollama: the empty list's one call to action, then a dashed full-width row at the foot of the list (subline _Recommended lists and Hugging Face_); local ONNX: under the table, or in the empty list; audio.cpp: a small button above the groups, always shown. It switches to the Models view (see **model finder**). |
| **machine hardware** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-30 (readiness B3, lane C).** What the pub's own machine has, detected once per process on first ask: `MachineHardware { gpu: { vendor: nvidia · amd · apple · null, name, memoryGb }, systemMemoryGb, platform, arch, detectedAt }` (`shared/connections/machineHardware.ts`), probed by `server/connections/hardware.ts` (`machineHardware()`: Apple silicon by `os.totalmem`, then `nvidia-smi` (largest card wins), Linux `rocm-smi`, Linux sysfs, else nothing; `execFile`, 5 s, never throws) and asked for on the admin-only, gated socket `models:machineHardware` (reply `{ hardware \| null, error? }`) through ONE client asker, `useMachineHardware.svelte.ts`. The interface says _this computer_ / _this Mac_: the computer Serene Pub runs on. ⚠ Not the viewing device (a phone looking at the pub is told about the pub's machine), and not the **memory tier**, which stays the person's answer. AMD on Windows without a tool reads as nothing found. |
| **detected memory tier** · **detected build** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-30 (readiness B3, lane C).** A proposal read off **machine hardware**, always shown with its reason (_Picked because …_) and never stored. `detectedMemoryTier`: usable memory is the card's, about two-thirds of system memory on Apple silicon, about half with no card; shown under the finder's tier line and in its popover until the person answers. `detectedBuild`: NVIDIA → the full build; AMD → a ROCm build if one is offered, else `-nocuda`; Apple silicon → `mac-arm64`; no card → `-nocuda`; wrong-architecture builds dropped; `-oldpc` never proposed; preselected in `KoboldCppBinaryVariantPicker` only when nothing is selected, its reason in the **Selected** box while the selection is still the suggestion. Code `client/components/connections/hardwarePicks.ts`; quoted sizes snap to common sizes within 8%. ⚠ Detection proposes, the person's answer wins; detection never writes storage. |
| **free tier** (of an OpenRouter key) · **free model** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-30 (readiness B2(a), lane C).** An OpenRouter key with no credit bought, as OpenRouter's `GET /api/v1/key` reports it (`data.is_free_tier`, `free_model_daily_requests`): kept server-side as `connections.extra_json.openrouter = { freeTier, freeRequestsPerDay?, checkedAt }` (`OpenRouterKeyFacts`, `server/connections/openRouterKey.ts`; like `extra_json.comfy`, no migration; a create strips a client-sent one, a changed key drops it), read on a passing **Test** and after a clean model listing, and sent to the client as `Sockets.Connections.ModelsSync.freeTier`. A **free model** is one OpenRouter serves for nothing: an id ending `:free`, or priced 0 both ways (`isFreeModel`). On a free-tier key the Models tab and the connections list put free models first (`freeModelsFirst`, a stable split; the Reply loadout's model still leads). UI: the status card's _This key has no credit yet, so paid models would be refused: pick a free one under **Models**, listed first, and press **Use in Reply**._ and the wizard's **Key saved** detail _No credit yet: free models only, about 50 replies a day_. ⚠ Not a gate and not a quota meter: Serene Pub refuses and counts nothing, and a paid model already in Reply is not flagged. |
| **lane status**             | `vectorization:status` / `ner:status`: whether the lane's model is loaded, when it was last used, its idle timeout, and the queue's pending count. The header line and the model view read it; the row's `local.loaded` is only a copy.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

**Resolved collisions**

- ⚠ **`wire mode` vs `prompt format`.** Both answer "what shape goes on the wire", and
  conflating them is what let a live defect hide: adapters derived wire mode from their own
  local flags while the pipeline rendered a prompt format nothing carried. **Wire mode is the
  _method_** (chat or completion, a property of the connection); **prompt format is the
  _delimiters_** inside a completion's single prompt string. Chat mode has no prompt format —
  not a default one, none. Say _wire mode_ for the first and never "chat format" for either.
- ⚠ **`model`** now has two senses in one sentence and they are not interchangeable. A
  **connection model** is a row: a name an endpoint answers to, with its own settings. A
  **local model** (§10, above) is a file on disk this install owns. A managed KoboldCPP
  connection has both, naming the same GGUF, and they are still different things — deleting
  the file forgets the row, deleting the row leaves the file. Say **connection model** or
  **local model** whenever both are in scope; bare _model_ is only safe when it clearly means
  "the thing on the other end".
- ⚠ **`capability`** → _connection_ capabilities. A plugin's is a **permission**. The
  manifest itself was never the obstacle it was feared to be: it has always spelled the
  field `permissions`, so the rename reached the code without touching the public
  contract. See §25 for the one sense it deliberately left alone.

| Term | Means |
| --- | --- |
| **model reads** · **model writes** 🚧 | The kinds a model takes in and gives out (`connection_models.reads`, `.writes`, migration 0109; `modelKindsOf`, `modelKindsAllow`): a NULL half is ungated (the connection's **Vision** / **Hearing** switches still judge reads). UI **What it's for**: **Writes replies** · **Draws pictures** · **Speaks** · **Hears** · **Sees** (`MODEL_PURPOSES`). ⏳ A generating model's single **modality** as its purpose is kept for filing only (§23). |
| **reads by kind** · **known kind** 🚧 | `ConnectionReadsV1.kinds` — per kind `{ reads, why?, cost? { perItem?, perSecond? }, accepts?, assistantTurns? }` (`connectionReadsKind`); media and I/O kinds are open (`MediaKind`/`IoKind` = **known** \| string; R41). ⏳ `.image` · `.pdf` · `.why` · `.tokensPerImage` (§23). |
| **requested outputs** 🚧 | `generate-text@1`'s `outputs` param (`['text']` default; `['text', 'audio']` asks for a spoken reply; `requirementForOutputs`, `capabilityForOutputs`). |
| **Transcription** · **Spoken reply** (loadouts) · **Hearing** 🚧 | `core:loadout/transcription@1` (audio→text; writes down a voice note for a model that can't hear) and `core:loadout/spoken-reply@1` (text→text+audio), both arriving unfilled; the transform `text+audio->text` is named **Hearing**, `text->text+audio` **Spoken reply**. |
| **Transcribe audio** (step) · **file transcript** 🚧 | `core:oracle/transcribe-audio@1` (shape `core:shape/transcription@1`; ⚠ not the provisional `speak@1`), the `heard` step before placement in the shipped replies; each recording heard once and kept as `files.transcript`. |
