Per-kind prompt cost (`InputLimits.cost`; `mediaTokens`, `mediaFit`). |

### Speech vocabulary 🚧 (proposed 2026-10-28)

The words the speech build uses (`plans/PLAN-speech-build-2026-10-28.md`, `plans/PLAN-speech-connections-and-timbre-2026-10-28.md`). Every one is 🚧 until the build is verified: free to move on contact with implementation. Grepped across both repositories and the schema on 2026-10-28; where a near-neighbour exists the ⚠ says what the word is not (§24 step 5).

| Term | Means |
| --- | --- |
| **speech facts** 🚧 | What a speaking model can be asked for: voices (each with labels, language, preview, origin), the `controls` it honours, formats, streaming. `connection_models.facts.speech` (`SpeechFacts`, `readSpeechFacts`). Voices come **discovered**, **catalogued** or **typed**. ⚠ Not `ModelFacts` (the model's context and reads), which carries no `speech` key. |
| **speech dialect** 🚧 | One module serving the OpenAI-shaped `/v1/audio/speech` route, reused across connection types (OpenAI, KoboldCpp, Ollama, audio.cpp); each type is a profile over it. ⚠ Not a **template engine** and not a connection type. |
| **voicebank** 🚧 | The pub's named voices: table `voicebank_voices`, namespace `Sockets.Voicebank`, UI Loadouts → _Voices_. No entry is starred: each loadout points at its own **loadout voice** and **other speakers** entry (0137; the stars were dropped in 0138). Each entry lives on a **loadout** (`loadout_id`; a `text->audio` loadout): one pair per voice, through its loadout's merge root; the entry's model is derived at read time, never stored (0136 dropped `connection_model_id`). An entry whose loadout was deleted is unassigned and one on an unfilled loadout has no model yet; both are skipped, with no fallback. It carries no narration prose: a narrator is picked from the voicebank, never written. ★15: the owner said "Roster"; the code word stays `voicebank` unless the owner objects. ⚠ Not the **cast roster** or **member roster**, and not a character's **timbre**. |
| **timbre** 🚧 | How a character sounds: `extensions.serenepub.timbre` on the card (`CharacterTimbreInput`, `timbreOfExtensions`): a voicebank pick as the base (only an administrator makes it, `canPickVoice`) with the card's own description, language, speed, seed and dials layered over it on dialogue only, and `narrationVoice`, an override narrator picked from the voicebank. No narration prose (`narrationDescription` retired 2026-10-29, §23). Card export keeps all but the picks. UI: the card's **Speech** tab. ⚠ Not **portrayal**, not the user voicing a character (**persona**, §9), not the adventure's _voice_ (§9, a cast member's turn in a reply), not a ruleset voice, and not the card's **Voice** tab (how the character writes). |
| **inflection** 🚧 | A line's mood: the record `{ label, intensity?, events? }` (`Inflection`; labels from `INFLECTION_LABELS`, the sprite standard set plus `neutral`; phase 1 writes `label` only). Carried to a voice by the **inflection sentence** or **inflection tag** layout, whichever the voice's `controls` take. ⚠ Not a **tone** setting. |
| **speech cue** 🚧 | One piece of a spoken line with its inflection: code type `Cue`. Always qualified (R3). ⚠ Not a **scene cue** (§9). |
| **silent timbre** 🚧 | `timbre.silent: true` on a card: this character's lines are never spoken, whatever the session's Read aloud says. UI switch **Spoken aloud** (on by default; off writes `silent`). Travels with the card. Owner ruling 2026-10-28: the session decides whether audio is made, the character whether it is spoken. ⚠ Not a muted voicebank row (`enabled: false`). |
| **spoken playback** 🚧 | How spoken lines play for ONE person: `user_settings.spoken_playback` ∈ `auto` · `click` · `never` (`SpokenPlayback`, `spokenPlayback.ts`; socket `userSettings:updateSpokenPlayback`; dossier `spokenPlayback`). UI **Settings → Spoken lines**: _Play as they arrive_ · _Play when I press_ · _No player_. Playback only — never whether audio is made (that is the session's **Read aloud**). |
| **cue map** 🚧 | Where each **speech cue** falls in a line's audio: `CueMap { source: 'concatenated' \| 'service' \| 'none', spans: { cue, startMs, endMs }[] }`, recorded in the **spoken metadata**. The spoken line names the cue playing from it. ⚠ Not the marker or tag crosswalk (which turns a mood into what a voice understands). |
| **spoken as** 🚧 | The receipt of how a line was spoken: `SpokenAs { voice, voices?, model, applied, ignored }` (SDK; no connection, R53 — the host's `SpeechResult.spokenAs` adds it). UI: the line _Spoken as ‹voice› · ‹model› · said with ‹mood›_ under a spoken line. |
| **spoken metadata** 🚧 | `SpokenMeta { spokenAs, cueMap, inflection, template, at }`, stored per swipe at the message's `metadata.spoken`; the audio itself is the line's `core:audio` part. |
| **line template** 🚧 | The Jinja context template that turns a message into the text sent for speaking (`SPOKEN_LINE_TEMPLATE_IDS`: whole · dialogue · narration); the session setting `speechTemplate`, UI **What is read** (_As the pipeline says_ — unset, the speak step's own — · _Whole line_ · _Dialogue only_ · _Narration only_). ⚠ Not a **message template** (§15). |
| **inflection sentence** · **inflection tag** 🚧 | The two variable layouts that carry the inflection into the spoken-line context: the sentence form (words) and the tag form (`[tag]`, kept only where the voice's `controls.tags` allows it). |
| **audio_streaming** 🚧 | The feature key for a connection that can stream speech as it is made. UI label **Streaming speech**. |
| **Read aloud** 🚧 | (1) The session settings card, and its field `speechReadAloud`, UI **Read replies aloud**: **Off** · **Make audio** · **Make and play** (siblings `speechTemplate` _What is read_ — unset is _As the pipeline says_, `speechNarratorVoice` _Narrator voice_ — a voicebank pick, `sessionLanguage` _Language_; reach owner; `speechNarrateUser` is a **reserved** key, no longer declared, for _Read my lines too_ when it is built). (2) The message verb **Read aloud** (`read-aloud`, with **Say it as…**, `say-it-as`) that speaks one line on demand. One meaning — speak the line — at two scopes; the card's own run starts from **message settled**, not inside the reply (**Built 2026-10-29**). ⚠ Not the Narration loadout (which says _who_ speaks, not _whether_). |
| **Spoken lines** 🚧 | The one folded row for spoken audio (_Spoken lines · N files · X MB · Clear_): a derived form of a message, never a media-list item (`media:list` leaves it out unless `includeSpoken`). Per session in its **Read aloud** settings card (owner, admins); pub-wide in **Admin › Data**. **Amended 2026-10-29:** a line's player lives in the **speech popout** too; message styles that draw the line as a bubble, page, compact row or cameo hide the strip's player row by CSS alone (the plain layout keeps it). **Amended again 2026-10-29 (owner):** the default sheet (`widgets.css`) hides the strip's glyph, player, clock, ⋯ and Stop and clips its Speaking… in every style, the plain layout too (the `<audio>` stays and plays); a user style may re-show them. |
| **audio.cpp, run by Serene Pub** 🚧 | The speech and transcription runtime this pub downloads, starts and stops: connection type `audiocpp_managed`, its managed view (an `acpp-binary` stage, then **Models · Process · Arriving · Settings**) and the Add menu item of the same name. Run by is the one verb, as for KoboldCPP; Serene Pub does run it. ⚠ Not the external `audiocpp` connection type — an audio.cpp someone starts themselves, shown as **audio.cpp**. |

| **envoy voice** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-29; description fields retired 2026-10-30.** How one seated envoy of the session's genre sounds: the keyed genre-field family `speechEnvoyVoice:<slug>` · `speechEnvoyNarrationVoice:<slug>` (`SPEECH_ENVOY_FIELD_PREFIXES`, `speechEnvoyFieldKey`, `parseSpeechEnvoyFieldKey`, `EnvoySpeech`, `readEnvoySpeech`, `readAllEnvoySpeech`, `sessionEnvoySpeech`; form field `speechEnvoys`). Voices are picked, never described: stored `speechEnvoyDescription:*` values are ignored. Blank means **Auto** (see **other speakers**). UI **Envoy voices** block on the Read aloud card, owner only; each row shows `SpeechFallback` (_Auto: Mira — avoids the narrator_); written only by the session settings form, never at creation or by presets. |
| **narration voice** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-29; pub scope replaced 2026-10-30.** The voice that reads the prose around a line's speech, qualified by scope (R3): a **character's** (`timbre.narrationVoice` slug, pub-local, dropped on export; UI **Narrator** › **Override narrator**), an **envoy's** (see **envoy voice**), the **session's** (`speechNarratorVoice`, UI **Narrator voice**) and the loadout's (**loadout voice**; there is no separate pub narration voice). Resolved by `resolveVoice` with `cueVoice: 'speaker' \| 'narrator'`. `VoiceFrom`: `timbre` · `envoy` · `narration-timbre` · `envoy-narration` · `session` · `other-speakers` · `auto` · `loadout-voice` · `loadout-first` · `loadout` · `service`. Dialogue with a speaker: card → envoy → other speakers (pinned) → auto → narrator chain. Narration in a line: card override narrator → envoy narration voice → narrator chain. **Narrator chain:** session narrator → the Narration loadout's loadout voice → its first voice → the loadout's sampling `voice` → the service's default. An unknown, off or unusable voice is skipped. Descriptions: only the card's own (dialogue) and the chosen voice's own. |
| **loadout voice** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-30.** A speaking loadout's default voice, the narrator: `loadouts.default_voice_id` (a voicebank entry on this loadout; `Loadouts.Summary.defaultVoiceId`). UI **Voice** on the loadout sheet. Seeded to the first voice on an empty voicebank; when its entry is deleted or moved it falls to the loadout's lowest-id enabled voice (`ensureLoadoutVoice`). ⚠ Not the loadout's sampling `voice` (a service voice id, the arm after it), not a voicebank entry's own service voice, not the retired **narration default**. |
| **other speakers** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-30.** The slot for every speaker without a voice of its own: `loadouts.other_speakers_voice_id` (null = **Auto**; `Loadouts.Summary.otherSpeakersVoiceId`). UI **Other speakers** beside **Voice**. Turning the pinned entry off (or moving or deleting it) returns the slot to Auto. ⚠ Not the cast, the **other participants** of a session or the **member roster**: it names a voice, never people. |
| **auto voice pick** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-30.** What Auto chose for one speaker: the keyed genre-field `speechAutoVoice:<speakerRef>` in `sessions.genre_fields` (`SPEECH_AUTO_VOICE_PREFIX`; `pickAutoVoice`, `server/speech/autoVoice.ts`). Always qualified (R3): a bare "auto" is also the `VoiceFrom` value and the UI word **Auto**. Rule: an enabled entry of the Narration loadout other than the narrator's, avoiding entries other speakers already hold; deterministic. Sticky per session; dropped when its entry is off, gone, moved to another loadout or has become the narrator's. Previews never write it. **Casting tags**: a genre envoy may declare `EnvoyDecl.casting` (`{role?: 'narrator-like' | 'speaker', gender?, age?}`, SDK, 2026-10-30; no shipped genre sets it), which narrows the pool to the entries whose `labels` match best — a hint, never a pick. ⚠ `casting` there is voice casting, not spell**casting** (the **casting pool**, `conventions.casting`, the `casting` repertoire tag and fit flag) — ★ rename to `voiceCasting` before 0.7 if the owner wants R1 kept strictly. ⚠ Not an envoy voice (the owner's explicit pick, which always wins). |
| **audio events** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-29 (speech polish, host-element vocabulary 1.7).** The host `audio` element forwards `play` · `pause` · `ended` · `timeupdate` (throttled page-side to 250 ms: `TIMEUPDATE_MIN_MS`, `shouldForward`) and `loadedmetadata`, each with detail `{ currentTime, duration, paused }` in seconds (duration 0 until known). `HOST_ELEMENTS_VERSION` 1.7. Lets a component draw play state, the clock and the playing **speech cue**. **Amended 2026-10-29 (heading audio control, vocabulary 1.8):** the `audio` element gains the boolean attribute `playing`; the page calls `play()` when it turns on (or lands on) and `pause()` when it turns off, flipping the old one off before the new one on, and never pauses an element that lands without it (so `autoplay` still plays). A `play()` the browser refuses is answered with a `pause` event so the component stays honest. Core's alone, like `autoplay` (`receiverRules.ts` refuses it from a plugin). The element's own events stay the truth. **One sound at a time** is the page rule behind it: the Messages widget plays one line at a time (`conv.speech`), and a voice try-out and a line hand off to each other. |
| **spoken voice name** · **cue text** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-29.** `SpokenAs.voiceName?` (the voicebank voice's name), `SpokenAs.voiceFrom?` (`SpokenVoiceFrom`: whose voice it was) and `CueSpan.text?` (the words of a cue, so the spoken line can caption the cue playing; only lines spoken from now on carry it). UI: the voice chip and the caption. |
| **collect suggestions** · **collect remember** · **collect preview** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-29.** Three optional fields on `CollectedText` (an action's text collection): `suggestions` (`{ value, label, icon?, common? }[]`, at most `MAX_TEXT_SUGGESTIONS` = 40; chips, the non-`common` ones behind **More** / **Fewer**), `remember: 'session'` (`TEXT_REMEMBER`; the last value is kept per viewer in the browser as `sp:collect:<sessionId>:<identity>`) and `preview` (an I18n template with `{subject}` and `{value}`). Drawn by `CollectSuggestions.svelte` for any action; **Say it as…** uses all three. App attributes `data-collect-suggestions` · `-suggestion` · `-more` · `-preview`. ⚠ Not the **voice try-out**'s mood chips. |
| **speech availability** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-29.** Dossier `speech { canSpeak, reason }`, stamped on `sessions:get` by `speechAvailability(db)` (`server/speech/voicebank.ts`) and read once at session load; `VerbContext.speechReason`, `SPEAK_VERB_KEYS`, `quickRowActions(primary, ctx, showDisabled?)`. A disabled speak verb says why (_no voice is set up on this pub yet_). Read replies aloud **Off** never disables it. |
| **Try this voice** · **SpeechClip** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-29.** The button on each block of a card's Speech tab (**Voice**, **Narration voice**) that points the one **voice try-out** at that voice (`tryoutRequest`, `TryoutTarget`); its headings read _Try the voice_ / _Try the narration voice_. `SpeechClip.svelte` is its clip player (_Play the clip_ / _Pause the clip_, clock, voice badge, _Clip position_ bar). |

## 11. Indexing

| Term                 | Means                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **lane**             | An independent background processing queue with its own model, TTL and lifecycle. **Indexing only** when bare — the session sense is always the qualified **channel lane** (§9, ruled 2026-10-12), which resolves the collision §25 carried: `lane` in `ChannelRef`, the widget `lane` setting and `slug:n` are channel lanes. Still loose: `llmQueue`'s own `Lane`, Argon2id's parallelism parameter (OWASP's word, leave it), and _a workstream_ in comments. |
| **broker**           | What a lane asks for a model. A lane never loads one itself.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **lease**            | Permission to use a model, possibly pending. _(was: `grant`)_                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **residency**        | Whether a model is loaded.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **promotion**        | Moving specific items to the front of a lane's queue because a query needs them now.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **sweep**            | A lane's periodic scan for new or stale work.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **turn hold**        | A running turn's mark that the lanes yield to (`indexing/turnHold.ts`: `withTurnHold` around `runTurn`, `isTurnHoldActive`, `whenTurnsQuiet`, `TURN_HOLD_GRACE_MS`). While one is open, and for the grace after the last closes, a lane picks no background item; a **promotion** is never held. ⚠ Not a lock — nothing a turn does waits on it — and not residency. A background picker gives way mid-pick through **`LanePickContext.giveWay()`**. |
| **named vector**     | One of several independently-queryable vector spaces per row.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **freshness triple** | `sourceHash` + `extractorVersion` + `gazetteerHash`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **annotation**       | An extracted entity recorded against a row.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Search by meaning** · **indexed** · **not indexed yet** · **needs re-indexing** | **Ruled 2026-10-11 (less-confusing H1).** One word per concept in copy. **Search by meaning** is the feature as people see it: the **semantic** mechanism (§7) over the session lorebook's entries and nothing else (`SEMANTIC_SEARCH_SOURCES`). **indexed** · **not indexed yet** · **needs re-indexing** are a row's states for it: a vector from the current model, no vector, a vector another model made. The indexing notice above the composer (`RagNotice`, words in `sessionPage/ragNotice.ts`) and the entry and character mark (`EmbeddingStatusIcon`) say only these. **Embeddings** stays the name of the connection **job** (§10, `text->embedding`): its Admin › Models › Defaults row and group, the Connections job tile and first-run door (_Powers Search by meaning_), _Use for embeddings_. ⚠ Copy never says _vectors_, _embedded_, _RAG_ or _Smarter lore retrieval_ for these; the code keeps its names (`RagNotice`, `ragIgnored`, `vectorization:*`, `EmbeddingStatusIcon`, `vectorizedAt`). ⚠ Search by meaning never searches messages, so copy never says it finds them. |

**Resolved collisions**

- ⚠ **`grant`** → **lease** for models. _Grant_ means a plugin permission. Fresh collision,
  cheap now.
- ⚠ **`lane`** → indexing only. Spec branches are **gather branches**; retrieval ways are
  **mechanisms**.
- · **`vector`** → the embedding. A **named vector** is the space.

## 12. Extensions

| Term                        | Means                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **hook**                    | A declared point where authored code may run.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **script**                  | Authored code at a hook, **written and edited in the app by an admin or a modder**. No packaging, no install step. Core may ship one, but that does not make _script_ mean first-party — origin is not the distinction.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **script kind**             | **Ruled 2026-09-15** (_was_ **script type**). The declared contract a script is checked against for a given hook (`core:script:candidates/filter@1`, `…/rescore@1`) — the kind-relation, so it takes the kind word, as **node kind** does. A slot accepts script kinds, not arbitrary code. **Landed in code 2026-09-16:** `defineScriptKind`, `ScriptKindDecl`, `allScriptKinds`, manifest `hookKinds`; a receipt's script record says `scriptKind`. ⏳ `pipeline_scripts.type_id` and the `Scripts.*.typeId` wire fields keep the old word — the ruling named the declaration, not the column. Open by the same logic: _entry type_, _attribute type_.                                                                                                          |
| **changes script kind**     | **Ruled 2026-09-17 (R11); 🚧 U4.** `core:script:changes/extract@1`, a transform over the `changes` port at a seam on `core:query/resolve-state-changes@1`: it turns text ("HP: 12/20") into changes the gate then validates. Extraction is the one job scripts keep in attribute logic; **rules** (§9) are Liquid and do the reacting. Fixed gate phases, never user-ordered across them: extraction scripts → rules → validation and turn lock → apply or propose.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **Liquid** (as an executor) | **Ruled 2026-09-17 (R11); 🚧 U4.** LiquidJS is the expression language for attribute logic (`derive`, `rules`) and a third **transport** for a script row behind the same chain applier that runs QuickJS and plugin chains, plus a `core:task/liquid@1` task a spec author drops between any two nodes. Pure, in-process, bounded by the parse/render/memory limits `contextLiquid.ts` already sets; its filters (`slot` · `has` · `count` · `clamp` · a seeded `roll`) are the whole power. Handlebars is never an attribute-logic language: prompts are either language, effects are one. ⚠ Templates read attribute results and declarations through three pure helpers written twice (`slot` · `stateOf` · `derive`, R15) and never run a rule or a script. |
| **plugin** 📘                                             | **Packaged** code, installed with a manifest. May contribute hooks, node definitions and scripts. Uninstallable as a unit.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **sandbox**                 | The isolated execution environment both scripts and plugin code run in. _(was: plugin "runtime")_                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **permission**              | What sandboxed code may do. _(never "capability")_                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **manifest**                | A plugin's declaration, stored verbatim; declared limits are clamped at runtime, since author-side validation is advisory.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **dispatch**                | The single seam through which scripts and plugin code are invoked. One interface, deliberately.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **hook ctx kind**           | **Ruled 2026-09-17 (plans/29 R-3; built as plans/30 U6).** Which kind of hook a dispatch is for, and so what its `ctx` carries — `HookCtxKind` in `plugins/hookCtx.ts`, one table both sandboxes read: **task · chain-link** → neither `storage` nor `fetch` (F11; parity with an in-app script); **query · outlet · event · lifecycle** → `storage` (F32); **oracle** → `storage` and `fetch`. Every `callHook` names one; a call without one throws. The word is _ctx_, per §9's rule against "hook surface"; the SDK's `assertHookSurface` keeps its name and is the boot's probe over the event and lifecycle rows.                                                                                                                                           |
| **per-user plugin settings**                              | **Built 2026-09-26.** A plugin settings field declared with scope `user`, stored per person in `plugin_user_settings` and resolved user → pub → default at dispatch (a call with no user gets the pub value); any other field (no `scope`, or `scope: 'pub'`) is the pub's. Edited under Settings → User in the card labelled **Extension settings** (`pluginUserSettings:list` / `:set`, own user only). ⚠ Not a **settings slot** (§4) nor a session's **declared setting** (§9).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **plugin variables** · **template engines** (of a plugin) | **Built 2026-09-26/27.** A plugin declares its **variable templates** (`ExtensionDecl.variables`, plus one per declared band) and its template renderers (`ExtensionDecl.templateEngines`); the packager writes `manifest.variables` / `manifest.templateEngines`, and the host reads both from there (variables are registered at install, boot and sync, withdrawn on uninstall). ⚠ A manifest's `engines` is version ranges only, and a slot's accepted renderers are `acceptedEngines` (§15, §23).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **plugin genre registration**                             | **Built 2026-09-26.** A plugin's genres, and the slots and sheets under its own namespace, registered in-process from the **stored manifest** while the plugin is **installed** — not while enabled (owner ruling 2026-09-26): disabling hides them from listings only, and uninstall withdraws them. App `plugins/pluginGenres.ts`: `registerPluginGenres` (one plugin) and `syncPluginGenres` (the reconcile at boot and on the plugins socket's sync, skipping a plugin whose manifest genres are unchanged); SDK `_registerPackageGenre` and the `_withdraw*` family (`_withdrawGenre` · `_withdrawAttributeSlot` · `_withdrawAttributeSheet`; also `_withdrawSessionEvent`, `_withdrawAnnex`) — host-only, underscored because no package calls them.        |
| **palisade** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-30 (readiness D5, lane P).** What a plugin can and cannot do on this pub, in plain words, read from its permissions alone: `pluginPalisade(permissions)` → `Palisade { can, cannot }` (`shared/plugins/palisade.ts`; `PalisadePermission`). `cannot` holds the fixed limits first (`FIXED_CANNOT`, each with a `rule` naming where it is enforced: no connections, keys or model calls; secrets reach its code as a stand-in; no files, programs or another plugin's files; no direct writes to characters, lorebooks or sessions), then each limit a permission it did not ask for leaves standing (the network, this computer and the local network, the two session-write halves, events, storage). Drawn by `PluginPalisade.svelte` as **Permissions it asks for** (the install review only) and **What it can't do** (the review, and the plugin's page under its permissions, following the ticks). ⚠ Not a **capability** (§10) and not a **permission**: a permission lifts a palisade line; the palisade is what is left. The word is code's; the interface says **What it can't do**. |
| **upload piece** | **Built 2026-10-30 (readiness K6, lane P).** One slice of a plugin package sent over HTTP, so a package of any size up to `SP_PLUGIN_PACKAGE_MAX_MB` passes adapter-node's `BODY_SIZE_LIMIT`: start (POST with the size) → `{ upload, pieceBytes }` (`PackageUploadStart`), each piece a PUT at `?upload&offset` (`PackageUploadPiece`), finish a POST at `?upload`; route `/api/admin/plugins/package`, server `server/plugins/packageUpload.ts`, wire contract `shared/plugins/packageUpload.ts`, client `packageUploadClient.ts`. `pieceBytes` is `BODY_SIZE_LIMIT` less 16 KiB, clamped to 64 KiB–8 MiB; pieces land in `<data>/plugin-uploads/<id>.part`, expire an hour after the last one, and are cleared at boot. Refusals: _That piece is empty._ · _The upload fell out of step. Choose the file again._ · _That upload has expired. Choose the file again._ · _A piece of the upload was too large._ · _This upload must come from Serene Pub's own page._ The button reads **Uploading… n%**, then **Installing…**. Always qualified (R3): ⚠ not a ruleset **piece** (§24, Rulesets vocabulary). |
| **finding code** | A line of `serene-pub check`'s or `serene-pub build`'s report, named by its code: `E_…` refuses (exit 1), `W_…` warns and the build goes on; `--json` prints each with its file, line, message and fix. Both commands run ONE validation (`validatePackage(dir, ignore, out)`, `cli/src/bin.ts`), so **`check` refuses everything `build` refuses** and writes nothing (readiness D3 c33, 2026-10-30): the entry evaluated (`E_ENTRY_THREW`), the compiled plugin, the install findings, the component build (`E_COMPONENT_BUILD`, `W_COMPONENT_BUILD`) and the sandbox bundle (`E_SANDBOX_BUNDLE`), the last two built in memory and written only by `build`. ⚠ One difference kept on purpose: an entry that can't be evaluated is _build validation skipped_ (exit 0) in `check` and a refusal in `build`. ⚠ Not a conformance **verdict** (§4). |
| **removed node definition** · `REMOVED_NODE_DEFINITIONS` · `removedNodeDefinitionSentence(id)` 🚧 (`@internal`) | **Built 2026-11-08 (lane s4-f-sdk, ★f-sdk-2).** A published node definition taken out of the SDK, with the one sentence that says what to do instead (`sdk/src/descriptors.ts`). The executor halts a run at such a node with `<nodeKey>: <sentence>`; `checkInstall` refuses a plugin that pins it (`E_UNKNOWN_TYPE`, the sentence as its `fix`); the app's library writes refuse an old pending change with it. "Removed", never "retired" (R1: a **retired** slot is greyed but kept). First entry: `core:outlet/attach-lorebook@1`. |

**The distinction that matters:** a **script** is one unit of code at a hook, edited in-app; a
**plugin** is a package with an install lifecycle. Both run in the **sandbox** and reach the
engine through the same **dispatch**. _Script_ versus _plugin_ is about delivery and
editability — **not** about who authored it.

## 13. Measurement

### Permanent

| Term                       | Means                                                                                       |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **corpus**                 | A named fixture set with one purpose.                                                       |
| **golden**                 | A recorded expected output. Derived by hand — there is no capture path.                     |
| **gate**                   | Fixtures that must hold; a break stops the work.                                            |
| **discriminating fixture** | One **proven** to move when its control moves. Anything else manufactures false confidence. |

**The rule:** a green suite is evidence only if the thing under test can move it. Perturb and
confirm before banking a pass. This outlives every particular corpus.

### Transitional — expires when 0.6 ships ⏳

These describe the 0.5 → 0.6 comparison and **should be deleted, not maintained,** once the
legacy path is gone. They are recorded here so they are read correctly _now_, not canonized.

| Term         | Means                                                                                                   |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **parity**   | Comparison against legacy 0.5 output. A **regression alarm for the legacy path**, never a quality gate. |
| **open**     | A known divergence expected to self-promote once fixed.                                                 |
| **departed** | A _deliberate_ divergence from 0.5, bounded to exactly what changed.                                    |

⚠ **Parity cannot validate anything new.** By construction it only says when we have stopped
matching the thing we are trying to beat. It is also blind to lore ranking entirely —
verified: zeroing every lore signal weight leaves all gate fixtures byte-identical. The
**measure** corpora exist because of that, and they are the ones that survive 0.6.

---

## 14. Knowledge _(designed, not built)_

| Term                 | Means                                                                                                           |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **clairvoyance**     | 0–100%: how much an entity's own knowledge constrains retrieval. 0 = fully constrained, 100 = presence ignored. |
| **presence**         | Where an entity is, or has been — an interval, not a point. ⚠ Half BUILT 2026-09-24 as a cast member's **presence** (§ lorebooks): same word, same idea. Retrieval does not read it yet. |
| **visibility grade** | How widely known a fact is, independent of who witnessed it.                                                    |
| **firsthand**        | Was there.                                                                                                      |
| **known**            | Aware of it, not present for it.                                                                                |
| **unfamiliar**       | Present, without the knowledge that usually accompanies being there.                                            |
| **universal**        | True regardless of perspective; a law of the world.                                                             |
| **timeline spine**   | The indexed table linking facts and associations to points in time.                                             |

⚠ **Two clocks, never conflated:** when a fact _became true_ and when someone _learned it_.

---

## 15. Templates and assembly

### Generic — any service

A context template is **not** LLM-specific. It is the root input of a service call, and a
service may be anything the app can talk to. **Do not define these terms in terms of prompts.**
A ComfyUI workflow is rendered with the template engine but is **not** a context template: it is a
**workflow** (§25, 2026-10-12), a provider document one dialect consumes, in its own table.

| Term                    | Means                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **context template**    | **The root document for a service call.** Service-agnostic and engine-agnostic: a prompt document for a chat model (never a ComfyUI **workflow**, which has its own table). It is the thing rendered, not the syntax it happens to be written in.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **template engine**     | What renders a context template into a service payload, named by a versioned id the template row carries as data. Core ships **Handlebars** (`core:template/handlebars@1`, the column default and what every seeded row is written in) and **Liquid** (`core:template/liquid@1`); an extension may register more. Neither core engine is _the_ definition, and neither may be taken over or released by a plugin.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **assembly**            | Turning selected content into a rendered payload.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **template variable**   | A named slot a template renders: `worldLore`, `characters`, `history`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **variable template**   | A declared _renderer_ for one variable (`core:var/world-lore@1`). ⚠ Not the same thing as a context template. **Accounted by variable, never by key** (owner rulings 2026-10-13): a key is the template's local name; the variable it resolved to (`ResolvedLayouts[key].variableId`) decides the rows offered, the default, the floor and the absence rule. A package may ship one for a variable it does not own (★4): offered, never the default (`isForeignPackageRow`). **UI and docs word: variable layout** (★1, 2026-11-10; PLAN-variable-layouts-2026-11-10): the Admin nav item, its pages and every doc say **Variable layouts**; code keeps its `variable template` identifiers (`pipeline_variable_templates`, `kind: 'variables'`, `VariableTemplate` names). Never bare _layout_ in the UI (that is a **session layout**, §9), except the template helper and filter `layout`, where no session layout can appear. A variable is written out by one layout for the whole pub (the **pub's layout**); a preset may state its own (**preset's variable layouts**); a context template may name one in place (`{{{layout characters "core/json@1"}}}`, Liquid `{{ characters | layout: "core/json@1" }}`). Resolution, in order: a layout a context template names → ⏳ **leftover pick** → the preset's variable layouts → the pub's layout → the pipeline author's pick for the step → the variable's default row (which may be the **automatic layout**) → no row; the run records which as `LayoutReason` (`template`, `leftover`, `preset`, `pub`, `authored`, `default`, `automatic`, `no-layout`). |
| 🚧 **layout reference** | **Built 2026-11-10** (PLAN-variable-layouts-2026-11-10). `<owner>/<slug>@<major>` (`core/titled-json@1`, `acme.dice/prose@1`, `mypub/prose@1`): how a context template, a preset and the SDK name one **variable template** row. Column `pipeline_variable_templates.reference`, unique with `variable_id`, so unique **within its variable**: two variables may each have a `core/json@1`. Fixed once saved. Core's rows and a package's are stamped at boot: core's fixed slugs `titled-json` · `json` · `titled` · `as-written` · `sentence` · `numeric` · `lines` · `bracket-tag`; an **automatic layout** `<owner>/json@<variable major>`; a package's from its seed's `slug`, else its template id's name. A person's row gets one when next saved, or when **Move into the template** needs one. Grammar: `parseVariableLayoutReference` · `VARIABLE_LAYOUT_SLUG` (SDK). ⚠ Not a **template id** (`core:template/…@1`, the row's app-wide identity). ⚠ Its old meaning, a step's stored layout pick (`config/world.ts`), is retired (§23). |
| 🚧 **pub's layout** | **Built 2026-11-10.** The **variable template** row a variable is written out by across the whole pub when the session's preset states none: `pipeline_variable_templates.pub_default` (at most one per variable, a partial unique index). None chosen means the package default. UI (Admin › Variable layouts): **In use**, **Use this**, _Chosen for this pub._, **Back to the default**. ⚠ Not a genre default and not a preset change: it sits below every preset and above the package default. |
| 🚧 **preset's variable layouts** | **Built 2026-11-10** (★2 option B). The layouts a preset states for its sessions, one per variable, as `{ [variableId]: layout reference }`: `session_presets.variable_layouts` for a pub preset, SDK `PresetDecl.variableLayouts` / `PresetInput.variableLayouts` (`@experimental`, checked by `presetVariableLayoutFindings`) for a declared one. Empty by default; nothing inherited or guessed. A reference no row goes by is skipped (the pub's layout renders) and named on the presets list (`danglingVariableLayouts`; status _Variable layout missing_). UI: the preset form's **Variable layouts** fieldset. ⚠ Not a **layout preset** nor a genre's `layouts` (session layouts, §9), and not a preset's `settings`. |
| ⏳ **leftover pick** | **Built 2026-11-10.** A per-step layout pick that data upgrade 0151 kept because removing it would have changed a prompt. Honoured at render before every choice but a layout a context template names; shown on its pipeline step with **Remove this pick** and **Move into the template**; written by nothing new (`config/leftoverPicks.ts`). Dropped at the 0.7 squash. |
| **template id**         | **Ruled 2026-09-17 (R19); built by U6.** The owner-namespaced identity a prompt, context or variable template row carries beside its storage `seed_key`: `core:template/adventure-planner@1`, `acme.rp:template/loot-table@1`. A spec's config default may name one (`{ templateId }`, resolved before `{ seedKey }`), an extension ships rows under `templates[]` beside `pipelines[]`, and `@N` is what governs breakage: a new major is a new row and the old id keeps resolving. ⚠ Not a **template variable** and not a **template engine**; it names the row, nothing about how it renders. |
| **allocation**          | What selection hands to rendering: a **decision** plus its rendered text and reason, ready to be placed. _(was: "context block" — it is not a block)_                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **artifact (of a run)** | A row a pipeline run produced — a message, file, variant or lore entry — recorded in `pipeline_run_artifacts`. Evidence of the run; it carries no FK to the thing itself.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **compiled payload**    | The finished request handed to an adapter.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **accepted engines**                       | **Built 2026-09-27.** A template slot's list of the **template engines** it will render (`SlotDecl.acceptedEngines`). ⚠ Was the slot's `engines`, retired under R1 (§23): a manifest's `engines` is version ranges.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **declared band**                          | **Built 2026-09-27 (typed templates P1/P2).** A **band** (§7) a node definition declares so a template can place it — `Descriptor.bands` — rendered under its own key at top level by any slot that declares `rendersBands`. Core has five (`CORE_BANDS`); a plugin declares its own (Twenty Questions' `secretEntry`, `briefing`). **One meaning per key is per template scope** (owner ruling 2026-10-13, ★1): two declarations may use one key for different variables, and only meeting in one document is refused (`bandsReaching` / `rendersAt`, law T1). A spec says what a step's key means with the node's own **`renders`** (§25, 2026-10-13).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **template scope** · **template fit**      | **Built 2026-09-27 (typed templates P3–P6).** A step's **template scope** is exactly what a template may read there, typed (`templateScopeAt`): static variables, the step's prompt fields, upstream port schemas, **declared bands**, `annex.<owner>.<key>` when Assemble's `annex` port is wired, and `state` from tracked slots. A template **fits** when it reads nothing else (`templateFit`, law **T1**; law **T2** keeps the `annex` port fed only by the annex view `'template'`). A misfit is refused at selection and publish and noticed on stored configs (§6 **misfit**). The **template check** (`@serene-pub/sdk/template-check`, `checkTemplateSource`) is the parser behind it, and the editor's _Variables available here_ tree draws the scope.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **object variable** · **automatic layout** | **Built 2026-09-27** (owner: "automatic and a requirement for objects"). An **object variable** is one with any object-valued root, decided from its declared `scope`, never a sample (`isObjectValued` · `isObjectVariable`, `entities/objectVariableLayouts.ts`): `object`, `record`, a list of those, the legacy `string[]` form — not `any`, not a primitive. Each gets an **automatic layout**: a **variable template** row named **JSON** (`OBJECT_LAYOUT_NAME`) rendering each root as minified JSON, so selecting it changes no prompt. A plugin's is projected at install and boot (`projectObjectVariableLayouts`, `writeTemplateSeed`, `registrySync.ts`) under the **template id** `<slug>:template/<variable name>-json@<variable major>` (`objectLayoutTemplateId`) when its manifest ships none. A core band's shipped layout keys are `SHIPPED_BAND_KEYS` (`variableLayouts.ts`). ⚠ _Layout_ here is the Variables slot's word for a variable template row, not a **session layout** (§9) — always say _automatic layout_ or _variable layout_. |

### Chat-shaped services only

These describe the LLM path specifically. They do **not** generalise — an image workflow has no
blocks and no seed line.

| Term                | Means                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **block**           | **One message**: `system`, `user`, or `assistant`. This is what a block _is_.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **prompt format**   | How blocks become wire text: Vicuna, ChatML, split-chat.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **macro**           | An author-facing substitution: `{{char}}`, `{{user}}`, `{{char:2}}`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **decorator**       | SillyTavern in-text markup, stripped on the way in.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **seed line**       | The trailing empty assistant block that invites continuation. Must be last. On the chat wire one that is only a label is not sent (B2, 2026-10-03; §25).                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **post-history**    | Instructions rendered _after_ the transcript, near the generation point.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **prompt block**    | One **section** of the prompt, named by the template variable that renders it — `characters`, `worldLore`, `history`. Always qualified: the bare word is a message.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **`blocks` param**  | The ordered pack of prompt blocks — which sections are in the prompt and in what order — declared on `core:task/assemble`. SillyTavern calls this a preset's _prompt list_; it is a **param inside the preset's pipeline configuration** (ruled 2026-09-10), never a session setting and never a table. _(say: `blocks` param, not "prompt-module pack")_ |
| **compiled prompt** | The chat-shaped compiled payload: one flat string, or a role-tagged message array.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

**The chain, in order.** A **context template** is the root document. A **template engine**
renders it, placing **allocations** and producing a **compiled payload** — for a chat service,
a sequence of **blocks**, which the **prompt format** turns into wire text. An **adapter**
ships it to the **service**. Each step names a different thing, and none of them is "the
template".

**Resolved collisions**

- ⚠ **`block`** → **a message**, in the chat sense. The codebase used the word for two
  things at **different granularities**, which is why it read as confused:
    - `ContextBlock` (`assemble.ts`) — **one retrieved item** with its verdict: source, id,
      content, tokens, `included`, `why`. → **`Allocation`**, landed. Assemble's out-port
      `blocks` landed with it, as **`allocations`**.
    - `systemBlock` / `userBlock` / `assistantBlock` — **one message**, formatted by
      `PromptBlockFormatter`. → keeps **block**.

    **A dozen allocations are rendered into the variables inside one block.** One is an item,
    the other is a container; they are not two kinds of the same thing. The old "context block"
    name also asserted a message shape that only chat-shaped services have.

    ⏳ **Two spellings of the old word survive the type rename**, both because they are
    seam vocabulary rather than ours: `AllocatedContext.blocks` and the compiled prompt's
    `meta.retrieval.blocks`. §25 carries them and says what holds them.

- ⚠ **A fourth sense: the `blocks` param.** One **section within** a prompt, named
  by the template variable that renders it. Recorded rather than renamed, because
  the word is the ruling's (2026-09-10) and the ledger below already carries
  `pipeline_blocks` as the third. In prose say **prompt block**; the bare word
  still means a message. What keeps the two apart in code is that they never meet:
  a prompt block is a **template variable name** in a config value, and a block is
  a **role** on a compiled message.
- · **`allocation`** → the **item**, as above. The ranker's token arithmetic
  (`allocateBudgets`, `scoreLedAllocation`, `groups[].allocated`) is **budget allocation**
  and deliberately keeps the word: it is a verb and an adjective over a divided resource,
  never a countable noun, so _an allocation_ has one referent. Checked before the rename
  rather than after (§24.2) — and in prose, say _budget allocation_ when the resource is
  meant, because that sense **is** countable in English even though the code never spells
  it as a noun.
- ⚠ **`seed`** → **three** meanings, all live: the **seed line** (chat), **seeding** (boot
  insertion of shipped rows), and the run's random **seed**. Never bare — say _seed line_,
  _seed rows_, _run seed_.
- ⚠ **`template`** → **context template** (the root document) vs **variable template** (one
  renderer) vs a prompt format's own template. Always qualified.
- · **`context`** → the assembled content. The token allowance is the **context window**; the
  node computing it is `contextBudget`.

## 16. Import and export

| Term                       | Means                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **card**                   | A character file: PNG/APNG with embedded JSON, bare JSON, or CHARX. **Never WebP as a container** — WebP is an asset _inside_ a card.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **book**                   | A lorebook file.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **wire name**              | The name a format uses on disk: `world`, `character`, `history`, and from **format 2** `location` and `item` (`ENTRY_EXPORT_KEY`, total over the core entry types). ⚠ **Never write an internal type id into a file.** |
| **format version** (lorebook file) | `extensions.serenepub.formatVersion` — **2** since places and items travel, stats travel (`serenepub.stats`) and the per-entry facts ride in the bag (plan A26, E-8). A file without it is format 1; the importer reads both on one path (`lorebookFileFormatOf`). The marker is not content: the import's unchanged-vs-conflict comparison leaves it out, and an overwrite from a format-1 file counts what that format cannot carry (**overwrite losses** `stats` · `places` · `items`). |
| **export profile**         | Which format a lorebook export writes (`LorebookExportProfile`): **`native`** (format 2 and every wire name; card export and the import's comparison) or **`0.5-compat`** (format 1: no marker, no stats, only the three wire names a Serene Pub 0.5 reader knows, `SERENE_PUB_0_5_EXPORT_KEYS`, a place or an item written as world lore with world lore's fields; nothing ships it while export is paused). ⚠ Qualified: bare _profile_ is an image-generation profile and a docs profile. ⚠ Never _ST_ here: _ST_ is SillyTavern everywhere else, and SillyTavern ignores `entryType`. |
| **extensions bag**         | A foreign format's `extensions` object, stored verbatim as provenance.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **V3 card** (what an exported card carries) | **Built 2026-10-11** (A.6, B.5, S4). Three layers, each readable without the next: **prose** — `description` / `personality` as the compiled cache (what every other tool reads); **`character_book`** — one entry per keyword **stroke** (`strokeBookEntries`: `keys`, `name` = label or slug, `enabled`, not `constant`, `use_regex` from the match mode), strokes first, then any lorebook chosen for export (`mergeStrokeBook`, ids renumbered); **`extensions.serenepub.{strokes,dowry}`** — the full stroke list verbatim and the **dowry** (§9), so Serene Pub ↔ Serene Pub is lossless. ⏸ The strokes layer is paused (2026-10-11, see **stroke** §8): while paused an export carries no `serenepub.strokes` and no stroke entries in `character_book`, and a plain `character_book` imports as a lorebook, not strokes; `serenepub.dowry` stays live. Import reads back down the same layers (`planCardImport`): `serenepub.strokes` wins; else a **plain book** (§8) becomes strokes; else the prose as written. Foreign `extensions` are stored on `characters.extensions` and written back on export with Serene Pub's keys overlaid (`exportedExtensions`; cap `CARD_EXTENSIONS_MAX_BYTES`, 256 KiB). The import reply's **`summary?: string[]`** (`ImportCard` · `ImportResolve` · `ImportFromLibrary`) carries one sentence per thing that did not arrive as written — strokes made from a book, a book kept as a lorebook and why, a re-owned or renamed declaration, a sheet not on this install, foreign data over the cap; shown in the central import toast (`cardImportedToast.ts`). |
| **clamp**                  | Coercing a foreign value into our range rather than rejecting it — a foreign `priority: 7` must still import.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **repair**                 | A one-off correction of already-imported rows, distinct from fixing the importer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **paused** (export)        | ⏳ Lorebook export is disabled until the format settles (owner ruling 1, 2026-09-28): the action stays visible and greyed with one sentence, `LOREBOOK_EXPORT_PAUSED` (`shared/lorebooks/exportPaused.ts`), and `lorebooks:export` refuses with the same one. Import is unaffected: SillyTavern files and **Serene Pub 0.5** exports (whose separate personas list lands as characters flagged `is_persona`). |
| **duplicate** (a lorebook) | An **exact copy**, row for row in one transaction (owner ruling 2, 2026-09-28; `duplicateLorebookRows`, `server/utils/lorebookDuplicate.ts`): every line, entry, amendment, presence, link, scene, tag and the calendar and clock, every id remapped; cards are shared, not copied. ⚠ Never an export→import. A scene's session capture and merge-undo logs stay with the original.                          |
| **held import**            | The file an import leaves on the server while the person decides (lorebooks plan S4; `server/imports/heldImports.ts`: `holdImport`, `takeHeldImport`, `HELD_IMPORT_LIMITS`, `HELD_IMPORT_GONE`): a **conflict**'s file, or a created card's embedded book waiting on the _Import the lorebook?_ dialog (**`HeldCardBook`**, the card reply's `book`). The conflict reply of `characters:importCard` / `lorebooks:import` carries its **`heldImportId`**, never the file, and the `…:importResolve` choice names it; `lorebooks:import` takes a held card book as `heldImportId` in place of `lorebookJson`. Owner-scoped (anyone else's id reads as _no longer waiting_), taken once, in memory only: each person's newest 2, for 15 minutes, 256 MB in all — past that the person holding the most gives way first. ⚠ Not the SillyTavern folder import's staging directory (`sockets/import.ts`), which is an admin's many-file upload for a multi-step import. |

**The standing rule:** _import carries intent; the pipeline decides semantics._ Compatibility
lives at the boundary; the engine is free to rank differently.

⚠ **Anything SillyTavern writes unconditionally is meaningless until proven otherwise** —
`use_regex: true`, `order: 100`, `selectiveLogic: 0` are all stamped on every entry.
