## 17. Graph

| Term             | Means                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **graph node**   | A narrative entity in the relationship graph. ⚠ Always qualified — a **node** unqualified is a _pipeline_ node.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **relationship** | A row of `narrative_relationships` joining two things in one book — two cast members, a cast member and an entry, or two entries — read from→to by its **relationship type**. A **reverse relationship type** makes it read, and between places walk, from the far end too. It may carry a **name** (column `title`, `name` on the wire, exactly as an entry's) and a description. **One row per way** (2026-09-29, plan B1): with an entry at either end, the writers refuse a second row that says what one already says — the same words read from the same end, on the same line, at the same date, with the same name, case aside (`findLinkedThatWay`, _These two are already linked that way._); the partial unique index `narrative_relationships_entry_pair_uq` holds the exact entry↔entry duplicate, and `narrative_relationships_entry_self_check` refuses an entry linked to itself. ⚠ The UI verb is _link_ (§22 **link** · **unlink**). ⚠ A place relationship is edited in place (its id is stable); a cast tie changes by a new dated row. |
| **perspective**  | One participant's view of a relationship. 🚧 Where a **tie** (§24) is two-sided, each person's held **tie side** reads onto their own perspective row. |
| **rule-fed row** 🚧 | A relationship whose words a held tie side writes (§24 **tie**, T2–T4): `rules_run_id` names the run that last wrote it (migration 0121); its fed words are the rules' (_from the rules_, refused when retyped by hand), written in place — never a new dated **tie version** — and how it changed is read from its runs' receipts (`tieHistory`). Drawing a cast tie makes the held sides of every session reading the book; deleting the row retires them; never the reverse. A book the session may not write is overlaid by the session's notes' own copy, which the session reads in the book row's place. |
| **reverse relationship type** | `narrative_relationships.reverse_relationship_type` (wire `reverseRelationshipType`; UI **Both ways** · _From there it…_ in `RelationshipFields`, B3; SDK `reverseLinkType` — `link-lore-entries@1`'s param, `LoreLinkInput` and `LoreLinkRow`, B2; empty is one way): the relationship type read from the `to` end — "leads south to" beside "leads north to". NULL is one way; a symmetric wording repeats itself (`connects to` / `connects to`). ⚠ Never on a cast↔cast row (`narrative_relationships_reverse_check`; the writers drop it): a cast tie's other side is its own **perspective** row. Not an inverse looked up in a vocabulary — each row states its own. |
| **lore link** | The SDK-side name for a **relationship** with an entry at either end: `core:outlet/link-lore-entries@1`, `lore-link-created@1`, `create-lore-entry@1`'s `links` (each a `LoreLinkInput`: `to`, `linkType`, `reverseLinkType`, `name`, `description`), `lorebook-entries@1`'s `withLinks` (each row's `links`, `LoreLinkRow[]`, said from that row: `loreLinkRowsOf`), the host's `writeLoreLink` and run-artifact kind `lore_link`. ⚠ **Idempotent** (B2), **as the session reads** (review round): a write that finds the link on the session's reading — its line and the lines it inherits, at its moment — saying everything asked (`linksOnReadingThatWay`) answers with that row's id and its own `from`, records no `lore_link` artifact and reports `written: false` — the run did not make it. A row that says only part of it, or no longer stands (resolved, broken, secret), is refused: _These two are already linked that way._ and why. An R5 reconciliation at the host boundary: the SDK says _lore link_, the table and the app say _relationship_. ⚠ Not §7 **link** (a resolved mention → entry or character). Always qualified in prose; the bare `links` port name is ⏳. |
| **cast-wide read** (of the narrative graph) · **`castRelationships`** | 🚧 **Built 2026-09-29 (genre plan F6(a)).** The graph read with **nobody speaking**: `core:query/relationship-search@1` under a scope whose `currentCharacterId` is null (an Adventure turn is the narrator's entry; its planner and narrator are nobody's voice) answers every relationship a cast member holds that is **not their secret**, one candidate each in the lane **`castRelationships`** (`GraphRelationshipLane`; `buildCastRelationshipRows`, `utils/graphContextFormatter.ts`; branched in `host.ts`'s `graph_relationships` read) — headed by its holder (`name`), naming the other end (`counterpart`). ⚠ Secrets withheld (`CAST_WIDE_VISIBILITY` = acknowledged · public, layer 2's rule): nobody's voice is not the holder's, and the planner's beats and the narrator's prose reach the player (review 2026-09-29; the earshot rule, fail closed until the owner rules). `build-planner-context@1` and `build-scene-context@1` take the ranker's allocation on the in-port **`castRelationships`** and render `{{castRelationships}}` (JSON: holder → other → entries, rank order; `castRelationshipsSection`, `prompt/rankedRelationships.ts`). ⚠ Not a **perspective** (one participant's view) but every member's at once, and not the speaker's `relationshipsPerspectives`. No voice declares the port. ⚠ Not the lorebook's **Cast** section or the **Views** sheet — a _read_, never a view. |
| **tie version**  | One row of a tie between two cast members at one date — its history entry, or none (undated). A tie is the same `from`, `to` and relationship type; its versions at different dates are its history, and every one a line has reached is read. Where a line holds its own version at a date an ancestor also holds one, the line's is read there (`nearestTieVersions`), as a nearer line's amendment wins; the ancestor's row is unchanged for every other line. A graph build that changes an inherited version writes the line's own at that date. ⚠ Not a **state version** or a **saved version**. |
| **proposal**     | A suggested graph change, awaiting review.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **review gate**  | The surface where a proposal is accepted or rejected. Nothing is auto-applied.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **cap pause**    | **Built 2026-09-23 (E1c).** A run tree held at a cycle cap for the session owner: the next run a session event would dispatch past `MAX_RUN_DEPTH` or `MAX_RUN_DESCENDANTS` parks (`runtime/capPause.ts`: `parkAtCap`, `resolveCapPause`, `CapPauseView`; sockets `pipelines:capPauses` · `pipelines:resolveCapPause` · pushes `pipelines:capPauseRequested` / `pipelines:capPauseClosed`; `CapPauseDialog.svelte`, UI _Keep going?_ · **Continue** · **Stop here**). **One per run tree**: every run of the tree a cap refuses before the owner answers waits on the same pause (`CapPauseView.waiting`). Continue grants the tree one more **window** of each cap (`grantWindow`, `capsOf`) and runs exactly the pipeline named (`expectSpec` on `dispatchSessionEvent`); Stop here receipts each parked run `cancelled`. In memory, like review parking. ⚠ Not a **review gate** — nothing is edited and the run has not started. ⚠ Never a _chain_ pause: _chain_ is the script, gather and config word. |
| **temp id**      | A placeholder for an entity a run invented (`new_3`), resolved only on apply.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

**Resolved collisions**

- ⚠ **`node`** → a **pipeline** node. The graph's are **graph nodes**, always qualified. These
  appear in the same retrieval paths, since graph content is a retrieval source.

## 18. Media

| Term           | Means                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **media**      | Any stored binary: image, audio, document.                                                                                  |
| **asset**      | A media item referenced by something else.                                                                                  |
| **thumbnail**  | A derived, smaller rendition.                                                                                               |
| **attachment** | A file on a message — a `core:image` / `core:file` **message part** (`MessagePartsView`, `Paperclip`), whether a person attached it or a pipeline posted it. ⚠ Not a lorebook reading (§23 _Attach_, retired), not a spec **origin** (that is _foreign_, 2026-10-02). |
| **tray** · **tray item** 🚧 | A file uploaded into a session's composer and not yet sent (`tray_items`); a person's tray items for one session are their tray. Expires unsent after 24 h; its file is deleted then only if the upload created it (`fresh`) and nothing references it. ⚠ Not a held import (§16), not the downloads tray (§10). |
| **attachment readers** · **reading call** 🚧 | What a session's reply can read, per **attachment kind** (`image` · `text` · `pdf`): each **reading call** (a model call of the reply handed a message's attachments) says what it reads and what it gets as a placeholder (`[image: cat.png]`, D3); a kind may be attached when at least one call reads it (D1). `attachmentReaders` (`attachments/readers.ts`), socket `attachments:readers`; the composer shows it in the **What can be attached** dialog (More ⋮; next-pass note 41 — the always-visible readers line is gone). ⚠ _Readers_ never bare (R3). Since phase 4 a reading call is the step a **place attachments** step's `connection` slot names (below). |
| **place attachments** (step) · **media lookback** · **text file budget** 🚧 | `core:task/place-attachments@1` (node key **`attached`**, Adventure's narrator `sceneAttached`): gives each transcript line an `attachments` string the template renders after its text (`{{{attachments}}}`) — a **media marker** for an image or PDF the call reads within the **media lookback** (`mediaLookback`, messages, default 10), a text file inlined under its name and cut to the **text file budget** (`textFileTokens`, default 4000) with a stated note, a placeholder for the rest. Judged on its `connection` slot's `metadata.reads` (`ConnectionReadsV1`, from `pairReads` in `world.ts`; `readsByModel` per model). Pure half `attachments/placement.ts` `placeAttachments`. ⚠ The node key is not **place** (a location entry, §9) nor the room rule's `place` step. |
| **media marker** 🚧 | `<@media:{uuid}>` — the in-band mark placement writes so a file reaches its own line's turn; `parseSplitChatPrompt` lifts it onto that message's `attachments`, and every other rendered value is neutralised (`MEDIA_MARKER_PATTERN`, `neutralizeMediaMarkers`, `neutralizeRenderScope`, `liftMediaMarkers`, `flattenMediaMarkers` → `[attachment]` in a flat render; `shared/utils/mediaMarkers.ts`). The role marker's twin (`ROLE_MARKER_PATTERN`). |
| **history attachments** 🚧 | `core:query/history-attachments@1`: a transcript's files by message id, active revision, part order — `core:shape/media-by-message@1` of **`HistoryAttachmentV1`** (a `MediaRef` + **`attachmentKind`** `image\|text\|pdf\|null`, a text file's `body` / `bodyTruncated`, param `textFileBytes`). Host read `history_attachments` (`attachments/history.ts`), the run's own session only. |

| **fitted** (variant) 🚧 | The whole picture, long edge ≤ 1568 px, uncropped — a single-image preview and a model payload's size (`MediaVariant.FITTED`, `?v=fitted`, `makeFitted`). Reduced fidelity, cullable, derived on first request. ⚠ Not a thumbnail (a thumbnail is a square crop). |
| **media strip** 🚧 | A message's images and files as square tiles **below its card**, never inside it (`MessageMediaStrip`, parts `messages.media-*`; its own cell of `messages.message` after the content): its `core:image` / `core:file` parts, every image a square tile, every file a **file tile**. ⚠ Not the character gallery, not a block tree's image (`messages.block-image`). |
| **lightbox** | The page's full-size image viewer. The **media lightbox** (`MediaLightbox`, answering `view-image`) pages through a message's images and has an **Info** pane (`GET /media/{id}/info`, `MediaInfoV1`). ⚠ Not the character gallery's viewer (`EntityGalleryViewModal`). |
| **provenance** | Where a media item came from — generated, uploaded, imported. ⚠ Same word as entry provenance, same meaning, deliberately. |
| **sprite** 🚧             | One labelled image a card can show — an emotion, an outfit, a pose (DESIGN-sprites, 2026-09-24). A **row** (`sprites`), not a file: its image is the `files` row it points at, a **role** like the avatar (`file_id`, `ON DELETE SET NULL`). Belongs to a **card**, or to a **cast member** as its own (`sprite_sets.cast_member_id`; owner 2026-11-05, own over card). The sprites module's writers take 🚧 `SpriteOwner` (`{characterId}|{castMemberId}`; a bare number is a card id). A member's sprite file has its book as provenance. 🚧 `copySpriteSets(tx, from, to, fileFor)` (`sprites/index.ts`; lane s4-cp, 2026-11-08) copies one owner's sets onto another's — a target that already holds a set with an image gets nothing, so a second call is a no-op; `copySpriteSetsToMember` wraps it, and **Copy to my characters** from a member uses it. The `characters:*` sprite sockets (`sockets/sprites.ts`: list, set create/update/delete, sprite upload/update/delete/reorder, standard sprites, `characters:testSprite`) take the owner as `{characterId}` **or** `{castMemberId}` (whoever may edit the member's book, `canEditCastMember`, may change a member's sprites); since lane s4-sdk2 (★7, 2026-11-08) **Sprite set fill**, **Re-express from neutral** and **Portrait** take `{castMemberId}` too — the pictures are the book owner's files with the book as provenance, `core:outlet/attach-sprite@1` / `offer-media@1` write to the member's own sets and gallery, and `core:event/sprites-attached@1` / `media-offered@1` payloads carry 🚧 `castMemberId`; `images:drawingSheet` takes 🚧 `castMemberId` (lane s4-tidy) so a member's Sprites tab can offer re-express; `SpritesTab` takes `owner: {characterId} \| {castMemberId}` and is mounted on the cast member page. 🚧 `spriteChoicesFor` takes `castMemberId` beside `characterId` (a card-less seat's speaker; offers the member's own sets only, lane s4-seat). ⚠ Not the **avatar** (a card's one identity image), not a CSS sprite sheet, and not _expression_ — that word is a Liquid formula (R11). |
| **sprite label**          | A sprite's name as the card authored it — `joy`, `swimsuit`, `sleeping` — normalised (trimmed, case-folded), never mapped onto a fixed vocabulary. Several sprites under one label are **variants**. R3: never bare _label_. The editor's "standard set" is go_emotions' 28, a starter only.                                                                                                                                          |
| **sprite set**            | A named group of a card's sprites — an outfit, an age, a form (SillyTavern: _sprite folder override_). Exactly one per card is the **default set**. A cast member chooses one BY NAME (`lorebook_bindings.sprite_set`, amendable); a session may override it for itself (`core:slot/sprite-set@1`). UI label **Sprite set**. A cast member's own sets are its art when any holds an image; a card's are read only otherwise. |
| **member gallery** · `cast_member_files` 🚧 | **Built 2026-11-08 (★2, lane s4-cl).** A cast member's own pictures: table `cast_member_files` (member `ON DELETE cascade`, file `ON DELETE cascade`, `position`, unique per member and file; migration 0147). The file is a **role**, never provenance. Read with `mediaFor(db, { castMemberId })`, written only by 🚧 `addToMemberGallery` (`media/index.ts`; P2). A picture moving to another user's book goes through 🚧 `fileForOwner`: the same row for the same user, otherwise the same bytes as the new owner's row (never through tmp); unreadable bytes stay shared. Whoever can read the member's book, or is in a session reading it or seating the member, can open them (`canReadCastMember`); `characters:listGallery`, `characters:uploadGalleryImage` and `characters:reorderGallery` take `{castMemberId}` beside `{characterId}` (list by the read rule, upload, reorder and delete by the edit rule, `canEditCastMember`; a member upload is the book owner's file, with the book as provenance, via `addToMemberGallery`; delete via 🚧 `removeFromMemberGallery` — unlinks, and deletes the file only when nothing else uses it — and `characters:deleteGalleryImage {castMemberId}`, ★cp-del, lane s4-follow-a 2026-11-09; the gallery and sprite replies are scoped `member:<id>` in `SCOPED_EVENTS`, ★cp-scope-1); the cast member page draws it in its **Gallery** tab (lane s4-tidy, ★sdk2-1 under ★7: 🚧 `EntityGalleryTab` `owner: {characterId} \| {castMemberId}`; an editor can upload, **Generate portrait**, reorder and **Delete**; a member's gallery has no **Set as avatar** or **Use as likeness image**); a seated member's gallery pictures are cast images for a backdrop. The SDK request `character-images` takes 🚧 `castMemberId` beside `characterId` (exactly one; page dep 🚧 `MemberGalleryRead` / `readMemberGallery`), so **Backdrop** and **Scene Portraits** list a card-less member's own pictures, each keeping its galleries by the member's `ref` (an opaque key, never parsed). ⚠ Not the card's gallery (`files.character_id`), not **lorebook-owned media** (`files.lorebook_id`). Replaces `files.cast_member_id` (0146–0147, never written). |
| **shown sprite** | The `{ set, label, source }` recorded on one line's active swipe (`metadata.sprite`, `swipes.spriteHistory[]`). `source` is `picker` or `person`; a picker never overwrites a person's. |
| **current sprite** | A cast member's shown sprite on their newest visible line, in the session's override set if there is one. 🚧 Amended 2026-11-11: when the page has a **Dialogue box**, it is the sprite as of the line the box shows (`show-line`), not the newest. **Derived, never stored** — published as `sprites.<castKey>` for enabled-when. |
| **sprite picker** | The rebindable node that chooses a line's sprite label — `core:oracle/pick-sprite@1`, all in one since 2026-10-05: handed the line's `text`, its `speaker` and the session `scope` by the reply spec, it reads what the speaker can show, embeds through the active embedding connection, and picks. Node key `spritePick` on each reply spec. Every picker publishes `core:shape/sprite-pick@1` on `main`. |
| _emotion_ (card boundary) | The CCv3 asset type (`emotion`, SillyTavern's `expression`) and a classifier's output. **Only at the boundary** (R5): inside Serene Pub it is a sprite with a sprite label.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **cut-out** · `cutOut` (param) 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-12 (I1, I4).** A **cut-out** is a picture after its background was removed (`core:task/cut-out@1`, BiRefNet-lite under modality `matting`, downloaded once); `cutOut` is the image oracle's request for one (_Off_ · _Transparent when possible_ · _Transparent from the model_). ⚠ Not _transparent_ bare (the drawing-sheet flag) and not _background removal_ as a type name (R4). §25. |
| **series** · **series key** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-12 (I2).** The pictures one image step is asked for, one item per picture (`core:shape/image-series@1`); each picture out carries the **series key** it was drawn for. The host's packing decides the calls. ⚠ Not a **batch** (the sampling knob: N pictures of one prompt); never bare _key_. §25. |
| **references** (port) 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-12 (I1).** The image oracle's in-port of pictures the output should resemble (a likeness image, say); param `preferred` · `required`. ⚠ Not `init` (the starting canvas) and not `mask`. §25. |
| **Portrait** · **proofs** · **offer-media** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-12 (I8).** **Portrait** is the picture pipeline `core:spec/character-portrait` (UI **Generate portrait**, a **card action**; review on by default); **proofs** (`core:task/build-proofs@1`) are its N identical series items; **`core:outlet/offer-media@1`** puts each picture in the card's gallery (event `media-offered`). ⚠ Not the **Scene Portraits** widget, not `orientation: portrait`; _proofs_ is not a retrieval **candidate** (§7); offer-media never sets the avatar or the likeness image. §25. |
| **Sprite set fill** · **sprite label phrases** · **attach-sprite** · **contact sheet** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-12 (I5).** **Sprite set fill** is the picture pipeline `core:spec/sprite-set-fill` (UI **Fill empty sprites**, display _Fill sprites_, a **card action**); **sprite label phrases** is its prompt row of `label: phrase` lines; **`core:outlet/attach-sprite@1`** files each keyed picture under its **sprite label** as a new sprite or variant (event `sprites-attached`); the **contact sheet** is the Sprites tab's tile-per-label view of one fill (**Keep** · **Redo** · **Redo all**). ⚠ A phrase is not a sprite label (R5); attach-sprite is not `show-sprite`; the contact sheet is not the **Album** widget. §25. |
| **lorebook-owned media** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-13 (PLAN-cast-retold-fields, ruling 3).** A `files` row whose provenance is a lorebook (`files.lorebook_id`, no FK, like the other provenance columns), uploaded for a cast member's **face** (§8) with `lorebooks:uploadMemberFace`, which only STORES it, or as the book's **cover image** (§8); the member wears it once a save picks it. Listed as **This book's pictures** (`lorebooks:listMemberFaces`). Belongs to the book, not to a card: it is never in the card's gallery. ⚠ Files are one row per user and bytes, so an upload may re-use a row stamped otherwise; who may see a face follows the members that wear it, not the stamp. ⚠ Not an **asset** of the card, not an **attachment**. |
| **avatar** (of an account) 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-21.** The picture an account is drawn with — the rail, the Users view, sharing, conversations: `users.avatar_media_id` (`avatarMediaId`, FK `files.id`, `SET NULL`, migration 0111), a personal file (bucket `avatars`, no entity parent) set or cleared by **`users:current:updateAvatar`** `{ avatarFile: Buffer \| null }` (`handleUserAvatarUpload`). Round, the name's initial when none. Any signed-in person may see it (`canViewMedia`), as they see the name; never offered as a background. ⚠ Not a **persona**'s avatar — a persona is a character the user voices and wears its own; the word is the same because the meaning is (an identity's one picture, R1). |
| **avatar picker** · `AvatarPicker` | The one control that chooses an identity picture — a character's avatar, an account's, a lorebook's cover image (`components/media/AvatarPicker.svelte`): the tile is the upload control (click, drop), the crop editor opens before anything uploads, the crop of a new file is held until its save answers (`commitPendingFrame`). UI **Adjust crop** · **Remove image**. ⚠ Not the **face** picker (a cast member's, which picks from galleries), not the gallery. |

## 19. Schema and migrations

| Term                      | Means                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **baseline**              | `0095_schema_0_6_0` — the one generated migration from 0.5.3's schema to 0.6's, which replaced the squashed pre-release chain (2026-10-01). The **migration chain** around it: `0000`–`0093` are 0.5.3's, byte-identical forever (the ledger repair matches them by hash); `0094_entry_keys_text` (a SQL function a generated column needs) and `0096_link_description_not_null` (a `--custom` slot: 0.5.3's `0033` created that column nullable while every snapshot says `NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`, a gap generation cannot see) are hand-written, and so are `0098_retire_session_sampling_column` and `0099_rename_widget_settings_instance_id` (`--custom` slots that carry a pr-4 install’s data across); everything else is generated. Squashed again 2026-10-03 for 0.6.0-pr-1 — the pre-squash `0095`–`0111` are archived in `~/.claude/plans/ARCHIVE-drizzle-migrations-0094-0111-pr1.tar.gz` — and 2026-10-13 for 0.6.0-pr-5: the unreleased `0098`–`0117` became those two slots and the generated `0100_schema_0_6_0_pr_5`, archived in `~/.claude/plans/ARCHIVE-drizzle-migrations-0098-0117-pr5.tar.gz`. |
| **journal**               | `drizzle/meta/_journal.json` — the ordered list of applied migrations.                                                         |
| **snapshot**              | `drizzle/meta/*_snapshot.json` — what generation diffs against. **The source of truth for generation.**                        |
| **defaults sync**         | The idempotent boot step that seeds and reconciles shipped rows. **Anything that must persist goes here, not in a migration.** |
| **data upgrade**          | A content transformation keyed to a migration, run in its transaction (`db/dataUpgrades/`). The one there is the 0.5.3 → 0.6 **attic** stash.                                    |
| **attic**                 | The `attic_0_5_3` schema a 0.5.3 database's rows wait in while the 0.6 schema is built on empty tables (`$lib/server/attic`). Its presence is the one "upgrade pending" signal; a fresh install never has one. Not a **backup** (the pre-migration tarball) and not `public`. |
| **attic restore**         | The `attic` startup task: every attic row back in `public` in the 0.6 shape, in one transaction, proven by a reconciliation against the stash's own counts (`restore.ts`). Critical — a failure stops the boot and leaves the attic. |
| **attic wiring**          | The tail of the `pipelines` task: the 0.5.3 configurations (read from the attic by `migrateLegacy` / `migrateContextTemplates`) and turn orders brought across, proven, and the attic dropped (`finish.ts`). |
| **ledger splice**         | ⏳ The one-time carry of a development database migrated by the pre-squash 0.6 chain (`0094`–`0111`, before 2026-10-03) onto the squashed one: a complete pre-squash ledger is rewritten to the squashed chain's rows (the schemas are identical); a prefix has its missing pre-squash files replayed first from byte-exact copies (`db/ledgerSplice.ts`, `db/ledgerSpliceChain.ts`); anything else is refused before any write. Not the **ledger repair** (stamps) and not the **ledger prune** (0.5.3's stray rows). Expires once no pre-squash dev database is left — delete both files then. |
| **ledger prune**          | The one deletion from the migrations ledger: rows whose hash matches no shipped migration file, removed inside the attic stash's transaction — so once, by a 0.5.3 database, never by a fresh pub or one already on 0.6 (`pruneUnshippedLedgerRows`). Not the **ledger repair**, which corrects a row's `created_at` and only warns about a row it cannot match. |
| **upgrade note**          | One thing the upgrade changed in somebody's data or could not carry, written once as an admin logbook record of object type `data-upgrade` (its topic is the object id). Not a config **notice** (a standing condition) and not a **notification** (`core:notification/data-upgrade-done@1` is the one that announces them). |
| **constraint projection** | Boot-time creation of CHECK constraints and indexes from declared entry types.                                                 |

⚠ A migration numbered at or below the highest already applied is **silently skipped** — and
**tests cannot catch this**, because a fresh test database short-circuits the ordering check.

## 20. Verbs

Verbs collide as readily as nouns.

| Verb          | Means                                                                                                   |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **retrieve**  | Find candidates. Never "search" — that means the semantic mechanism specifically.                       |
| **admit**     | Let a candidate be _considered_.                                                                        |
| **score**     | Assign a number.                                                                                        |
| **rank**      | Order by score.                                                                                         |
| **select**    | Choose within a budget, producing decisions.                                                            |
| **assemble**  | Turn decisions into a prompt.                                                                           |
| **render**    | Turn one thing into its display or wire form.                                                           |
| **declare**   | Author a type's shape in the SDK.                                                                       |
| **project**   | Turn declarations into database objects. ⚠ **Not** row→candidate mapping — that is **toCandidate**.    |
| **reconcile** | Align stored values with current declarations.                                                          |
| **cull**      | Remove a declared address and its stored values.                                                        |
| **promote**   | Move queued work to the front because a query needs it. Also: move a fixture from `open` into the gate. |
| **sweep**     | A lane's periodic scan for work.                                                                        |
| **seed**      | Insert shipped rows at boot.                                                                            |
| **degrade**   | Contribute zero with a receipt line. **Never** halt, throw, or exclude.                                 |
| **start from** | Copy another row's content in as the starting point of a new thing, or of this one; the result is its own and keeps no link, so a later change to the source reaches nothing. Already the app's word for it (Admin → Sampling _New_, a lorebook's calendar, a character's emotion set); the layout editor's **Start from** (§9) is the same verb, and **Start again from** repeats it from the same row. ⚠ Not _make a copy_ / _clone_ (a new row whose content is a copy), and never said of a live reference. |

⚠ **`promote`** carries two senses — queue priority and fixture status. Both are established
and neither is likely to be confused in context, but say which if ambiguous.

## 21. Abbreviations

Acceptable unexpanded in code and casual speech: **RAG**, **NER**, **BM25**, **idf**, **TTL**,
**LLM**, **FK**, **PK**, **UI**.

Expand on first use in user-facing documentation. **Never** invent new ones — `SP` for Serene
Pub is acceptable internally and must not appear in the UI.

## 22. Icons

An icon is a term's pictogram, and it is vocabulary. A person who meets `BookMarked` in the
nav, on a session's "View lorebook" button and beside a summarization target learns the word
once; a person who meets three different books learns nothing. So icons obey the rules the
words do, and the associations below are canon in the same sense — **where a screen draws a
term with a different icon, the screen is wrong.**

The library is `@lucide/svelte`, imported as `import * as Icons from "@lucide/svelte"` and
drawn as `<Icons.BookMarked />`. An icon is named by its **export name** — `BookMarked`,
`MessageSquareText` — in prose, in code and in declared data alike. The two non-lucide marks
are vendor logos (the Ollama and KoboldCPP managers), and a vendor's own mark is the one
place a logo is the right icon.

**I1 — One icon, one term (R1 for pictograms).** A collision is dangerous exactly when the two
terms can share a screen. `Network` meaning _embeddings_ in the connections list and _graph_
among the lorebook's lenses was the collision; `Globe` meaning _world lore_ on a door and
_website_ on an About link is not, and is tolerated.

**I2 — The declared source wins.** Where an icon is declared as data — the navigations, the
connection sections, the lorebook doors and lenses, a widget manifest — that declaration is
the canon, and an inline `<Icons.X>` that disagrees is the one that changes. It is R1's
"load-bearing use stays": a nav entry is seen on every screen, a stray empty-state icon on one.

**I3 — Kind icons are borrowed, never redrawn.** A modality, a sampling shape and a defaults
group each show the icon of the **output kind** they produce; none has an icon of its own.
That is what lets the Embeddings section, the **indexed** mark on an entry (§11) and the
Embeddings defaults group read as one thing — and it is why _add icons for the modalities_
was a two-line change and not a design exercise.

**I4 — Two spellings on the wire, one in the app.** Declared data names an icon as a string.
App-side tables and widget manifests use the export name verbatim (`'HeartPulse'`); the SDK's
trigger and action declarations use kebab-case (`"book-open-text"`, `"user-round"`) and
the `sp-icon` host element (`client/components/hostElements/SpIcon.svelte`, the one resolver since C7 — `actionIcon()` retired with the native conversation) PascalCases it at the seam; an export name passes through unchanged and an unknown name draws nothing (core's conversation falls back to `play` itself). R5 — translate, never
merge — but the kebab spelling is the older of the two and is not to spread: a new
declaration writes the export name.

### Kinds and modalities

The output kinds are the SDK's `IO_KINDS`. Each has one icon; everything below borrows it.

| Output kind | Icon           | Borrowed by                                                                                                                   |
| ----------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `text`      | `Type`         | **text-gen** · the `text` sampling shape · the Text defaults group · the static text card in a context template               |
| `image`     | `Image`        | **image-gen** · the `image` sampling shape · the Images defaults group · one image asset (the media _collection_ is `Images`) |
| `audio`     | `AudioLines`   | **tts** 🚧 · the Speech and audio defaults group                                                                              |
| `video`     | `Clapperboard` | the Video defaults group                                                                                                      |
| `document`  | `FileText`     | the Documents defaults group · a document asset · export-as-JSON                                                              |
| `embedding` | `Zap`          | **embeddings** · the **indexed** mark on an entry (**needs re-indexing** is `RefreshCw`) · the Embeddings defaults group            |
| `entities`  | `ScanText`     | **ner** · the NER lane panel · the Named entities defaults group                                                              |

| Modality       | Icon         |                                                                                                                |
| -------------- | ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **text-gen**   | `Type`       |                                                                                                                |
| **image-gen**  | `Image`      |                                                                                                                |
| **embeddings** | `Zap`        | ⚠ Was `Network` — the one modality that had drawn its own, and it drew the graph's. Landed with this section. |
| **ner**        | `ScanText`   |                                                                                                                |
| **tts** 🚧     | `AudioLines` | Named in §10, no section yet. Takes audio's icon when it lands; nothing to decide then.                        |

One exception to I3, stated now so it is not invented twice: when two modalities share an
output kind, the second takes an **input** icon. A transcription modality (`audio->text`)
would be `Mic`, never `Type`, because `Type` already means text generation wherever it
appears. 🚧 — no such modality exists.

⚠ **Two tables agree by discipline, not by construction.** `connectionSections.ts` (per
section) and `outputKinds.ts`' `OUTPUT_KIND_ICONS` (per kind, read by Admin › Defaults and
the defaults summary) each spell the kind icons, which is how one table once came to say
`Network` and another to lack `entities`. Sampling's per-shape `CATEGORIES` went with its
category level (2026-10-10). One `KIND_ICONS` map both read is the shape I3 wants; until it
exists, a change to one is a change to both.

### Nouns

_Declared at_ names where I2 finds the canon. Where it is blank the icon has no declaration
and holds by usage alone.

**Session**

One square is a session; several are what is in it.                                                  |
| **persona**                                                               | `UserRound`                                      | the persona badge after a character's name, the **Personas** filter pick, the persona picker; the `Avatar` fallback. ⚠ Not a rail item since 2026-09-15 — the Characters view holds both. |

### Resolved collisions

- ⚠ **`Network`** → the **graph**. It was declared twice — the graph lens and the Embeddings
  section — and I3 settles it: embeddings is a kind and borrows `Zap`. The pipeline detail's
  "Map" step view also draws `Network`, and a spec map is not the narrative graph — see
  _needs an icon_.
- ⚠ **`MessageSquare` vs `MessagesSquare`** → one **session** vs the **message stream**. The
  admin nav's Sessions entry lists sessions and takes `MessageSquare` (§25); the messages
  widget keeps the plural.
- ⚠ **`CloudSun`** → the **narrator**, load-bearing since 0.5 across six sites. The World State
  widget took it second; since W7 (2026-10-11) World State is Stats (an alias), so the
  narrator holds it alone again — the ⏳ `world-state` declaration keeps it until 0.7.0, and
  nothing offers or draws that declaration. _Needs an icon_ closed.
- ⚠ **`BookOpen`** → **documentation**. A lorebook is `BookMarked` by I2; `Book` inside the
  workspace and `BookOpen` on a lorebook menu are the ones that change (§25).
- ⚠ **`Users`** → **accounts**, by both navs. Characters are `UsersRound` (I2). **Who's here**
  holds it by right (W10: its rows are accounts); the cast borrows it today and is under _needs an
  icon_. Scene Portraits left it with W6 (2026-10-11, `SquareUserRound`).
- ⚠ **`User`** → **one person where the count is one**: an account row, the `user` chat role,
  the character-lore door. Tolerated, because none of the three shares a screen with another.
  ⚠ Not a persona and not a character — both have their own, and the six persona sites and
  eight character sites drawing `User`, `UserCog`, `UserCircle` are strays (§25).
- ⚠ **`Type`** → **text**, the kind. The KoboldCPP model-kind toggle draws its Text segment as
  `MessageSquareText`, which is a prompt (§25).
- ⚠ **`Drama`** is **sprite**'s since 2026-09-24. Its one other use, the narrator-visibility
  mark on a character-lore row, was never canon and should be the narrator's `CloudSun`.

### Needs an icon

The pictogram equivalent of the ledger's **needs a word**: a term drawing a borrowed icon it
has no right to, where picking the replacement is a design decision and not bookkeeping.

| Term                                 | Holds                     | Because                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **cast**                             | the accounts' `Users`     | It means "the people in this session" and the accounts icon does not; **Who's here** holds `Users` by right (W10). **Scene Portraits** left this row with W6 (2026-10-11, `SquareUserRound`). |
| pipeline **step map** view           | the graph's `Network`     | A spec's node map is not the narrative graph.                                               |
| **spec** (as distinct from pipeline) | `Settings2` ("Open spec") | A settings gear says _configure_, not _the document_.                                       |
| **Apps** 🚧 (the rail view; the empty applet poster) | the cards lens's `LayoutGrid` | M2d 2026-11-04: the rail item and the **cards** lens (lorebook workspace, `lenses/registry.ts`) can share a screen, which I1 forbids; no replacement chosen — a design decision. |
| **hook**                             | nothing                   | No screen draws one.                                                                        |
| **context window** / **budget**      | `ChartPie` on one screen  | Not declared anywhere.                                                                      |
| **routine** 🚧 (the composer's **Routines** menu; a routine row's **Run now** item) | `Repeat` (the menu), `Play` (each item) | Lane 7, 2026-10-21: `Repeat` is the **loop** clause's icon (Nouns, Pipeline) and a routine is not a loop; no icon is declared for routines, the **While you were away** widget or a cadence. A design call. |
| **Composer** · **Turn line** 🚧 (the widgets, `composer` · `turn-line`) | nothing | Built 2026-11-05 (lane lay-B, open ★7): the two widgets split out of Messages hold no glyph yet; no screen draws one, and the Messages icon is not theirs. A design call. |

## 23. Retired words, and why

Recording _why_ a word died is what stops it being reinvented.

| Retired                                                                                                                  | Why                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **plugin rows** — the table `plugin_rows` (dropped in 0128), `ctx.storage.get` / `keys` / `query` / `put` / `delete` / `deleteAll`, `RowQuery`, `RowEntry`, `RowPage`, `rowQuotaFor`, `StorageUsage.rowBytes` / `fileBytes`, `MemoryStorage.snapshot`, `memoryStorage({ seed, rowQuotaBytes })`, the app's `rowStore` | **Retired 2026-10-25** (pr-6 sprint 2, lanes G2 and I1). Audit pass 10: `plugin_rows` had no envelope core understood. A plugin keeps hidden state in `ctx.storage.files` or in an annex field (**files-only storage**, §24). |
| `sessions.metadata.turnOrder` · `.turnTally` · `.laneReads` · `.rulesetDecks` as their homes; the per-key locks `hashtext('turnOrder')` / `hashtext('turnTally')`; `LANE_READS_METADATA_KEY`; `RULESET_DECKS_KEY` | **Retired 2026-10-25** (pr-6 sprint 2, lane G1). They are the **core runtime keys**, on annex owner `core`, under the one annex lock. `session.metadata` holds only `playerLabel` and `scenes`. |
| **annex delta** — table `annex_deltas`, `recordAnnexDelta`, `retractAnnexDeltasAnchoredTo`, `restoreAnnexDeltas`, `AnnexDeltaTaken`; also the core annex keys `rulesetConversions` / `seatBenches` as homes, `SeatBenchRecord`, `RulesetConversionRecord`, `retractSeatBenchesAnchoredTo` | **Retired 2026-11-11** (lane sense-st3, migration `0155_chubby_lockjaw` with a data upgrade). Replaced by per-key `annex` **session imprints** (§9; 🚧 provisional name), whose store `annex_imprints` in the seat keys was `annex_deltas`. ⏳ `AnnexDeltaSide` stays only to read an old `rewind_taken` record. |
| `sessions.metadata.branchOf` · `withBranchOf` · the client's `branchOf(metadata)` · `BRANCH_OF_KEY` | **Retired 2026-10-25** (pr-6 sprint 2, lanes G1 and H1). The **branch marker** is three columns, read with `branchOfSession`. |
| `timbre.narrationDescription` · UI **How their narration sounds** (card) | **Retired 2026-10-29** (voice loadouts). A card's narration is a voice picked from the voicebank (`timbre.narrationVoice`), never prose; the chosen entry's own description is the design prose. Dropped silently on import. The envoy's narration description (session setting) stays. |
| `presetPinnedSettings` · `listSessionPresets` · `chooseSessionPreset` · `CONFIGURATION_RETIRED` · `PresetOption` · `noBookDutyOverrides` · `LOREBOOK_DUTIES` | **Retired 2026-10-25** (pr-6 sprint 2, lane G4). Unused, deleted. |
| `turnsAhead` · `replaceNote` · `REWIND_NONE_AHEAD` · `createPendingReplies(…).hear` / `.running` · `RunStatusFrameLike` | **Retired 2026-10-25** (pr-6 sprint 2, lanes H5 and H2). The first three had no reader (the SDK's strip words stand); the session store's runs replace the pending-replies copy of the run frames. |
| **phantom** · **phantom lorebook** — the file `phantom.ts`, every `phantom*` export, `LoreWriteRoute` `phantom`, the `"phantom"` route | **Retired 2026-10-25** (pr-6, lane B3). Every session now owns a book from create (audit pass 11), so the word for "the one made on the first world write" had no referent left. Say the **own book** in code and **Session notes** on screen (§24, §28). _Phantom_ stays banned on screen. |
| **`sessions:createLorebookFromPhantom`** · `CREATE_LOREBOOK_FROM_SESSION_REFUSALS` · the interface's _Create lorebook from session_ and _Make a lorebook from its notes_ | **Retired 2026-10-25** (pr-6, lane B3). Replaced by **Share as a lorebook** (`sessions:shareAsLorebook`), which also gives the session fresh notes (§24). |
| **revision point** — `annexRevisionPoints.ts`, `REVISION_POINT_LIMIT` | **Retired 2026-10-25** (pr-6, lane A4). The annex is taken back through its **annex deltas**, which carry the writer's version. |
| `dropTurnWritesElsewhere` · `lastTurnOf` · `turnOfRow` · `rewindUnitOf` · turnYield as a definition of "the last turn" | **Retired 2026-10-25** (pr-6, lane A1; ruling R-c). One definition of the last turn serves every genre: the **turn unit** (§24). |
