## 24. Naming something new

1. Pick a **distinctive** word (R2). If it sounds slightly odd, it is probably right.
2. Grep for it first — across `src`, the SDK, and the schema.
3. If it collides, either pick another or **rename the other use in the same change**. Never
   ship a second meaning.
4. Qualify it if the bare noun could ever stand alone (R3).
5. Say what it is **not**, in the declaration, if a near-neighbour exists.
6. UI labels are prose and need not match internal names — but must not _contradict_ them.
7. A new pipeline: its id is genre first (`core:spec/<genre>-<what>`, or `core:spec/<what>` when
   every genre uses it) and its name says what it does, with no genre in it (§2).

### Rulesets vocabulary 🚧 (proposed 2026-10-16)

The words the rulesets programme builds with (`~/.claude/plans/PLAN-rulesets-2026-10-16.md`,
`BACKBONE-rulesets-2026-10-16.md`). Every one is 🚧 until 0.7: decided for building, still free
to move on contact with implementation. Each was grepped across both repositories and the schema
on 2026-10-16; where a near-neighbour exists, the ⚠ says what the word is not (step 5). None of
these words is shown to a player — the interface says the plain words in §28.

| Term | Means |
| --- | --- |
| **ruleset** 🚧 | A namespaced bundle of game rules, `<creator>:ruleset/<name>@<n>` (`core:ruleset/vis-itineris@1`): its **mechanics**, its stat slots, its **repertoires**, its **compendium**, its scripts and its conversions from other rulesets, declared with `defineRuleset` — the same builder for core and plugins. A lorebook names one (its **primary ruleset**) and a session names one (adopted from the attached lorebook, else picked at creation); both default to **Freeform** (`core:ruleset/freeform@1`, since 2026-10-19), so "no ruleset" and Freeform are one state. Rulesets are independent of genres: a genre says how play goes, a ruleset says what things do. **Charter (owner ruling 2026-11-05): a ruleset is stateless** — it carries just that: rules, scripts and prose that genres and sessions act on; it owns no state of its own (values live on the session and the lorebook; a "blank book of a ruleset" is a lorebook that plays it, never the ruleset holding a book). ⚠ Not a **genre** (an interaction mode, §9), not an **attribute sheet** (a ruleset _contains_ sheets), not a **spec**, not a store of anything. |
| **mechanics** 🚧 | A ruleset's rules: its conventions (its **check methods**, the degrees of success and their crosswalk to one five-band scale, time units, rest, the action economy, a **casting pool**) and the closed verb set its pieces' effects use. Always "the ruleset's mechanics" or "Vis Itineris's mechanics" in prose. Also the middle **rigour** level, `mechanics`. ⚠ Not the conformance **laws** a declaration must obey (§27, `R-20`), and not an attribute **rule** (`SlotRule`, `{ when, set \| add \| remove }`, §9) — which is why neither _laws_ nor _rules_ names this. The casual English _mechanics_ in code comments ("core owns the mechanics") is not this word and need not change. |
| **rigour** 🚧 | How much of a ruleset a session runs, on a cascade where each level includes the ones before: **`prose`** (the model reads words: names, descriptions, prose, traits; no numbers, nothing decided) › **`mechanics`** (effects, thresholds, durations and validated changes computed by the handler; 🚧 since 2026-10-22 every check decided by its **check method**, and the ruleset's scripts at all five phases) › **`scripts`** (`mechanics`, with sheets at index depth by default; where a genre lets the rules decide unasked, the Lair's _Decide checks at once_, was _Auto roll_ — §23). Interface labels **Words only** · **Rules** · **The rules decide** (`RIGOUR_LABELS`, §28). A ruleset that **decides nothing by its rules** (no check method but `none`: Freeform) plays `prose` alone (`rulesetDecides`, `rigoursPlayed`). ⚠ `Rigour`'s SDK doc comment still says `scripts` adds the scripts and chance; the engine runs both from `mechanics` (accepted 2026-10-22, lane M2), so the comment is the one to correct. A session setting within the genre's declared options; changeable mid-session. Fields outside the active ruleset render at `prose` whatever the rigour. ⚠ Not a **tier** (spent: loadout tier, memory tier; the resolution tier is retired), and it supersedes Dungeon Crawler's `core:slot/stat-mode@1` (_Story only_ / _Numbers and dice_), which becomes ⏳ when the setting lands. |
| **repertoire** 🚧 | A **list slot** that declares what its items are: a piece shape (properties, prose, traits), the mechanics its pieces may carry, its default **render depth**, who reads its pieces (🚧 `earshot` `all` · `holder`, and 🚧 `gmOnly`, 2026-10-17 — was `audience`), and whether it is entryable (yields a derived entry type). Declared with `defineRepertoire`; items and spells are repertoires, not slot types. ⚠ Not a **cast member** and not the plan's _member field_, which it replaces for that collision; not `FieldDecl.members` (`MemberDecl`, a band or labelled choice of a settings field). |
| **piece** 🚧 | One item of a repertoire: inline (`{ name, description?, prose?, traits[], equipped?, duration?, …properties }` — the six **universal piece parts**, `PIECE_FIELDS`; 🚧 `equipped` and `duration` added 2026-10-17), a lore reference (a lorebook entry, with optional overrides) or a compendium reference (pinned to the compendium's revision, with optional overrides). One resolver reads all three. ⚠ Not a plain **list item** (a word or a lore reference in a list slot that declares no repertoire); not a _member_. |
| **compendium** 🚧 | A ruleset's shipped, read-only content — the pieces its repertoires offer (gear, spells, conditions, creatures, classes), each row carrying its source and licence, versioned with the ruleset. A row is `{ id, version, source?, lang?, piece }` — bookkeeping beside, the piece nested (2026-10-17). It needs no lorebook, so lorebook-less sessions use it directly. ⚠ Not the community **Library** (§26, characters to import) and not the **pipeline library** (`/pipelines/library`); its interface word is qualified accordingly (§28). |
| **bridge** 🚧 | A field's declared, additive integration with a ruleset: a small list of operations (`modify`, `adjustDegree`, `rider`, applied after the ruleset's own — the before/after listing was cut 2026-10-17; registered with `registerBridge`, read with `bridgesFor`) a ruleset's handler applies at the `mechanics` level, validated when authored so it can never redefine or override the ruleset's own fields. Always "a ruleset bridge" where it could stand alone (R3). ⚠ Not an **export profile** (§16) or the plan's _compat_, which it replaces; not the **capability bridge** (QuickJS's async host-function transport, §25). |
| **parked** 🚧 | The state of data that belongs to a ruleset the session or lorebook is not running: kept byte for byte under its ruleset's namespace, never written, never validated, never deleted, shown once under _Other rulesets_ until it is converted or the ruleset returns. "Parked data" in prose. ⚠ Not **dormant** (a 0.5.3 node state the attic imports), and not a **cap pause**'s run that "parks" for the session owner (a verb sense, §9). |
| ~~**bestow**~~ | **Cut 2026-10-17** (owner ruling, §23): the verb was declared and validated, never read by a host; a piece is given by an ordinary state write. The word stays unused — never reintroduce it as **grant** either (R2). |
| **render depth** 🚧 | How much of a repertoire a prompt receives: **`index`** (one line for the whole field), **`summary`** (one line per relevant piece), **`full`** (the piece's card). A repertoire declares which properties each depth includes and a default; the context budget lowers a depth before it drops a block. Prompt shaping, not display: it lives on the declaration (owner ruling 2026-10-16), while how a widget draws a piece stays a widget setting. ⚠ Not a **tier**; not a display _format_. |
| **ruleset voice** 🚧 | The short paragraph (≤ 60 tokens) a ruleset declares per rigour, telling the model in words how play feels under its mechanics; rendered byte-stable as the handler's first block. Prompt content on the declaration (owner ruling 2026-10-16). ⚠ Not a channel's **voice** (`character` · `narrator` · `none`, §9). |
| **primer** 🚧 | A starting bundle a new lorebook can be made from: it sets the lorebook's primary ruleset and fills it with starter content in our own voice (a region, places joined on the places graph, factions, cast, a calendar and clock, hooks). Applied once at creation, never re-applied, never to an own book. Catalogue data, versioned. ⚠ Not a **template** (context templates, §15), not a **preset** (pipeline presets) and not a **genre preset** — which is why the owner's _lorebook template_ was not used. |
| **own book** 🚧 | The session's own lorebook, which replaced the _phantom lorebook_ (§23): see **Session data vocabulary** below. The interface says **Session notes** (§28). |
| **table channel** 🚧 | The folio a ruleset's outcomes are written to: rolls, checks, totals and their explain traces, in no voice, under no speaker, each row anchored to the story message it belongs to so it reads "at that moment" and retracts with it. The story channel's history never holds them; the model reads outcomes only through the handler's labelled `outcomes` block, placed after the history. A Messages widget may interleave its rows by anchor. ⚠ Not the ⏳ **table line** (a `metadata.tableLine` row on the story channel, which it retires for new writes), not the **travelogue** (Dungeon Crawler's _Journal_ folio of round summaries), and not a database table. |
| **Vis Itineris** 🚧 | `core:ruleset/vis-itineris@1`: core's rigorous d20 ruleset, built on the open d20 reference rules (CC-BY-4.0) with its own options — four degrees of success, three actions a turn, typed bonuses plus an `edge` type that rolls twice, dying 1–4, sustained spells — and a _Classic_ preset that restores the reference rules as published. The licence's own notice lives beside the compendium data and on the Licences screen; no compatibility claim is made. |
| **Freeform** (the ruleset) 🚧 | `core:ruleset/freeform@1` (was `core:ruleset/story@1`, renamed 2026-10-19 — §23): the identity ruleset — a lorebook as it already is, words only, no mechanics that compute. Every lorebook and session defaults to it, and every custom field lands in it as prose. Its entryable lists are **Things** and **Conditions**, with no library. ⚠ **Story** is the genre now (§9), never the ruleset. |
| **Bonds** 🚧 | `core:ruleset/bonds@1`: core's relational ruleset — feelings between people measured on pieces anchored to the relationship between them, thresholds that unlock moments, scheduled events on the story clock; addable beside another ruleset through bridges. ⚠ A bond's piece decorates a graph **relationship** (§17); it never replaces the relationship row. ⚠ Not **Wherewithal**'s `bonds` repertoire, one part of a whole ruleset. |
| **Sojourn** 🚧 _(deferred)_ | The planned narrative-rules fantasy ruleset (2d6 moves with partial success), built on open reference rules under their licence; deferred until Vis Itineris lands. The name is held, not built. |
| **shared vocabulary** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-20 (R27–R29, A19).** A declared object of attribute members grouped by owner — `vocabulary(id, { world?, cast?, location? })` (`Vocabulary`, `VOCABULARY_OWNERS`); core's **common vocabulary** `core:vocabulary/common@1` (`rulesets.common`, `commonVocabulary`: world location, time, weather; cast health, mood, level, class, currency, things, conditions, relationships; location ways out, notes). A ruleset **plays** vocabularies (`plays`, common last) natively or with a **map** onto its own stats (`map: [[member, ownStat]]`); a ruleset may retitle a member (Vis Itineris shows _currency_ as _Gold_), the slug stays. ⚠ **Collides with the app's session vocabulary** (`vocabularyFor`, the words a session's genre uses for its lines): always _shared vocabulary_ or _common vocabulary_ for this, _session vocabulary_ for that — never bare _vocabulary_ where both could be meant (R3). |
| **attribute reference** 🚧 | How an author names a property (A19, R30): an object (`rulesets.common.cast.health`, a ruleset's own, a custom vocabulary's) or a string (`stat('shields')`, warned, never refused); `AttributeRef`, `resolveAttributeRef` → own · vocabulary · map · direct, else null with a reason. |
| **condition property** 🚧 | A typed handle `sessionOf(genre)` derives from what a genre declares (`ConditionProp { path, type, members?, slot? }`, `SessionOf<G>`; world · cast.any · locations.any · fields · annex · **host facts** — generating, the open form, backdrop, sprites, the message). The condition builders `isTrue` · `eq` · `gt` · `gte` · `lt` · `lte` · `oneOf` · `and` · `or` · `not` · `same` produce a registration's `when`; **any member** is the stored `*` path segment. ⚠ Not a DataRef and not a settings field; never "session view". |
| **check method** 🚧 | How a ruleset decides a moment that could go either way (`CheckMethodDecl`, SDK `checkMethods.ts`; ruling R1, built 2026-10-22): a kind — **`die-target`** · **`dice-pool`** · **`card-draw`** · **`compare`** · **`bid`** · **`none`** (`CORE_CHECK_METHOD_KINDS`; `CHECK_METHOD_KINDS` holds each kind's words, `chance`, `rollsDice`, `takesBands` and options) or a package's own `owner:name` (accepted with a warning; the app has no resolver and refuses its checks in words, `no-resolver`) — with that kind's options, keyed by a name of the ruleset's own under `conventions.methods`, one of them `conventions.defaultMethod`; a check selector names another with `method`. Difficulty bands belong to a method made against a target (`die-target` · `card-draw` · `compare`: `method.bands`). No method, or only `none`: the ruleset **decides nothing by its rules** (`rulesetDecides`). Always _check method_ where it could stand alone (R3), never a bare _method_. The interface says **way** (§28). ⚠ Not a **mechanic** (a piece's effect), not a **rigour**, not a **degree** (how a decided check reads). |
| **outcome block** 🚧 | A decided check as a message block (`OutcomeBlock`; the stored kind **`dice`** kept, so every written block still reads): `method`, `rolled`, `pool`, `cards` (`OutcomeCard`), `compare { versus }`, `against`, `outcome`, `five`, `explain` — what was checked, what it came to, against what, how it came out in the ruleset's words, tinted by its five-band step, with how it was reached under it. The Messages widget draws it by method (`data-method`, a glyph per kind). Its line in the story is the **outcome line** (§28). ⚠ Not the handler's **`outcomes`** prompt block (what the model reads: the outcome's words, never the block); not a **roll form** (the question before it). ⏳ `DiceBlock` is its old type name. |
| **repertoire tag** 🚧 | What a repertoire's pieces are, said once on its declaration (`tags`, `RepertoireTag`): core reads `condition` · `casting` · `weapon` · `armour` · `relationship` · `resource` · `exit` · `note` · `creature` · `class` (`REPERTOIRE_TAGS`); open, lowercase words joined by `-`. What a ruleset provides is read from them (`rulesetProvides`: `conditions`, `casting`, `tags`, `tagged`, `chance`, `methods`); a ruleset none of whose repertoires says tags is ⏳ guessed from names (`guessRepertoireTags`, warning `untagged-repertoires`; the shipped catalogue may not be, C38). Always _repertoire tag_ where it could stand alone (R3). ⚠ Not a **Tag** label (§22), not a **cast tag** (`{{char:N}}`), not a piece's **traits**. |
| **amount expression** 🚧 | How much a `harm` or `heal` moves a stat (`AmountExpr`, `mechanicAmount`): a number, a dice string (only in a ruleset one of whose check methods throws dice, else `amount-needs-dice`), or `{ selector }` (a ruleset selector or `piece.<field>`). ⏳ A rule's `dice: 'piece.x'` reads as `amount: { selector: 'piece.x' }`. |
| **casting pool** 🚧 | What a cast spends when a ruleset spends a pool for it rather than the piece (`RulesetCasting { pool, cost, repertoire?, refill?, max? }`, `conventions.casting`; read by the app's `castingPoolOf`). Vis Itineris lays one with its `casting: points` choice (`VIS_ITINERIS_SPELL_POINTS`). A ruleset's numbers live in its declaration, never in the engine. ⚠ Not the **casting** repertoire tag (what pieces are). |
| **ruleset template** 🚧 | An archetype to start a ruleset of one's own from: a complete, small ruleset (`template: true`, at most 60 lines since 2026-10-23) with sample rows and a **playtest scene**, declared with `defineRulesetTemplate` into its own registry (`RulesetTemplate { id, label, about, goodFor, ruleset, playtest }`, `getRulesetTemplate`, `rulesetTemplates`). Core's `RULESET_TEMPLATES`, in the order _New ruleset_ offers them: the four of `core-catalog/src/rulesets/archetypes/` (`ARCHETYPE_TEMPLATES`: `core:ruleset/template-romance@1` · `template-slice-of-life@1` · `template-workplace@1` · `template-card-game@1`; 2026-10-23), then `template-d20-style@1` · `template-dice-pool@1` · `template-diceless-pools@1` — all in the seven sections over core's functions. Copied, never played: `defineRuleset` refuses one (`template-not-played`), a genre may not name one (`template-ruleset`), and a copy is never one. **One term, R1:** the interface says **archetype** for every ruleset template (§28); in code the word qualifies only the first four's folder and list, never a second kind of thing. Always qualified (R3). ⚠ Not a **context template** (§15), not a **primer**, not any **preset**. |
| **playtest scene** 🚧 | A sample party of one to four, the situation in a sentence, and one change, put through a ruleset as a turn would (`RulesetPlaytest { party, situation, change }`, `PlaytestMember`, `PlaytestChange`, `playtestFindings`, `bad-playtest`): what a ruleset template carries and what the editor's **Playtest a scene** seats. Nothing a run does is saved; 🚧 a scene **saved as a test** (2026-10-23) is kept on the ruleset — `RulesetProps.playtests` (`SavedPlaytest { name, party, situation?, change \| null, rigour?, seed? }`, `savedPlaytestFindings`, `bad-playtests`; what a test names is read, never refused when stale). ⚠ Not a story **scene** (§9). |
| **Wherewithal** 🚧 | `core:ruleset/wherewithal@1` (built 2026-10-22, ruling R3): core's diceless ruleset, original to Serene Pub (Apache-2.0). Three pools, **Nerve**, **Favour** and **Provisions** (0–6, default 3; `core:slot/wherewithal-*@1`), each spent by a `bid` check method (_dare_, _sway_, _make-do_: 1 _It holds, at a cost_ · 2 _It carries_ · 3 _It carries clean_); **mettle** (derived, on the sheet: the best pool, one more per steady bond, at most two) weighed in a **contest** (`compare`; _Slight_ 1 · _Even_ 3 · _Steep_ 5 · _Towering_ 7); everything else **judgement** (`none`, the default). Repertoires **bonds** (relational, tag `relationship`; **tie**, **footing** _steady_ · _strained_ · _broken_), **troubles** (its conditions; _light_ · _heavy_) and **boons** (help on hand); scripts at `derived`, `effects` and `render`. ⚠ Not **Bonds** (the held relational add-on). _Provisions_, never _supply_ (an item's supply, R1); _mettle_, never _bearing_ (the Exits line's). |
| **function module** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-23 (PLAN-rulesets-functions D1).** One small rule as a declaration — a **header** (`name`, `meaning`, its **function kind**, **function bindings**, `adds`, `prose` the model reads, a reply `schema`, an options `form`, its **function phases**, `emits`, `invokable`) and, where it computes, a **body** (an ES module the **rules sandbox** runs; none: **header-only**, judged in words). `owner:function/<name>@N`; `defineFunction` / `definePluginFunction`, `getFunction`, `functionHash`. **Function kind**: value · deciding · changing · pieces · zones · scope · asking · time · progression, or a package's `owner:name`. **Function phase**: effects · derived · before · after · render (_before_ / _after_ replace _pre-roll_ / _post-roll_); outside them a **way**'s `decide`, a scope's `members`, an invoked `invoke`. **Function binding** (always qualified): a role the header declares, bound to an attribute, entry type, zone type, scope or owner kind (`FunctionBindingDecl { to, tags?, pick?, many? }`). A ruleset uses one by a **function reference** (`FunctionRef { ref, key, bindings?, options?, module?, hash? }`: its **key** names the use; a pin `hash`, refused as `function-hash-moved`); editing a body **forks** it into the ruleset as a **carried module** (`forkFunction`, `forkedFrom`). **Reserved function ids** (`CORE_FUNCTION_IDS`) are what the shapes before the sections read as. A deciding function **decides** only when it is a **way**: its body exports `decide`, or a check names it as its way (`functionRefDecides`, `functionWayKeys`, 2026-10-23). ⚠ Not a pipeline node, not a pipeline **script** (a function body over `value`), not a **task**. |
| **ruleset sections** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-23 (D2).** A ruleset declared in eight keys — `attributes` · `functions` · `entryTypes` · `zoneTypes` · `outcomes` · `time` · `library` · `options` (`RULESET_SECTIONS`; the editor's seven, outcomes and time one) — nothing required beyond its `name` (R9: **from scratch** is `{ name }`). A **ruleset attribute** (`RulesetAttributeDecl`: kind number · pool · tally · label · list, bounds, `carriedBy`, `visibility`, `changedBy`, tags, prose, **shown-as hint** `shownAs`) is filed under the slot it names or a **derived attribute slot** (`<owner>.<ruleset>:slot/<attr>@N`, registered with the ruleset); a **ruleset entry type** is an entry type; a **zone type** (`ZoneTypeDecl`) is instanced per owner as a **zone** — the host's **carried** zone type is every owner's; **outcome words** (an optional ladder onto the five bands); the **time section**; the **ruleset library** (⚠ always qualified: the rail's Library is §26's); **ruleset options**. ⏳ The shapes before them read in (`rulesetSections`, `rulesetInSections` — what data upgrade 0119 persists) and back out: conventions through `normaliseConventions`, and on a registered declaration in sections its `stats`, `repertoires`, `selectors` and `compendium` hung **unenumerated** (`sectionsLegacyView`) — never hashed, never in its document, never judged; a section beside its old shape is refused (`legacy-beside-section`). ⚠ A ruleset attribute is not an **attribute slot**; the shown-as hint is not `EntryShape.render` nor a **render depth**. |
| **held entry** 🚧 | An entry in a **zone** (D5): a copy stamped from its lorebook entry, `entryId` kept so a function may read the source (`HeldEntry`, `stampHeldEntry`); stored per changed zone as **zone contents** (`zone_contents`, migration 0119, anchored to the turn's message). A **zone ask** (`ZoneOp`: move · add · remove · reveal · hide) is how a function or a reply changes one. ⚠ Not a lorebook **scope**; not a list slot's **piece**, which a type kept in a list slot stays (read there wholly). |
| **tie** (on the lorebook graph) 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-23 (ties on the graph, rulings T1–T5, lane T2).** A relational **ruleset entry type** that says its **far end** (`farEnd`: `person` · `place` · `entry`, `FAR_ENDS`; findings `bad-far-end`, and `bad-holders` for holders against its sides). Its **tie sides** are worked out from the ends, never said (`tieSidesOf`, `tieHoldersOf`): a person to a person is two, each person holding their own side (the graph's two **perspective** rows); anything else is one, held by the world. A held tie side carries its **side owner** (`HeldEntry.sideOwner`, an owner key); `stampTieSides` stamps every side at once (`TieEnds`, `TieSideStamp`). A tie's numbers live on its held sides (Romance's _affection_); the graph row keeps words, a **projection**. Any field may **read onto the lorebook** (`readsOnto`, `READS_ONTO` = `relationship-type` · `relationship-name` · `entry-field` · `cast-state`, `READS_ONTO_BY_OWNER`, `CAST_STATE_WORDS`; `bad-reads-onto`): ONE per-field setting, validated by owner kind; the host writes it whenever the value lands, through the outlet (the **one writer**, `writeLandings` / `writeAttributeLandings`), the row carrying the run (`narrative_relationships.rules_run_id`, migration 0121) — a **rule-fed row**, read _from the rules_. Each field says what the model is told (`modelShare` `{ words?, number? }`, `modelShareOf`: words on, the number off; `bad-model-share`). A **tie field selector** `<type>.<field>` (`bond.affection`, `tieFieldSelectors`) is read at a check as the side of the one aimed at, towards the one checking. ⚠ _Far end_, _side_ and _end_ are always qualified (R3): never a bare _side_. ⚠ A tie side is not a **perspective** row (it reads onto one), not a **piece**, not the ⏳ untyped `towards` of a relational repertoire (no far end: read as before). 🚧 **Lane T3 (2026-10-23):** a one-sided tie is held in a zone type the world owns, else the ruleset is refused **`unheld-tie`** (`unheldTieFindings`, naming the zone type to add; Workplace's **Footing**, held on the **Grapevine**, is the worked example); a function's `add` on a two-sided tie stamps the other side wherever its holder is, resolved from its key when the moment does not read them (the far end, `farEndsOf`); a value fed onto a book the session may not write at Full lands in the notes' **rule-fed overlay** (§24 below). |
| **entry field selector** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-23 (lane T3, ★2).** `<entry type>.<field>` of any entry type's number field (`entryFieldSelectors`; a **tie field selector** is one): what an attribute role may be filled by when its function says **`entryFields`** (`FunctionBindingDecl.entryFields`, refused on any other role, `bad-function-binding`). Read per held entry — a tie's per side — never per owner (the host's `entryFieldOf`, `bindings.<role>.fields`); a `derived` module so bound is worked out on what the moment's asks left (`runEntryFieldFunctions`, `entryFieldUses`). `core:function/rungs@1` takes one, with **`into`** (_Kept in_): the field its words are kept in — Romance's _Standing_ worked out from _Affection_ (cold 0–2 · wary 3–5 · warm 6–7 · close 8–10). Its prose reads _Affection on a bond_. ⚠ Not a ruleset **selector** (a stat or a check by key). |
| **an outcome moves a number** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-23 (lane T3).** `core:function/outcome-moves@1` (`outcomeMovesFunction`, changing group, phase `after`): how a check came out moves a number by its outcome word's amount (`check`, `moves: [{ outcome, by }]`, `whose`: `aimed-at` · `checker`) — an attribute (`add`), or an entry's number field (`entryFields`): the side the one aimed at holds, towards the one checking, by the zone ask `set` with `by`. Romance's _Confess_: cooled −1, warmed +1, confessed +2. ⚠ Not **margins** (a margin read as an outcome word). |
| **rule-fed overlay** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-23 (lane T3, ★5).** What the rules fed onto a book the session may not write at Full (`entry-field`: a held thing's or a place's field, by entry id; `cast-state`: a member's state, by the book's member id; and 🚧 `placeValues`: a place's world-scope attribute values, by the book's entry id and slot id — ★pl-1, 2026-11-05, lane pl2), kept on the session's notes' own row (`lorebooks.extra_json.ruleFed`; `RuleFedOverlay`, `ruleFedOverlayOf`) and read in the book's place by the session's lore read and the graph's cast (`memberAt`). A landing so kept says `overlaid`. ⚠ Not a **dated overlay** (an amendment, written into the book by its owner); not a copied entry — a copy would be offered by _Apply to the lorebook_ and read twice. |
| **scope function** 🚧 | A function of kind `scope` (D4) answering who is **in reach** — core's same-place · within-tie · aimed-at · everyone (`CORE_SCOPE_IDS`, answered natively), or a body's `members`. Never bare _scope_ (R3); the interface says **Who's in reach**. An attribute's or zone type's **visibility** is holder · gm · everyone or a scope (`VISIBILITY_WORDS`); an instance may be **exposed** by its holder. **changedBy** (rules · gm · holder · everyone) says who may change an attribute — enforced at the write (`changedByAllows`, the `state:set` door). |
| **rules sandbox** 🚧 | Where function bodies run (D3, app `rulesets/sandbox.ts`): one QuickJS context per resolve moment, modules loaded once by content hash, one budget per moment, each call capped and seeded. A **function handler** answers a **function ledger** — deltas, lines, outcome words, emits, asks (⚠ not a receipt) — and never writes (R8): the resolve outlet applies, or files for review; a resolve moment reports **held deltas**. Events a function raises are **emitted at the end** — after the run's receipt, as its children under the depth cap (`dispatchRulesetEmits`) — unless the step's `emits` parameter or the pipeline's **`functionEvents: false`** says not (⚠ never the pipeline's `emits`, the events it declares, R6). Core's own ways stay native in the engine; their modules are read, not run. |
| **core function catalogue** 🚧 | Core's function modules (`CORE_FUNCTIONS`, `CORE_FUNCTION_GROUPS`: values · deciding · changing · scopes · pieces and zones · time and order · progression and economy · asking): among them **rungs** (⚠ not the outcomes' ladder), **word value**, **refilling pool** (⚠ not a casting pool), **lasting condition**, **tie standing**, **obligation** (`obligation-came-due`), **deck** (adds deck · hand · discard; ⚠ not the card-draw way's `DeckState`), **carrying limit**, **recurring**, **scheduled** (`scheduled-moment-reached`; ⚠ not a cadence), **deadline** (`deadline-passed`), **turn order by**, **actions per turn**, **rest** (`rest-taken`), **experience levels** (`level-reached`), **prices**, **reputation gate**, **limited supply** (⚠ never _provisions_), **ask and wait** (a stub); 🚧 **at zero health** (values, below). Their **body contract** (`core-catalog/src/functions/body.ts`) is the one the rules sandbox runs. 🚧 Every event one raises is a declared core event, since `onEvent` refuses an undeclared one: `coreEvents.restTaken` (lane G3) · `levelReached` · `obligationCameDue` · `deadlinePassed` · `scheduledMomentReached` (GM 2026-10-23, ★G3-4), family `data`, caused by `core:task/ruleset-resolve`, the function's values on the payload's `values`. 🚧 A **check** reference may carry its own words (`label`, GM 2026-10-23, G2 ★1: Vis Itineris's _Strength save_, _Sleight of hand_), what a roll form and the Lair's outcome line read; a check with none is its key read plainly. |
| **rules action** 🚧 | An **invokable** function of a session's ruleset offered as an action (D6): one generic pipeline, `core:spec/rules-action` (inlet `core:inlet/rules-action@1`), registered once per such function in the genre's layer (`rulesActionRegistrations`; identity `core:spec/rules-action#<key>`), listed at the composer, fired with `rulesActionPayload`. ★ Runs Full: an action registration carries no mode (R37). ⚠ Not a **mechanic** event, not a genre's own action. |
| **Replies carry changes** 🚧 | Story's reply option (D7, R7): the reply duty `changes` (owner reach, off; mode key `reply-changes`), the reply answering JSON against the **reply schema** (`ruleset-resolve`'s `replySchema`, built from the session's attributes and entry types; 🚧 in the grammar subset every backend compiles since GM 2026-10-23 — no `null`, no type union: empty text is none, an amount is text a number is read out of) — its `message` the words, its **reply changes** applied at its own duty mode (`reply-changes`; an event registration carries no mode, so on is Full — G1, S2; was the reckoning's) (`replyChangesAsDeltas`, `unknown-change`). While it is on at Full the reckoning's _Keep the sheets_ and _Track conditions_ are **ceded** (§4 **duties**). 🚧 The `reply` junction holds only what differs — the call and what reads its answer; the **shared tail** after it (save, commit, the line's face, the tick) runs once whichever branch fired (RF fix 3, 2026-10-23). ⚠ A JSON step never streams today (the stream law, ★). |
| **handbook** 🚧 | What players read of a ruleset or genre (D8): pages generated from the sentences it carries (`renderHandbook`, cli) beside the author's own (`RulesetProps.handbook`, `GenreProps.handbook`: `HandbookPage { title, body }`, `handbookFindings`, `bad-handbook`; a page titled as a generated one replaces it). A documentation word: never a prompt block. |
| **one change grammar** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-23 (PLAN-genres-seams S1, lane G1).** The ONE schema a genre asks a model for changes in: `ruleset-resolve`'s **reply schema** change — `owner`, `changes` (attribute · entry), `attribute`, `entryType`, `op`, `value`, `name`, `reason` — built from the session's rules at run time, in the grammar subset (empty text is none; never `null` or a type union). Story's reckoning (`RECKON_CHANGE_SCHEMA`; `STORY_RECKON_SCHEMA` its envelope `{changes, clock, place}`), the Lair keeper (the same graph) and the Dungeon Crawler's **Planner's grammar** (`core:script/dungeon-crawler-shape`, the genre's own fields and checks laid on top, G3) ask in it; what the rules keep goes through the ruleset handler, the sheets' other words are written in words. ⚠ Not the retired delta grammar `slot` / `repertoire` / `piece` (§23), which the handler still reads (`asDelta`, `deltaOf`). |
| **at zero health** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-23 (★I, lane G3).** The **fall rule**: `core:function/at-zero-health@1` (`atZeroHealthFunction`, values group; binding `health`; `AtZeroHealthOptions` — `sides`, `door { target, step, upOn }`, `saves? { target, passes, failures, low, high }`, `savesWhen? { option, is }`), one ES5 rule (`AT_ZERO_HEALTH_JS`, `atZeroHealthOf`: `survives` · `down` · `stable` · `dying`) its body and the Dungeon Crawler's death's door both splice. A ruleset that references it has a fall rule with its own numbers (Vis Itineris: `VIS_ITINERIS_AT_ZERO_HEALTH_RULE`); one that does not has none, and the fall is told in words. Not invokable. ⚠ Not Vis Itineris's _Dying 1–4_ track, not the crawl's `fate`, not a **check** (a fall adds nothing to the roll). |
| **ruleset gist** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-23 (S4, lane G3).** What a genre reads of the session's ruleset, at run time, laid on every inlet's `ruleset` (`rulesetGistOf(decl, settings)`, `RulesetGist`, DC `fromRuleset.ts`): `name`, `decides` (`rulesetDecides`), `rests` (longest first, `time.rests`), `atZeroHealth` and `playsSaves`, `levels`, `decidingKeys`, `casting`, `kits` (rows of the entry type tagged `class`), `exits` (tagged `exit`), `conditions` (tagged `condition`); `rulesetOffersRest`, `conditionsOf`. ⚠ Not `RulesetRolls` / the Lair's **rules row** (`lairRulesRow`), not `rulesetInletSections` (the inlet's `attributes` / `entryTypes`, G1) — three readers, three keys, no collision. |
| **difficulty** (always qualified) 🚧 | Three things, never bare _difficulty_ where two could be meant (R3; lane G0, 2026-10-23). The UI label _Difficulty_ stays per genre. **Story difficulty** — Story's field `difficulty`, `story` · `normal` · `hard`, shown _Gentle_ · _Normal_ · _Hard_, read by the reckoning's and the sweep's cribs (⚠ its member `story` predates the genre's name). **crawl difficulty** — the Dungeon Crawler's `core:slot/difficulty@1`, `gentle` · `fair` · `brutal` (its steps `DUNGEON_CRAWLER_DIFFICULTY_STEPS`, G3). **difficulty band** — a ruleset's named target (§25 Lair rewrite L1; a check way's `bands`); a Lair plan's risk `difficulty` names a band id, so prose says "the risk's difficulty band". |
| **attribute carry** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-23 (RF fix 2, item 3).** Whether one holder carries one of the rules' attributes in one session — a switch per holder beside the values (`attribute_carries`, 0122; `server/state/carries.ts`). Off: not shown (the sheet leaves it out), not read (the holder's state bag and the rules' owner view have no key for it), not written (a write is refused); what it held is kept and comes back when it is on again. Switched by whoever plays the holder, or the session's owner for anyone (the world and places, the owner alone). An attribute marked `required` is always carried. Member copy: **Carries ‹attribute›**, under **Who carries what**. ⚠ Not a **pick** (`session_attribute_picks`: what the whole session tracks) and not `carriedBy` / `appliesTo` (which owner kinds may carry it at all). |
| **free text** (an attribute kind) 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-23 (RF fix 2, item 2).** `kind: 'text'`: a few sentences of each holder's own (a vow, a backstory), a text slot; shown as words, read by the model as a sentence of its own under the holder's sheet line, changed as `changedBy` says. ⚠ Not a `label` — one of its words, or a word or two, read inline beside the numbers. |
| **what a message changed goes with it** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-23 (RF fix 4; owner: "what about lorebook entries affected by messages/pipelines").** The one retraction rule. (1) Everything a run writes is anchored to the message that caused it — the run's live row, else the session's newest (`turnAnchorOf`) — and carries the run: state rows and zone snapshots on their own columns, every write on a lorebook as a **lore imprint**. (2) A swipe, a regenerate, a reply that failed empty and a **delete** take the same things back — `retractStateAnchoredTo` (values, configurations, proposals, clock moves, `zone_contents`, then `retractLoreAnchoredTo`: imprints, and the notes' entries anchored by `source_message_id` alone); a delete reaches the plain-int anchors inside its own transaction (`messages/store.ts` `deleteLegacy` / `deleteLegacyWhere`), the rest by the FK cascade; a retake also takes its runs' imprints anchored elsewhere (`dropTurnWritesElsewhere`); a failed replacement puts everything back (`restoreRetractedState`). (3) A shared (real) book is never silently rewritten: a write is reverted only while it is the newest standing imprint of its field and the field still holds what the run wrote (a made row: as made, nothing standing on it); otherwise it stays, **kept**, and the entry says _Written by a reply that was since replaced_ with **Revert** · **Keep**. The session's notes always revert. (4) Under Review nothing landed; proposals cascade. (5) A message **edit** (its prose) takes back nothing. A person's press (an action with no live row: _File as a room_) writes as the person and files no imprint. ⚠ Not **On revision** (what a delete or regenerate of the latest turn does to the timeline: overwrite or branch); this rule is what an overwrite takes back. |
| **lore imprint** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-23 (RF fix 4, migration 0124).** One change a session's run made to a lorebook row (`lore_imprints`, `loreImprints`; `server/lorebooks/imprints.ts`): its **subject** (`subject_kind` `entry` · `relationship` · `member` · `overlay` — the notes' rule-fed overlay, by the notes' id; `subject_id`, no key), the **field** it wrote (a column `title`, a typed field `fields.<key>` — `entryFieldAddress` —, an overlay path `entryFields.<id>.<field>` · `castStates.<id>` · `placeValues.<entry id>.<slot id>` (pl2, 2026-11-05); NULL: the run **made** the row), `before` / `after` wrapped `{ v }` (NULL = absent), anchored (`message_id`, a plain int) and carrying the run (`run_id`; NULL for a person's accepted held change). 🚧 Also an **`origin`** (`IMPRINT_ORIGINS` / `ImprintOrigin`: `run` · `routine` · `press` · `person` · `apply` · `book-run` · `upgrade`; CHECK `lore_imprints_origin_check`; only `run` and `apply` are written today), a **`batch`** (one per **Apply** press) and a **`cause`** (who pressed, the session, the message) — 2026-11-11, lane sense-b1. An `apply` record keeps `before` and `after` of a field **Apply to the lorebook** wrote from a **held amendment**, or, with `field` NULL, where an entry or a link it moved was before (`cause.moved`; 2026-11-12, lane sense-b2); a turn never takes it, and settling never compacts it. Filed by the one writer of each lorebook write: `create-lore-entry` (the entry, its links, its Exits links), `update-lore-entry` (each column and field it changed in an entry of the own book; on an entry of the attached lorebook it holds a **held amendment** instead and files no imprint until Apply), `link-lore-entries` (a link it made), the ties' landings (a tie's words and the run on its row, a held thing's or a place's field, a member's state, a row it made or copied into the notes, the rule-fed overlay). Taken back by **the one rule** (`retractImprints` over `retractionAct`, which **session imprints** share — 2026-11-11: newest first — a later standing write of the field is **spliced** when it continued this one, else this one is **dropped**; **reverted** on the notes or while unchanged; a made row **unmade**; else **kept**), put back by `restoreImprints` (`TakenImprint`). A **kept imprint** is the entry's note (`LorebookEntry.keptImprints`, `KeptImprint`, `keptImprintsByEntry`; the list row's mark _replaced_), settled by `lorebooks:settleImprint` (**Revert** puts `before` back or removes the made row; **Keep** leaves it; either way it goes) for whoever may edit the book. ⚠ Not a **receipt** (a run's whole record), not a **run artifact** (which rows a run touched, no values), not an **amendment** (a dated overlay a person writes), not the **rule-fed overlay**; never shown by that name — members read _Written by a reply that was since replaced_. |
| **session imprint** 🚧 (provisional name, unruled) | **Built 2026-11-11 (lane sense-st3; owner: "Move to columns (Recommended)").** One change a turn made to a **session row**, kept so it can be taken back: table `session_imprints`, `sessionImprints` (`sessions/sessionImprints.ts`), the sibling of the **lore imprint**. 🚧 The owner has been shown the name and has not ruled it. **Purpose / why:** Back, a swipe, a regenerate and a delete must put a session's own changes back as they put a lore row back, and the old homes (the core annex keys, `annex_deltas`) were three records of one idea. **Owns:** the kinds `SESSION_IMPRINT_KINDS` — `seat-bench` (a pipeline's bench or bring-back), `ruleset-conversion` (the rules' version), `deck` (**a card draw: every draw files one, anchored to the turn by `turnAnchorOf` in every mode, propose included**), `annex` (one per changed key, with the key's audience before and after and the owner's version); one row per write, anchored to the turn's message, `standing` / `settled`. Filed by `fileSessionImprint`; taken by `retractSessionImprints`, put back by `restoreSessionImprints`, settled by `settleSessionImprints` (the settle line, as for lore imprints), read by `sessionImprintsAfter`, converted from an old `rewind_taken` record by `sessionImprintsFromOldRecord`, copied to a branch (ids mapped to the branch's messages and seats) by `copySessionImprintsToBranch`. Keys: `seatBenchKey`, `annexImprintKey`; `standingSeatBenches`; `isTimelessAnnexKey`. **The rule** is `retractionAct` (`lorebooks/imprints.ts`), shared with lore imprints; a session row is always **reverted**; a seat a person already set the other way is left and its row dropped. **Decks:** when two turns drew from one deck and the earlier is taken, the earlier turn's cards stay spent (the later card was dealt from the position the earlier draw left — the rule's splice); taking the later afterwards puts the deck where it stood before both. **A branch** is the session as of the fork: the parent's later imprints are folded back onto decks, ruleset version and bench flags. **Does not own:** turn order and read marks (bookkeeping, **core runtime keys**); a lore row's change (**lore imprint**); who may see it (never shown by that name). ⚠ Not an **annex delta** (retired, §23), not a **lore imprint**, not a **receipt**. |
| **rewound turn** · **forward stack** · **Back** · **Forward** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-23 (RF fix 5; owner: "disable message deletions by default and introduce a back and forward button. If clicking back, rewind the history. On continue/new write, replace the rewound history.")** A **rewound turn** is a turn **Back** took out of the session's history — kept, never deleted: its rows carry `session_messages.rewind_ordinal` (1 = the first Back, the newest turn) and are `is_hidden`, and every reader of the history leaves them out (`liveMessageWhere`, `messages/store.ts`; the anchors' `newestMessageId` / `turnMessages`, the turn yield, the channel head, the page's log and pages, a branch's copy, retrieval's window). The **forward stack** is the session's rewound turns; **Forward** brings back the highest ordinal. The **unit** (`rewindUnitOf`, `sessions/rewind.ts`): the newest person's line on the story's lane and every row after it there — at a table of several players the newest **round** the turn tally uses (R52, `replayStoryLane`) — with the rows the turn's runs wrote on other channels (their turn yield) and the table rows anchored to them; never before the first person line (greetings and the opening stay), never into a branch's copies (`metadata.copyOf`: refused, pointing at the parent). What Back takes it takes by **the one retraction rule** (`retractStateAnchoredTo(…, { ticks: 'take' })`: values, configurations, proposals, every clock move its tick included, zone snapshots, lore imprints, the notes' entries), plus what the turn's runs wrote anchored elsewhere, the annex (taken back through its annex deltas) and the story lane's tally (replayed); all of it is kept on the row (`session_messages.rewind_taken`, `RewoundTakenV1`), so the stack survives a reload, and Forward restores it with the same ids (`restoreRetractedState`, the clock stepped forward). One `message-hidden` per press under an edit's cause, its payload's `rewind` `back` · `forward` (the turn order recomputes; auto-advance never fires on an edit, and no routine wakes on it — `onSessionEvent`). The session's owner presses them, never mid-run, the story's lane only (other channels untouched). Member copy: **Back** · **Forward** · _2 turns ahead_ · _2 turns ahead will be replaced if you write now._ · _There is nothing to go back to yet._ · _There is nothing ahead to bring back._ · _This is where this branch begins. To go further back, open the session it was branched from._ · _Only the session's owner can go back or forward._ · _Wait for the reply to finish._ ⚠ Not **On revision** (what a delete or retake of the latest turn does to the timeline), not a **branch** (which keeps both stories), not the clock step's **Forward** / **Back** (a direction, §25 _clock step_), not _retake_ (which deletes and plays the turn again). Never say _rewind_ to a member. |
| **replace on write** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-23 (RF fix 5).** Any new write while the session holds a forward stack deletes it for good (`discardForwardStack`, `messages/store.ts`): every new row (`insertLegacy`, `insertLegacyMany`), a reply, a regenerate, a swipe's new version or an extend (`runReply`), a press that passed its door (`fireAction`), a retake. The rows go through the store's one delete (what is still anchored to them goes with them; Back already took their state back), and the unread session changes about them go too. The ONE deletion of messages on by default; raises no event. A verb on a rewound row is refused (_That message was taken back with Back. Press Forward to bring it back first._). ⚠ Not a **deletion pipeline**'s work: nothing is dispatched. |
| **deletion pipeline** · **Deletion asked** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-23 (RF fix 5; owner: "Deletion requires a pipeline, so it's managed by the genre").** A message offers **Delete** only where the session's effective registrations hold an event pipeline on **`core:event/message-deletion-asked@1`** (`coreEvents.messageDeletionAsked`, `sessionEvents.messageDeletionAsked`; an action, declared root; carries session · message · actor · user; payload `core:shape/deletion-asked@1`, `DeletionAskedPayload` `{ sessionId, messageId, channel, person, cause }`; UI name _Deletion asked_) — `deletionOffered` (`messages/deletion.ts`). Core registers none: deletion is off everywhere by default. The press checks the door (the message is live and the session's, `canActOnMessage`, ⏳ `messageVerbs.delete: false` still subtracts, the kept-turn rule) and dispatches the event (`askDeletion`); the pipeline enters through **`core:inlet/message-deletion-asked@1`** (`C.messageDeletionAsked`, `DELETION_ASKED_INLET_ID`; ports `messageId` · `channel` · `person` · `cause`) and ends in **`core:outlet/delete-message@1`**, the **deletion outlet** — the only document besides the built-in's own where it may stand (`deletionPipelinePlaces`, `validate()` and the host), any owner, deleting only the message the event carried — handed to it whole on its **`asked`** port (`core:shape/deletion-asked@1`), wired from the inlet's `main` (`C.deleteMessage.v1({ asked: $.input.main })`; `validate()` holds `asked` to that one edge and refuses `target` there, the built-in's own spec's port); one transaction: the one retraction rule, then the row; its new `taken` port counts what went (`takenSummaryOf`). ⚠ Not `message-deleted` (the fact after the write), not **replace on write**, not Hide. Member copy: _Deleting messages is off in this session. Hide it from the story instead, or use Back to take back the last turn._ |
| **Hidden from the story** 🚧 | **Member copy, 2026-10-23 (RF fix 5).** What a hidden message (`messages.is_hidden`) is called: the badge _Hidden from the story_, its tooltip _the characters no longer read this line. What it changed stays._ Hide retracts nothing: the line was said; only the model no longer reads it. ⚠ Not Back, which takes a turn and what it changed out of the story. |
| **host state** · **Where and when** · **tool state** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-23 (RF fix 8; owner: "location and the story clock are host world state, not attributes").** What the host keeps of a session beside the rules' attributes — **never an attribute**: never on a sheet among them, never a carry switch, never counted in fit. Roles (`HOST_STATE_ROLES`): **place** and **time** — together **Where and when**, a sheet's row of its own (`stats.where`; the story clock as `SessionStateV1.storyTime`) and the prompt's place and time words (_The scene is at …_) — ⏳ **carried**: what someone carries, the host's carried zone kept as the `inventory` list for Story and the Lair (each character, the world, each place), whose reckoning hands the lorebook's items out on it with their supply checked, drawn as a list under a sheet (`stats.carried`, never hidden) until those item lines write the zone itself — and **tool**: what a genre's own pipelines keep for their tools (the Lair's whisper and direction, the crawl's standing order, fate, death saves, difficulty, goal and ⏳ piece lists), drawn in a block of its own under a sheet unless a Stats copy sets **The game's own state** to _Hidden_ (`toolState`, default _Shown_). Stored as slot values as before (anchored, earshot kept). SDK `hostState.ts`: `HostStateDecl { slot, role, owners?, genres }`, `declareHostState` (core's catalogue, `CORE_HOST_STATE`, `registry/hostState.ts`), `hostStateFor(genre)` (the world's place wherever `shape.scenes.place` is `HOST_PLACE_KEY`), `hostStateRoleOf`, `isHostStateSlot`, `HOST_PLACE_SLOT_ID`; `TrackedSlot.hostState`, `SessionStateSlotV1.hostState`. A package's tools use annex fields. ⚠ Not an **attribute** (the rules'); not an **annex field**; not a **host fact** (a registration's `when`). |
| **plays best with** · **expectation** 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-23 (RF fix 8; owner: "genres can expect certain attributes, shapes, zones … but we won't lock someone into using their own conventions").** What a genre names in `uses` — `attributes` · `entryTypes` · `zoneTypes`, each a `UsesExpectation { tag, kinds?, label, why }` (an attribute's `kinds` its fitting attribute kinds), required or `optional` — met where the rules say that tag (an attribute's id counts; the host's carried zone is tagged `inventory`, `ZoneTypeDecl.tags`), else **told in words**: it lowers the **ruleset fit** rating, never makes it Incompatible. `rulesetFit(...).inWords` (rows `attribute` · `entry-type` · `zone-type` with `label`, `why`), `rulesetProvides(...).attributeTags` / `.zoneTags`, `playsBestWith`, `playsBestWithLine` (_Plays best with a health-like number and …_); the start form's Rules card shows the line (`GenreRulesOffer.playsBestWith`) and the chosen rules' whys (`fit.inWords`). Member copy, never the machinery's words. ⚠ Not a requirement, not a lock. |
| **time a function counts on** (`countsTime`) · **time a genre keeps** (`keepsTime`) 🚧 | **Built 2026-11-11 (PLAN-sensible-engine §2.12, lane sense-age; owner: "and it should be a measurable against ruleset compatibility").** Which time a function module counts on — `FunctionProps.countsTime`: `'story'` (the story clock) · `'real'` (real elapsed time) · `'both'`; left out, neither; content inside the function's hash; an unknown value is the finding `bad-counts-time`. Core's `scheduled`, `deadline` and `obligation` say `'story'`; `recurring` with `every: 'hour' | 'day'` is read as story (its declaration is unchanged: what it counts on depends on its option). A ruleset's need is the union of its functions'. Which time a genre keeps — `GenreDecl.keepsTime`: `'story'` (Story, the Lair, the Dungeon Crawler) · `'real'` (the Guide, Chat) · `'none'`; refused by `genre()` otherwise. `rulesetFit` weighs the two when the genre says `keepsTime`: a time the rules count on that the genre does not keep lowers a better rating to **Poor** with one sentence (_its rules count story time, and this genre runs on real time: they would never move_) and names it in `RulesetFit.timeUnmet`; Incompatible keeps its own reason. The app's genre fit lets a genre with `keepsTime` and no `uses` (the Guide, Chat) speak only then. ⚠ Not the ruleset's **time section** (rests and time units); not **host state**'s time role (the clock itself, never counted in fit as an attribute); never bare _time_ (R3). ⚠ Not a lock: a rating and a sentence (genres expect, never lock). 🚧 The fact a body is handed — how long since a value was last written — is built (lane sense-age2): `writtenAgo` on an attribute role, `{ minutes, realSeconds? }` per attribute id, `realSeconds` only for `countsTime` `'real'` / `'both'`; counted from the `attribute_values.story_clock_*` stamp (the writing session's clock), with `realNow` on the run's facts. ⚠ Not `elapsed` (the moment's story time passed), not the `stat-trail` `since`. |
| **option role** · `unknown-way` 🚧 | **Built 2026-10-23 (RF fix 8 — RF fix 6 ★2/★3).** An option in a function's form that names something of the ruleset's (`FunctionProps.optionRoles`, `FunctionOptionRole { names: 'value' \| 'function', kinds? }`): a **value** it reads — a way's `modifierOf` / `poolOf` / `opposedBy`, a spend's `resource`, a check's `base` (an attribute of number kinds, a number entry field, a worked-out value's key; a word or free text is refused `bad-binding-kind`) — or one of the ruleset's **functions** by key (a check's `way`, an outcome's `check`; naming none is refused **`unknown-way`**, `FunctionRefContext.functionKeys`). Stored where they always were. ⚠ Not a **function binding** (a role bound in `bindings`). |

### Session data vocabulary 🚧 (pr-6, built 2026-10-25)

The words the pr-6 sprint (settle line, own book, archive, lore sources) and its sprint 2 (core runtime keys, the judged scene check, the session store, files-only storage; both 2026-10-25) build with. Every one is 🚧 until 0.7, like the rulesets vocabulary above: built, still free to move on contact with use. Each was grepped across `src`, the SDK and the schema on 2026-10-25; where a near-neighbour exists, the ⚠ says what the word is not (step 5).

| Term | Means |
| --- | --- |
| **settle line** 🚧 | How far a session's history is fixed: `sessions.settled_message_id` / `settledMessageId`, read with `settledLineOf` (which also counts every `done` scene) and moved with `settleThrough` (forward only, never past the forward stack, compacting in the same transaction), announced by `announceHistorySettled` as the event `history-settled@1`; on the session payload as `settledLine`, and on the conversation's dossier as `SessionDossierV1.settledThrough` (the dossier's spelling of the same line). A summary a person saved, a scene's applied summary, a lore write that carries `sources`, and 🚧 an **Apply** (through the newest applied item's turn, never past the message before the oldest item still held; 2026-11-12, lane sense-b2) move it; taking an Apply back never moves it back. ⚠ Not `settleSessionEvents` / `addSettleProbe` (test helpers that wait for the event queue to drain). |
| **settled** (history at or below the line) 🚧 | A message at or below the settle line, and a lore imprint (`lore_imprints`) compacted to status `settled`. Back refuses below the line with `SETTLED_SENTENCE` (= `REWIND_REFUSALS.settled`) by throwing `SettledRefusal`; `assertRetractable` is the one guard the retraction entry points ask; `markImprintsKept` keeps the imprints of a person's own edit. ⚠ Collides with `messages.status = 'settled'` (a finished generation, `projectLegacy.ts`): always qualify — _settled history_, _a settled imprint_ — never the bare _settled_. |
| **history.settle** 🚧 | `GenreDecl.history.settle`: `'on-write' | 'on-commit'` (`HistorySettle`, `historySettleOf`, `sessionHistorySettle`, `settleOnWrite`). `'on-write'` keeps every turn as it is played, so Back is refused with `EVERY_TURN_KEPT_SENTENCE` (= `REWIND_REFUSALS.everyTurnKept`). ⚠ The one lock a preset cannot loosen (`preset()` refuses a `history` key). |
| **anchor swap** 🚧 | The commit-time move of an attribute value from its session anchor onto the timeline (history entry, branch, `source_*`), keeping `session_id` so session-scoped owners never leak across sessions. Done by `settleThrough`. |
| **turn unit** 🚧 | The one definition of "the last turn" for every genre: `turnUnitOf(db, sessionId, { includePersonLines })`, `turnUnitAt`, `TurnUnit`, `TurnUnitVerdict`, `ReplayedLine.turnOf`, `ReplayedLine.userId` (the table-of-players rule counts people by account, so one person switching persona is one person); every branch floors `unitRuns` at the unit's first message id, and a run's yield joins the unit only when that run CREATED a unit row (a rewriting run stays in `runs`, its older yield does not); with `keepLaterState` and `takeRunWritesElsewhere` (rewind.ts), and the scene boundaries a retraction moves (`SceneBoundaryTaken`, `takeSceneBoundariesAt`, `restoreSceneBoundaries`). Back takes a whole turn unit; Regenerate takes the same unit without the person's lines. |
| **`sessions:refresh`** 🚧 | The member push: `Sockets.Sessions.Refresh`, carrying the newest `REFRESH_ROWS` (100) live rows and `Refresh.Response.coversFromId`, narrowed per member (`buildSessionRefresh`, `withSessionExtras`); the client merges it by row id (`mergeRefreshedRows`, `MergeableRow`, `client/sessions/store/refreshMerge.ts` — moved there from `components/sessionPage/` by pr-6 sprint 2: the merge is a store merge). ⚠ `sessions:get` stays the asker's own paginated reply. |
| **live history** 🚧 | `messages/liveHistory.ts` holds `liveMessageWhere` (re-exported by `messages/store.ts`), the one live-history predicate; the mirror column `messages.rewind_ordinal` makes it a column test. |
| **lore sources** 🚧 | The message ids a lore write was generated from: table `lore_sources` (`run_id`, `from`, `through` per subject); port `sources` on `create-lore-entry@1`, `update-lore-entry@1`, `link-lore-entries@1` and `graph-proposal@1`; shape `S.loreSources` (`core:shape/lore-sources@1`); `recordLoreSources`, `checkLoreSources`, `loreSourceIdsOf`; conformance law C39. Present = a generated write, which commits (moves the settle line); absent = a change. ⚠ Never the bare _sources_ (R2/R3): §7's retrieval _source_ and an exported package's _source_ are other things. |
| **`LoreMatch`** 🚧 | Port `match` on `create-lore-entry@1`: `{ entryId } | { name } | { key }` within the write's entry type (`loreMatch.ts`). The host finds or updates the entry; two candidates are refused, naming both. |
| **`bind`** (a lore outlet port) 🚧 | Port `bind` on `create-lore-entry@1`, a `character:<id>`: sets `anchor_binding_id` (the entry type's `anchor` role). ⚠ R2 names _binding_ a dangerous word: `bind` is only this port — not a pipeline binding, not a function binding. |
| **minAge** 🚧 | A registration option, a count of messages: `minAge` (`registrations.min_age`, `minAgeOf`, `DEFAULT_ROUTINE_MIN_AGE` = 20, `HostScope.minAge`); the host refuses a run whose span is younger (refusal tag `summary depth`). 0 for an action or an event. ⚠ A message count, never rounds (§23). |
| **channel lore role** 🚧 | `ChannelDecl.lore`: `story | aside | never`, read with `channelLoreRole`. ⚠ Never the bare _role_ (R2). |
| **`fileLore`** · **`rememberNote`** 🚧 | Core-catalog builders for a lore write (`core-catalog/src/shared/lore.ts`, exported from the package). |
| **`migrate`** (lifecycle moment) 🚧 | `migrate(fromVersion)`: `LifecycleMigrateInput`, `fireMigrate` (`plugins/lifecycle.ts`), `migrateAnnexOwner`, `migrateOwnerDocument`, `ownerVersionOf` (`plugins/annexMigrate.ts`). ⚠ Not a database migration (§19). |
| **the three events** 🚧 | `session-archived@1`, `scene-summary-applied@1` and `history-settled@1` (`sessionEvents.sessionArchived` …), in `CORE_EVENTS` and off the ledger. |
| **own book** (code) · **Session notes** (the interface) 🚧 | The lorebook a session owns (`lorebooks.session_id`), made at create, at a chat import and at a branch, Gregorian with its clock unset (`OWN_BOOK_CALENDAR`); `overlay_of` is the attached book. **Landed:** `Network` (Embeddings section icon) → **`Zap`**, and the defaults groups gained the `entities` kind with **`ScanText`** (§22, 2026-09-14) · `connections.model` (the column) → **legacy mirror of the default
model**, with the model itself moving to `connection_models` and every selection
becoming an **(endpoint, model) pair** (0114) · `SourceKind` → **band** · `project()` → **toCandidate** · _arm_ →
**mechanism** · `role` (entries) → **field role**, in prose · `grant` (models) →
**lease** · `lane` (specs, retrieval) → **gather branch** / **mechanism** ·
`runtime` (plugins) → **sandbox** · `capability` (plugins) → **permission** ·
`ContextBlock` → **`Allocation`**, with assemble's `blocks` out-port → **`allocations`** ·
`koboldcpp_models` (table) → **`local_models`**, with `koboldCppModels` →
**`localModels`** and `Select`/`InsertKoboldCppModel` → **`…LocalModel`**.

⚠ **The vendor name was the only vendor-specific thing about that table.** It
already had what a registry needs — `filename` unique, provenance, a download
`status`, and a trust ordering on what it claims — and embedding and NER models
need exactly that. One concept, one table, one scan protocol. It gained `format`
and `modality`; it deliberately did **not** gain an `engine`, because a `.gguf`
is not KoboldCPP's and a stored engine would go stale the day a backend is added
(`enginesFor` derives it instead).

⚠ **`kind` was kept, not collapsed into `modality`**, and the two are not
synonyms. **`kind`** (`text` · `image` · `unknown`) is a _loader lane_ — which of
koboldcpp's two directories opens the file, which is what a GGUF header read can
actually answer. **`modality`** is the _role_, in the vocabulary above.
Collapsing them would make that header read record `text-gen` at `detected` —
the top of the automatic trust order — for a BERT `.gguf`, whose architecture is
a language model and whose modality is `embeddings`. That is manufacturing a
measurement, so instead **one function projects one onto the other**
(`modalityForKind`) and every write site goes through it, which is what stops
two columns that mean different things from coming to disagree.

⚠ **What the _allocation_ pass could not reach, and why.** The type renamed; two
fields did not, and neither is a rename this pass was free to make:

- **`AllocatedContext.blocks` is the SDK's word at a seam, not ours.** The object
  rides the `context` port into the SDK executor, and `isAllocatedContext` — an
  **exported** predicate, so a third-party node may call it — recognises an
  allocated context by `Array.isArray(v.blocks)` and nothing else. Renaming the
  field leaves `receipt.preview.blocks` and `preview.totals` silently empty on
  every run (verified against a real preview turn: populated before, `[]` after)
  and breaks the predicate for every plugin. R5 applies — translate at the seam,
  never merge — and the seam's word is the SDK's. ⚠ The deeper problem underneath
  it is not a rename either: `sdk/src/wire.ts` exports **its own** `ContextBlock`
  and `AllocatedContext`, a _different shape_ under the same names, which the
  app's object satisfies only by accident. That wants its own pass.
- **`meta.retrieval.blocks`** is derived from the field above and typed in the
  socket contract. Moving it alone would give one array two names on one path, so
  it moves when the field does.
- **`pipeline_blocks` was a third live sense**, and the only one with a table: a
  spec's `each` / `gather` / `loop` / `junction` containers. **Ruled 2026-09-15: it is a
  _clause_** (§4). The table, `BuiltClause.kind` and the builder verbs say `clause` /
  `gather` / `each` / `junction` since 2026-09-16 (plans/29 R-14, 30 §U3).

⚠ **What the _arm_ pass could not reach, and why.** Three things still spell it,
and none of the three is a rename:

- **`semantic.arm.*` and `names.arm.*`** are node keys, so they are _declared
  config addresses_. Moving one is a **cull** (§6): `reconcileConfigs`
  hard-deletes the value with a notice, and stale `pipeline_node_overrides` rows
  survive it and need a hand-written `DELETE`. Worth doing — as a migration.
- **`foundBy: "arm0#3"`** is a value written into receipts. Changing it changes
  what already-stored receipts say.
- **The retrieval-explain labels** — "Both arms", "One retrieval arm found it" —
  are prose a user reads, so they are free to change but are a copy change and
  not a rename (§24.6).

⚠ **`arm64` is not an instance of _arm_.** A whole-word search for `arm` returns
CPU-architecture strings in the tunnel binary manager, where `"arm64"` and
`"arm"` are values matched against `process.arch`. Renaming them breaks platform
detection on ARM machines, and it breaks it at _download_ time — the failure is a
wrong binary, not a type error. **Any mechanical `arm` pass must exclude
`tunnels/`.** Recorded because the residual count looks larger than it is: of the
hits outside tests, the architecture strings are a meaningful share and none of
them are this word.

⚠ **What the _runtime_ pass could not reach.** Two things, and neither is a
rename this pass was free to make:

- **`plugins/RuntimeManager.ts` still exists**, as a re-export of
  `SandboxManager` carrying a tombstone. Two files under
  `pipelines/runtime/` — `pluginBindings.ts` and `pluginBindings.int.test.ts` —
  still import the old name from the old path and belong to another lane's tree.
  The shim is one line and its removal is one line on each side of that seam.
- **QuickJS's own `runtime` is not ours.** `qjs.newRuntime()`, `JS_FreeRuntime`
  and the per-call VM object keep the library's word. R5: translate at the seam,
  never merge — a `sandbox.dispose()` that is really a WASM VM teardown would be
  the merge this rule exists to stop.

⚠ **The one _capability_ sense the permission pass left alone.** Where the word
names the **object-capability machinery** rather than a thing an admin may deny
— the _capability bridge_ (QuickJS's async host-function transport), the _abort
capability_, the SDK's `sp-capability-guard` — it stays. Those are not "what
sandboxed code may do"; they are how anything reaches it at all, and a
"permission bridge" that also carries ambient host functions would be a worse
name, not a better one. Everything permission-gated — network, storage,
resources, events, and every grant derived from them — now reads _permission_.

### folio, `item.channel`, the channel strip — 2026-09-17 (plans/genres §2, U2)

Landed with the Writing Room, which is a showcase plugin since 2026-09-30
(`serene-pub-plugin-writing-room`; its own words — **manuscript**, **scribe**,
the `writing` family, the fields `pov` · `tense` · `chunkLength` ·
`authorsNote` and its action keys — live in that README). These three are
general and stay core's:

- **folio** — the channel **role** whose messages fold into one block of prose.
  Landed with R-C: _document_ was retired the day it landed (R1 — a _document_
  is a pipeline's stored spec), and _folio_ is the distinctive word (R2).
- **`item.channel`** — a published value on the message venue, beside
  `item.isNewest`. Which channel a row is on, so an action declared for one
  channel's messages can say so in an `enabled-when` predicate. Added because
  `venue.channel` — the declared way to say it — cannot be relied on yet: an
  action listing is built for ONE channel and the client asks for none.
- **the channel strip** — the composer's control for which channel the next
  message lands on. Not a _tab strip_: it does not switch panels, it switches
  where a message goes, and `docs/sessions.md` already used _tab strip_ for the
  composer's More panels.

### plugin widget id — 2026-09-17 (ruled the same day)

A plugin's own widgets — the ones it declares under ⏳ `surfaces.panels`, which
belong to no genre — are now seated in every session, and they are seated under a
**plugin widget id**: `<pluginId>:<panelId>`, composed by the SDK's
**`pluginWidgetId`** and read back by **`parsePluginWidgetId`**
(`sdk/src/surfaces.ts`). The app composes it once, at the boundary where a
stored manifest is read (`frameHost.surfacesOf`), so every reader past that line
— `sessions:view.modePanels`, `session_panel_layouts`, `widget_settings`,
`widget_styles`, a `surface:open` intent — names one string.

- **plugin widget id** — R3-qualified, because the bare _widget id_ is what core
  and a genre use and those stay **plain**. Only a plugin's is qualified, and
  only because a package's panel id is the one id nobody else controls: two
  packages each picking `map` pick one widget id, and a layout row outlives the
  install that could have told them apart. `:` is the separator on the pattern
  of `core:genre/chat`, and it is unambiguous by grammar — the plugin slug
  (§23) admits no colon and neither does the panel-id grammar
  `^[a-z0-9_-]+$`.
  ⚠ Not a _panel id_: the panel id is the bare half the package declared, and it
  is what the ⏳ `sessions:view.panels` row still carries.
- **`enabledPluginWidgetIds(db)`** (`server/plugins/frameHost.ts`) — the one
  answer to "is this plugin widget id real?", read from the stored manifests
  through **`pluginWidgetDecls(manifest, pluginId)`** (2026-09-29): a package's
  component widgets (`manifest.widgets`) and its ⏳ frame panels (through
  `surfacesOf`), each under its plugin widget id, with `maxInstances` when it
  is a number. `widgetStyles`'s `announcedWidgetIds` is its first reader.
- **`emitSurfaceIntent(…, pluginId?)`** — the emitting package's id, so a bare
  panel id it names is qualified server-side. A plugin may open its own widgets
  and nobody else's: an id prefixed with another plugin's is dropped (a drop,
  not a refusal — the whole verb is a proposal). Core and genre callers omit it
  and keep plain ids.

No migration, and nothing to migrate: no stored row has ever held a plugin panel
id, because they never mounted. `res.panels` is now explicitly ⏳ **remove at
0.7.0**. A disable deletes nothing — `sessions:view` simply stops listing the
plugin's widgets and the client draws them as missing, so a re-enable brings the
arrangement back. `announcedWidgetIds` refuses a NEW style for a disabled
plugin's widget while leaving the rows already made alone.

⚠ Two claims this falsified, both fixed in the same change: the
`FrameSurfaceDecl.settings` ⚠ in `sdk/src/surfaces.ts` said a `surfaces.panels`
declaration's settings never reach a frame (they do now — the genre loop in
`sessions:view` also never copied `p.settings`, so a genre's widget had the same
bug), and `userStyleSlug`'s uniqueness argument rested on "widget ids are
colon-free", which a plugin widget id is not. The argument survives on segment
count; the comment says so.

### contract · policy (of a definition) — 2026-09-17 (plans/31 V6, ruled the same day)

A node definition's content hash covers its **contract** — what a pinned spec
runs against — and nothing else; everything else on a `Descriptor` is
**policy**, what is offered or shown, stored on the registry row and never
hashed. _What is offered is policy; what runs is contract._ The SDK's
`definitionContract` / `definitionContractHash` compose and digest the
contract from a `Descriptor` or a `RegistryEntry` alike; the descriptor
registry's re-declaration guard and core's `pipeline_definition_registry`
pointer both call it, so the two answers to _is this the same definition?_
are one. `hash.ts` keeps its display denylist for every other registry.

- **contract (of a definition)** — §5. `DESCRIPTOR_CONTRACT_KEYS`. `review.fields`,
  `shape`, `earlyExit`, `liveRow`, `declaresRandomness` and `media` gained
  registry columns so a row read back reproduces its own pointer
  (`live_row`, `review`, `media`, and the existing `early_exit`,
  `declares_randomness`, `connection_kind`).
- **policy (of a definition)** — §5. `DESCRIPTOR_POLICY_KEYS`; `RegistryEntry.policy`
  and the `policy` jsonb column (migration 0150) carry `provisional ·
reviewDefault · timeoutMs · timeoutKind · toggleable`; `i18n` and `public`
  keep their own columns. `RegistryEntry.provisional` moved inside it.
- **provisional** — §5 amended: policy, not hashed. U6's "binding it
  republishes" is reversed; the row's `status` still derives from it.

Cost: every published definition republished once (112 pins in
`registryHashes.test.ts`; the id and version are contract and were never in
the material, so no pin could stay). Two definitions never share a hash now.
No spec document moves. The rename retry in `adoptCurrent` (0134) is gone:
a hash older than this build's material is kept beside the row as this
build reads it, never recomputed.

### one identity for an action — 2026-09-17 (plans/31 V2, ruled the same day)

An action had three keys: its `key`, its `function` (what routing resolved,
shareable across specs), and the identity `<spec slug>#<key>` the U5c passes
had already made the storage key. V2 keeps the identity alone. Bindings map
a **subject** — an identity, or a core event id for what core emits — to the
spec that serves it; a genre's enabled-when defaults, a session's override,
a preset's included set and the fire all key by identity; a slash name
means one action. _Function_ is retired (§23).

- **subject (of a binding)**, **binding (pipeline)** — §9, new rows.
  `pipeline_function_bindings` → **`pipeline_bindings`**, `function_key` →
  **`subject`** (migration 0151, a rename); pre-V2 rows re-keyed at boot
  (`boot/bindingSubjects.ts`: `respond` → `core:event/message-respond@1`, a
  bare key → its sole declarer, else dropped with a notice).
- **action** — §9 amended: the identity is the one key. `ActionDecl.function`
  is a one-release alias (`normalizeAction` reads it as `key`); `CORE_ACTIONS`
  are key-only; `GenreDecl.enabledWhen` is keyed by identity (`core#retry`,
  `core:spec/look#look`) and refuses a bare key; `slashCollisions` compares
  identities; a block's `fn` is the action's **key**.
- **slash name** — §9 amended: the same key under one name is a collision.
- SDK: `resolveFunctionVerdict/Spec` → **`resolveSubjectVerdict/Spec`**;
  `bindFunction` → **`bindSubject`**; `functionCandidates` →
  **`subjectCandidates`**; `EVENT_FOR_FUNCTION` deleted;
  `resolveSessionEventVerdict` gains the session's own binding as its first
  layer (the R-6 event half). Sockets: the **field** `function` retired for
  `action` / `key` (⏳ a bare key the door resolves) on `triggerFunction` and
  `setFunction`, `subject` on the binding pair; event names unchanged. The
  palette's `shared` row is gone with the alternatives it stood for.
- The `session_functions` bare-key fallback is retired (column name kept).
- ⚠ **R1 collision, pending the owner:** _binding_ now names both the cast
  link (§8) and the pipeline row (§9). Kept as the plan wrote it; flagged on
  both rows.

Cost: the compiled documents of every action spec lost one field, so the
Lair, Whodunit and Writing Room document pins moved once (their test files
record the old hashes). No definition hash moved.

### next-speaker strategy — 2026-09-21 (plans/19 §5 U-C5 closed; ruled the same day)

None of the genres' turn detection worked: the socket pre-picked every turn
with the 0.5 lookback rule, fed it to the run as an explicit pick, and every
strategy honours a pick — so the `speaker` node recorded the socket's guess,
the Turn order dropdown changed nothing, and planner-driven genres got a
character stamped on their narrator's placeholder row. Ruled: retire the
pre-pick and the column outright; plugins dictate the menu and may ship their
own detection as a script kind; round robin becomes once-per-turn-of-the-
person's.

- **next-speaker strategy** — §9, new row; **planner** amended.
- **group reply strategy** · **`nextSpeaker`** — §23, retired.
- SDK: `SessionShape.speakerStrategies` (replaces `nextSpeaker`);
  `PresetDefaults.speakerStrategy` (replaces `groupReplyStrategy`);
  `core:script:turn/select@1` (`turnSelect`, the `turn` content scope);
  `ctx.scripts.apply(point, value)` beside `applyText`; contracts
  `turnUserSplit` · `turnScripted`; respond, guide and writing-room specs
  seat `speaker` BEFORE `placeholder`, pinned `turnRoundRobin`, and the
  placeholder reads `$.speaker.*`.
- App: `runtime/speakerRotation.ts` (the rules, pure), `entities/speaker.ts`
  (`effectiveSpeakerStrategy` · `previewNextSpeaker` · `NEVER_DECIDES`),
  `speakerNodePin`, `listSpeakerStrategies(db, genreId?)`,
  `ReplyTurn { kind: 'respond' }` with nobody named, `ReplyOutcome.nobodyDue`,
  `sessions:triggerGenerateMessage.nobodyDue`, `sessions:speakerStrategies`
  by `genreId`, `sessions:create.session.speakerStrategy`,
  `GetResponseOrder.{known, speaker}`; migration 0152 (rebinds from the
  column, then drop); `getNextCharacterTurn.ts` and `GroupReplyStrategies.ts`
  deleted.

Cost: every respond/create document pin moved (the shape rides in them) and
the respond spec was edited in place under the freeze, content-addressed.
Three definition hashes added, none moved.

| **one primary row** / **one write per pipeline** (F7, F37, C21 — 09-B B4, R-17) | **one live row** per run (W1, owner R44 2026-09-23): the live row is a placeholder or claimed row, never a complete message; other writes, complete messages included, unlimited and allowed inside clauses; the live row never inside an `each`/`loop`; no second message on the live row's channel (validator for a literal channel, host `racesLiveRow` for a wired one). _Primary row_ survives only in comments on create → update pairs. |
