| _(new)_ — private messages words (PLAN-private-messages-2026-10-12; owner rulings Q1–Q7 the same day) | **conversation** — one private room between people on a pub: `conversations` (`kind` direct · group; a **direct conversation** is two people, unnamed, one per pair by `pair_key`; a **group conversation** is named and has a **host**, `host_user_id`, who renames and manages members and passes to the oldest member on leaving), `conversation_members` (`last_read_message_id` is the one unread marker; `muted_at`), socket family `conversations:` (list · open · create · send · edit · remove · read · rename · addMembers · removeMember · leave · mute · people · attachable · person; pushes `message` · `changed`), client context `contexts/conversations.svelte.ts`, view key `conversations`. Plain word by ruling: the session-side `conversation` store and `ConversationDossierV1` keep their names; context tells them apart. ⚠ Not a **session**, not a **channel lane**, never _chat_ (§23). · **message** (in a conversation) — `conversation_messages` (qualified because `messages` is a session's pipeline-shaped line in the same schema; body is markdown under the STRICT profile, `CONVERSATION_BODY_MAX` 8,000; a removed one is a **tombstone**, `deleted_at`, reading _Message removed_). · **attachment** (in a conversation) — a session, character, lorebook or file carried with a message: `conversation_attachments` (`kind`, `subject_id` with no FK by the media provenance rule), the **Attach** button and picker, `ConversationAttachmentCard`; gated for every member at send (`conversations/gate.ts` `canAttach`) and per reader at open (`available: false` → _Not shared with you_ / _No longer available_). | a new entry Apply moved filed no record; `batch` was null with entries only | every moved entry and every link that moves with it files an `apply` `lore_imprints` record (`field` NULL) whose `cause.moved` keeps its prior `lorebookId`, `branchId`, `position`, `anchorBindingId`, `anchorEntryId` (and the entry's `updatedAt` after the move); `batch` is set whenever anything was applied | `ownBook.ts` |
| _(internal)_ `takeBackApply` undid held changes only, and had no socket | 🚧 **Take back** (UI, the card's **Applied to the lorebook** list): one whole Apply, all or nothing — entries and links back where they were, fields back, changes held again; refuses in a sentence when the entry is edited, amended, filed under, linked to, named by a history day or by another session's story, carries another session's values, or is a place | `sessions:takeBackApply`; `docs/lorebooks.md` |
| a held change the lorebook already read was a conflict (a branch's copy of what its original applied) | 🚧 **done**: not listed, dropped by every Apply; a change waiting on the session's own earlier change says so 🚧 *An earlier change from this session to ‹label› is still waiting; apply it first.* | `ownBook.ts` `heldChangeVerdict` |
| _(new)_ | 🚧 sockets `sessions:appliedBatches` (SCOPED by `sessionId`) and `sessions:takeBackApply`; `sessions:overlayItems` SCOPED by `sessionId`, its response gains `mayApply` (the reader owns the lorebook) and `appliesItself`; `TakeBackApply.Response.refused` (a refusal said in place, never an `:error`); a record's `cause.automatic` (`scene-close` · `scene-summary` · `close-out`) and `cause.sceneId` beside `cause.by` | `shared/sockets/types.ts`, `shared/sockets/interest.ts`, `client/sockets/typedSocket.ts` |

### The own-book route: links across two books, history days, reading and Apply — 2026-11-12 (owner rulings S3 "Only Apply settles", Stage B questions; PLAN-sensible-engine §5.9 step 4 item 8; lane sense-b3)

Under **Full** and for a session whose lorebook is its notes alone: unchanged | `pipelines/runtime/host.ts`, `pipelines/runtime/loreMatch.ts`, `sessions/branch.ts`, `lorebooks/ownBook.ts`; `docs/lorebooks.md`, `docs/session-actions.md`, SDK `guides/storage.md`, `outlets.ts` JSDoc |

| the check "does the lorebook hold this day" was written at each site | 🚧 one function, `lorebookDayOfDate` (`scenes/historyEntryOfDate.ts`) | `historyEntryOfDate.ts`, `ownBook.ts` |
| the overlay's items were `entry` and `entry-change` | 🚧 a third item kind, **`link`** (a link whose ends are both the lorebook's), and a held history paragraph as an `entry-change` carrying **`notesEntryId`** (the own-book day that holds it; `amendmentId` absent); Apply's params gain **`linkIds`** and its result **`appliedLinks`** (links moved), **`mergedDays`** (own days merged onto the lorebook's day, the own day's id), **`droppedLinks`** (links the lorebook already said) and **`heldDays`** (`{ notesEntryId, reason }`: days left because merging would make a link say the same thing twice); an Apply record's **`cause.standalone`** (a link moved by itself) and **`cause.merged`** (a merged day's before-image and what was repointed). Take back returns a link, and a merged day while its paragraph is still the day's last | `lorebooks/ownBook.ts`, `shared/sockets/types.ts`, `server/sockets/sessions.ts`; collisions: none in either repo for the new names (`linkIds` was already a local name in tests and `sessions.ts`, never a published one) |

### The flip: where scenes end by themselves, the own book takes a pipeline's writes — 2026-11-12 (owner rulings 2026-11-12; lane sense-b4)

| Was | Is | Why/where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| under **Full** a pipeline's new entry, place (room), history day or link was written straight to the lorebook for every session; only **Review changes**, **Off** and a book someone else owns sent them to the own book | for a session that reads an attached lorebook **and whose scenes end by themselves** (it runs the *Find where scenes begin* routine, not Off, and its scene mode is **Automatic**: Story's Living and Rule Based presets, the Lair, the Dungeon Crawler; not Story's Minimal preset, not Chat) those four kinds are kept in the own book **whatever the write mode, Full included**, and read at once with the lorebook, notes first (places list, map, retrieval, keyword match, names list, the Lair's room flows); a turn owns them (swipe, regenerate, Back, delete take them, Forward returns them) until **Apply**; `create-lore-entry`, `update-lore-entry` and `link-lore-entries` results carry `route: "own-book"` and the own book's `lorebookId` (values only, shape unchanged); every other session writes as before | the owner's flip 2026-11-12: a story's world waits for its owner's say, not only a review session's; §24 **own book** row, §8 **held amendment** row, SDK `guides/storage.md`; 🚧 `scenesEndByThemselves` (`lorebooks/ownBook.ts`, exported) is the one test |
| a summary written with `sources` moved the settle line ("Back stops at …") for every session | for such a session a summary with `sources` no longer settles; **Apply** does ("Only Apply settles"); other sessions unchanged | S3 "Only Apply settles"; 🚧 the `scenesEndByThemselves` field on the host-internal `sessionLoreWriteTo` result carries the answer |
| a branch session riding its parent's line forked its own line on its first lorebook write | for these kinds it forks at its **first Apply** (pressed or automatic), inside the Apply, so an Apply with nothing to apply forks nothing; a cast version, a value, a summary's save, a person's own entry and a scene compile still fork on their first write | lines (`docs/lorebook-time.md`) |
| automatic Apply skipped a branch session | a branch's changes reach its own line by themselves as scenes close | the first Apply is where its line is made |
| a ruleset tie or rules field for a room was written to the lorebook under **Full** | for a room that lives in the notes they are written in the notes (they follow the row); 🚧 `annexWriteBookOf` (`host.ts`) names the book an annex write lands in; 🚧 `Routing.ownBookId` (`rulesets/ties.ts`) | ties follow the row |
| _(none)_ | Unchanged: stat values, timeline captures, cast versions and the lorebook annex route; while a new history day waits in the notes those are still dated by the lorebook's latest day (★, accepted). No new table, column, migration, setting or published name | |

## 26. Shell

The app-wide frame around every page (ruled 2026-09-15, built the same day). Vocabulary is
user-facing: these words appear in labels, docs and code alike.

| Term             | Means                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **pub**          | One installation of Serene Pub as a person meets it: the app running on someone's computer, phone or home server, with everything saved in it. _Your pub_, _this pub_, _everyone on this pub_; **Pub settings** (Admin's **Pub** group), **Pub theme**, **Pub default**. Lowercase in prose, capitalised only where a sentence or label starts (STYLE-GUIDE §10). ⚠ Not a **widget instance** (§9), not a KoboldCPP/Ollama process, not _the server_ (the Node process, which logs and failures still name). Retires _instance_ / _server_ / _installation_ in this sense (§23). Code says _pub_ too (`scope_kind 'pub'`, `isPubTheme`, `ScopeAddress.kind 'pub'`, the SDK settings scope `'pub'`, renamed 2026-10-02); `system_settings` keeps its name. |
| **rail**         | The one navigation strip on the left edge. Its entries are **rail items**. ⚠ Not a _nav bar_, not a _sidebar_.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **sidebar**      | The single 400px column beside the rail that shows one **sidebar view** at a time. There is one; "left/right sidebar" is retired.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **sidebar view** | What a rail item opens: Characters, Models, Admin… Code: `view`, `activeView`, `openViews`. ⚠ Never _panel_ — a panel is an area session widgets inhabit (§9).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **detail**       | The read-only screen for one item inside a sidebar view, shown beside the list at desk width: "open the character's detail". Code keeps the legacy file names `*ViewPanel.svelte`; prose never says _panel_ here.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **list column** | The left column of a sidebar view that holds its **items**: `PanelSplit`'s list pane, 340px (380px where rows carry faces or cards), the **view toolbar** pinned above the rows. Sessions, Characters, Library, Users, Tags, Help, Models, Connections, Sampling (since 2026-10-10; off the rail and back the same day 2026-10-11, §23). Beside the **detail** at desk width; below 900px it fills the view and an opened item replaces it. Every list column fills the whole view at desk until something opens (`listFills`, centred at `fillWidth`: `list` 560px for rows, `reading` 1120px for cards, `whole` for the Library's grid; Models' and Connections' alone until 2026-10-24, PLAN-0-5-polish-parity L7). ⚠ Not a **section list**, which holds places, not items. (2026-10-09) |
| **section list** 🚧 | The 240px column of a sidebar view's places (its sections) at desk width: Settings, Admin, a lorebook's scopes (Sampling became a **list column** 2026-10-10). `SectionList`: a `nav` of links or buttons with `aria-current`, rows grouped under `ListGroupLabel`s, an optional head and foot. Below 900px it fills the view and a chosen section replaces it, under a `PanelNavHeader` whose back returns to it. ⚠ Not the **rail** (the shell's strip of rail items), not a tab strip (`PanelTabStrip` is for tabs inside a detail), not a **list column** (which holds items). Replaces Settings' vertical tab list, Admin's own list and `LoreRail` (2026-10-09). 🚧 Provisional until a second release has used it (§25, 2026-10-09). |
| **atmosphere**   | An animated background layer that paints with the theme's roles and sits under a screen's content: rain, snow, mist, glyph rain, a candle's glow. Code: `src/lib/client/atmospheres/`, ids `core:atmosphere/<slug>`, registry `ATMOSPHERES`, component `AtmosphereLayer`. Today only the login screen, one at random per load. ⚠ Not a _background_ (a session's image, §9) and not an _effect_ (pipeline kinds are effect classes, §4). A computed still scene, if built, is a **backdrop**, never an atmosphere. 🚧 Provisional until a second surface adopts it. |
| **tab**          | An opened sidebar view kept mounted while another shows; marked by a dot at the end of its row in the **wide rail** (the narrow rail draws none since 2026-10-11), whose title says _still open_. Not a UI tab strip.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **width**        | How wide a sidebar view is shown: **Dock** (the 400px sidebar, beside the page), **Half** (half the room right of the rail, beside the page; reached by dragging the view's **edge**, which snaps to Dock, Half or Focus) or **Focus** (over the page, which stays mounted). Code: `ViewWidth`, `panelsCtx.viewWidth` / `setViewWidth`, `shellPrefs.dockWidth` (which of Dock/Half a view comes back at), `fullPageView` (the view in Focus). Focus owns the view's **address** (`/characters`, `/lorebooks`…, `viewRoutes.ts`) through shallow routing, so Back steps down a width. Replaces _full page_ (2026-09-26). |
| **Jump**         | The one search: the **Jump pill** (top-right entry point), the **Jump overlay** (input + results), the **scope chip** (what it searches), **jump scope** (`view` / `route` / `manual`), and **jump kind** / **jump hit** (§25 ledger row). A **wire jump kind** is served by `jump:search`; a **client jump kind** (`doc`, ruled 2026-09-16) is produced by the client from data it already holds and never crosses the wire. One vocabulary, two producers.                                                                                                         |
| **wide rail**    | The rail with its **navigation titles** shown: 208px, the wordmark, a label per item, group names **Play** and **Tune**. Toggled by the user; `panelsCtx.railWide`, `localStorage serene-pub:railWide`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **Library**      | The sidebar view that browses the community character library (`library`, `/library` in Focus) and imports into Characters. Characters only: there is no persona shelf. ⚠ Not the **pipeline library** (`/pipelines/library`), and not "your library" meaning the characters you have (§9).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Characters** 🚧 | The sidebar view (rail item in **Play**, `Icons.UsersRound`, key `characters`, `/characters` in Focus; `CharactersSidebar.svelte`) that lists **one row per character** (owner 2026-11-05): one of your character cards with every cast member linked to it, a card shared with you, someone else's card that a lorebook you can read uses, or a cast member with no card. Paged by 🚧 `characters:page` (**Load more**; re-asked on `characters:list` pushes); rows drawn by 🚧 `CharacterRowItem`. A card's row wears one badge, **Card** (its tags behind the `+N`); the meta line's lead is the summary (a shared card's _From ‹owner›_) and its fact the **reach line** (_Not in a lorebook yet_ · _In ‹book›_ · _In ‹session›'s notes_ · _In N lorebooks_). Groups: your rows, your folders, **Only in lorebooks**, **Shared with you**. Filters: Favorites · Personas · a tag, then the **Card** · **Words** · **Lorebook** · **Story** groups and the **In my stories** switch (members kept only in your sessions' notes). A cast member's row opens the member in Lorebooks; **Copy to my characters** where the card isn't yours or there is none. Named by ★C-1 (owner 2026-11-08), reversing ruling 12's _Character cards_ for the view only (§23). ⚠ Not **character card** (the item, a library card) and not the **Library** (community cards). |
| **bottom bar**   | The rail's form under the `lg` breakpoint: Home, Sessions, Characters, Lorebooks, Views.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **Views sheet**  | The sheet the bottom bar's Views item opens: the open views first (a phone has no rail to carry their dots), then every other rail item. Code keeps `isMobileMenuOpen`. Replaces _More sheet_ (2026-09-26).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Activity**     | The sidebar view (rail item at the foot, Bell) that holds the person's **notifications** (§25, 2026-09-28) in three sections: **Waiting on you** (open rows), **In progress** (running and awaiting-review job cards), **Earlier** (cleared rows); administrators also get its **LLM queue** tab. Its rail dot is the worst level among UNREAD notifications (red `error`, gold `attention`; `info` lights none; a job card is never counted — a finished job raises its owner an `activity-ready` / `activity-failed` row, 2026-09-28, and counts through that), and on a phone the Views button carries the worse of the Activity and Admin dots, counts in its aria-label. `ActivitySidebar.svelte`. |
| **spine**        | The 56px strip on the right of a view in Focus over a session: the cast, an ember dot while a reply is being written, and the way back. On a phone it is the **return bar** at the top of a view's sheet. Only drawn when a page is underneath.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Full screen**  | Ctrl/⌘+Shift+F, the header's Full screen button or the phone ⋯ item: the app header, the rail, the bottom bar and the sidebar step aside and, since 2026-11-05, the session shows the WHOLE **opening zone** (`openingZone`; no zone switch; the other zones stay mounted, `display: none`; `fullscreenActive`, `placementRules.ts`). A per-viewer, per-session stored choice (`useSessionFullscreen`, `FULLSCREEN_PREF_KEY`); `panelsCtx.fullscreen`; `data-fullscreen` on the shell root is the flag a page reads. The corner control `FullscreenExit` ("Exit full screen", Esc) is the way out. |
| **furled header** | The session header rolled up by its own quiet toggle (top right), per device: the bar alone rolls up (the layout's top strips went with the strips, 2026-11-05), and a small tab at the middle of the top edge brings them back (the Jump pill steps out too). `shellPrefs.headerFurled`. ⚠ Not **full screen**, which hides the header too, with the rail, the sidebar and every side. |
| **folder**       | A user-made group of characters in the Characters sidebar view (ruled 2026-09-15): flat, no nesting, a character sits in one folder or none, a folder holds only characters. `character_folders` + `characters.folder_id`. ⚠ Not a **tag** (a tag is a many-to-many label); not the message model's container metaphor, whose schema comment now says _envelope_.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Messages**     | The sidebar view (rail item in **Play**, `Icons.Mail`, key `conversations`, `/messages` in Focus, `/messages/<id>` on one conversation, `/messages/people/<id>` on a **person detail**) that holds a person's private **conversations** with other people on the pub (§25 _private messages words_, 2026-10-12). Shown once accounts are on and `system_settings.messaging_enabled` is true; never on Android. Its rail dot is primary while any conversation is unread, count in the aria-label; the phone's Views button carries it. `ConversationsSidebar.svelte`. ⚠ Not the **messages** widget (§9, a session's log), and not Activity, which holds the notifications a new message also raises. |
| **Apps** 🚧       | The sidebar view (rail item in **Play** after Sessions, `Icons.LayoutGrid`, key `apps`, `/apps` in Focus) of **applet cards**, one per plugin that offers an applet genre; registered only while at least one is listed (a cold `/apps` with none goes Home); a card opens the **launcher** `/apps/<pluginId>`. `AppsSidebar.svelte`. ⚠ "Apps" is a label only: "app" stays Serene Pub (§9); not the launcher itself and not Sessions (§25 **applet**, **Apps view**). |
| **view toolbar** | The top of a sidebar view's list: the **action row** (the view's one labelled primary, secondary icon buttons, `⋯`), the **find row** (filter box, filter popout, list/card pair) and the **chips row** (picks and narrowings in force). `ViewToolbar`. ⚠ Not `PanelToolbar`, an action group inside a panel. |
| **advanced controls** 🚧 (UI **Show advanced controls**) | **Built 2026-11-10 (owner GO; PLAN-advanced-controls-2026-11-10, lanes adv-A…D, adv-F).** **Purpose:** keep everyday surfaces short — one per-user switch that leaves out the controls only a power user reaches for. **Why:** P3 (few settings, no admin for everyday use) and P4 (power controls are purposeful). **Owns:** the switch (Settings › User, the first card; help _More choices on sessions, lorebooks and characters. Off keeps the everyday ones._) and its **`AdvancedHiddenLine`** (below). **Not:** a permission — it never shows what a role hides; the admin views (Admin, Sampling, Models, Loadouts, Connections, Pipelines, Rulesets), which it leaves untouched; the **Advanced fold** (★E-2) or `advanced: true` on a FieldDecl (ruled 2026-10-19, §5-2), both unchanged and shown in both modes (R1: the switch never acts on them). **Code names:** column `user_settings.show_advanced_controls` (boolean NOT NULL default false, migration `0149_familiar_silk_fever`); wire `showAdvancedControls` on `userSettings:get`; event `userSettings:updateShowAdvancedControls` `{ enabled }` → `{ success, enabled }`, error `userSettings:updateShowAdvancedControls:error`, handler `userSettingsUpdateShowAdvancedControls` (`server/sockets/userSettings.ts`), types `Sockets.UserSettings.UpdateShowAdvancedControls` (`shared/sockets/types.ts`); account-wide, so not in `SCOPED_EVENTS`; client helper `showsAdvancedControls(settings)` (`client/advancedControls.ts`, `settings?.showAdvancedControls ?? false`). **Data upgrade:** `dataUpgrades/0149_familiar_silk_fever.ts` copies `show_all_character_fields = true` into it once (a second boot changes nothing); the 0.5.3 attic restore (`attic/etl/accounts.ts`) does the same. **Off hides:** _session start_ — the rules choices (**Play it with**, a starter's rules, **Start blank** and its rules list, the in-words list) and **How strict**, the adopted-rules sentence and the preset hint staying as text; _session edit_ (Settings tab) — Actions, How replies are made, On revision, Rules options, Pipelines, Retake ask, Session data, and makes **Where this session's story stands** read-only (**`lockedByAdvanced`**); _session view_ — core's _Branch from here_ (**`ActionListDeps.advancedControls`**), the full-screen control's _Customize layout_ (the header's **Layout** and its phone menu's _Customize layout_ are drawn for everyone since owner 2026-11-12), the Author's note widget's depth, interval and _Sent as_ (**`ViewerV1.advancedControls`**); _characters_ — the fields _Show all fields_ used to add; _lorebooks_ — the entry tuning fold (`EntryAdvancedFields`), Book settings' Rules and Calendar, the **Graph** and **Lives** lenses (**`lensesShown`**), _See in graph_ and the _Build graph_ buttons. Kept in both modes: the session preset switch, the lorebook choice, starter lorebooks, creation modes, start asks, the session settings form (Advanced fold included), _Writes from sessions_, the story's present. Behaviour: `docs/themes-and-settings.md#show-advanced-controls`. **Hidden never means changed** — a hidden control keeps its value and still acts; this is a preference, never a permission. _Replaces **Show all character fields** (§23)._ |
| **`AdvancedHiddenLine`** 🚧 | **Built 2026-11-10 (owner GO; PLAN-advanced-controls-2026-11-10, lane adv-A; drawn by lanes adv-B, adv-D, adv-F).** The one muted line (`text-surface-600-400 text-xs`) at the foot of a form that hid something for this viewer: _Some controls are hidden._ then a quiet `button.anchor` **Show advanced controls** that emits `userSettings:updateShowAdvancedControls { enabled: true }`. `AdvancedHiddenLine.svelte` (`client/components/`). Static: counts nothing, never toasts, no listener — the form redraws when the shell's `userSettings:get` updates. **Drawn by:** the session edit form's Settings tab foot, the start form (book pick and rules card), Book settings, the character form (not on Stats, Likeness, Speech), the entry editors (`EntryAdvancedFields`). **Not drawn:** in the lens track, the message menu, the session header or the Author's note widget. STYLE-GUIDE §6.21. ⚠ **Not a hidden line** — that is a message hidden from the story (STYLE-GUIDE §6.16 `messages.message-badge-hidden`); say _the line that says controls are hidden_, or use the code name. |

## 27. Documentation

The docs suite (ruled 2026-09-16, `~/.claude/plans/DESIGN-docs-suite.md`). One compiler, two
**profiles**, two hosts: pages are **rendered** at build time and both the app and
serenepub.com serve the rendered output. User-facing words appear in labels and the guides;
the rest is code.

| Term                 | Means                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **docs compiler**    | `@serene-pub/docs`, a workspace in the SDK repo beside `cli`. Markdown in the **docs dialect** in, **docs-dist** out. Content-agnostic; knows nothing about the app. ⚠ Not a generator — a generator _emits_ markdown, the compiler _renders_ it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **docs dialect**     | Markdown plus the compiler's fences: highlighted code, `playground`, `:::note` / `:::tip` / `:::warning` admonitions, captioned figures with `{w=N}`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **docs-dist**        | The compiler's output: `manifest.json`, `search.json`, `pages/<slug>.html`, converted assets. One per **docs profile**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **docs profile**     | Which sources one compile reads and where it writes them — `scripts/build-docs.js`, `buildDocs({ profile })`. Two: **app** (`app` + `sdk`, into `src/lib/generated/docs` + `static/docs/assets`, held to the page budget, the only one the Vite plugin builds) and **site** (`app` + `sdk` + `api`, into the gitignored `docs-site/`, `npm run docs:site`, copied whole by serenepub.com). ⚠ Not a **source** — a profile _selects_ sources. Qualify it: bare `profile` is already an image-generation profile schema and an evidence profile (§13).               |
| **guide**            | A hand-written page about the app (`docs/*.md`). The **source** `app`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **reference page**   | A page rendered from declarations — never hand-written. Two **sources**: `sdk` (the catalog, from a package's announcement — its genres with **the genre's defaults**, its presets as changes, its pipelines with what they suit, read and emit — then 🚧 the **events page**, _Events and what they carry_, from the SDK's event, action and cadence declarations (`renderEventsDocs`, 2026-10-21, A1), then the **laws**, from `@serene-pub/conformance`'s requirements) and `api` (the TypeDoc API reference, emitted by the SDK's own build into its gitignored `docs/generated/api`, slugged under `sdk/api`). Both carry the same banner and repo line. `api` is read by the **site** profile only — 2.4 MB of rendered HTML the app will not carry — and an unbuilt SDK checkout drops it with a warning rather than failing the compile. |
| **executed example** | An SDK example (`sdk-tests/examples/<slug>.example.ts`) whose source is shown verbatim, run at SDK build against the fixture host, and whose output is kept as a **golden** (§13). Built 2026-09-16; the app never runs one, it reads what the SDK build proved.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **banner**           | The per-source notice the compiler prepends to every page of a source — today the SDK's "plugins are a preview in Serene Pub 0.6 …" (reworded 2026-10-03 for 0.6.0-pr-1, and 2026-10-30 when plugins shipped on: _releases ship with them on (an administrator can turn them off with SP_PLUGINS_ENABLED)_). Emitted by the build, never written by hand, so no page can forget it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **playground**       | The interactive SDK code runner embedded in a page (`@serene-pub/playground`, classic scripts, an opaque-origin `allow-scripts` frame). It _runs in_ a **sandbox** (§12); it is not one, and is never called one. Built 2026-09-16.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **nav group** · **order group** | A **nav group** is one heading of the docs nav (`DocsManifest.nav[]`, a source + a group name + its slugs). A source's `order` is flat (one nav group, headed by the source's `group`) or a list of **order groups** (`{ group, pages }`), each its own nav group, so the `app` source fills **Start here** · **Guides** · **How-to** · **For power users** · **Reference and help** while `docs/` stays flat. ⚠ The nav group **Guides** is a subset of the **guides**: every page of the `app` source is a guide, whichever group it sits in.                    |
| **Help**                        | The rail item (`BookOpen`, §22) that opens the documentation as a sidebar view; `/docs/<slug>` is its Focus address and Document View's `/document-view/docs` its mirror. Its search box and **Jump** (§26) share one query; a heading is a `doc` hit.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| _(new, 2026-10-02)_ | **Roleplay - Living Scene** — a shipped reply prompt in the `core:task/build-template-context#prompts` pool, offered beside *Roleplay - Simple* and never a default. Adapted from an r/SillyTavernAI prompt (credit in the catalog row's comment); its rules are *turn as event*, *player authorship*, *committed beats*, *stop on the last action*. | A row name, not a concept: the pool and its vocabulary are unchanged. |
| _(new, 2026-10-16)_ — strict-model walk of Dungeon Crawler: a swipe on the opening scene ran a story round; the standing-order question read *Superseded* under the table line after it; a failed reply re-entered prompts as a bare `Narrator:` turn; a Retry wrote `Name: Ann.` twice; run cards named node keys | 🚧 **failed reply** (already the widget's _message-failure_) made a server fact: an error and no words — `isFailedReplySql` / `notAFailedReplySql` (`messages/failedReply.ts`), left out of every `session-history@1` window and the unplayed talk; `LastMessage.replyFailed` on a session card. **row no reply wrote** — `questionRowRefusal` widened: a rerun (retry · swipe · extend, and core's `swipe-message` new alternative) is refused on a row whose creating run (or root) is no reply spec of its genre; a card greeting (`isGreeting`) keeps its swipes. `RetractedState` · `restoreRetractedState` — a failed swipe puts back what its retraction took. **table line** does not move the **staleness head** (`stalenessHead` · `stalenessHeadOf`) and is said once (a verbatim repeat at the channel head is not written). `RunProgress.haltStep` — the halted step's heading (step label, else definition name); the card never shows a node key. `SidebarListItem.itemName` | Owner walk 2026-10-16. ⚠ _failed reply_ is not a _stopped_ row (`generationOutcome: 'stopped'`), whose partial stands. |

### Modder vocabulary

The words a modder learns first (R36: at most 25, raised to 28 by R59 on 2026-10-21 for
**registration**, **routine** and **cadence**; more needs the owner). The SDK's
`guides/vocabulary.md` gives each one sentence, one example and a link back here, and
`guides/your-first-plugin.md` uses only these words, linking any other canon term where it first
appears. Each word's entry here carries **📘**. The guide never redefines a word: where the two
disagree, this file wins and the guide is fixed. `sdk-tests/vocabulary.test.ts` holds this list
and the guide's equal, checks each mark, and fails on an unlinked canon term in the first-plugin
guide.

- **plugin** — §12.
- **genre** — §9.
- **spec** — §4.
- **node** — §4.
- **inlet** — §4, under **node kind**.
- **query** — §4, under **node kind**.
- **task** — §4, under **node kind**.
- **oracle** — §4, under **node kind**.
- **outlet** — §4, under **node kind**.
- **port** — §4.
- **node definition** — §5.
- **handler** — §4.
- **pin** — §9, under **swap**.
- **swap** — §9.
- **receipt** — §4.
- **event** — no entry of its own yet. The sense a modder means (an occurrence in a session,
  core's `core:event/…` or one a package declared and a write recorded) is stated in passing
  under **action** (§9) and in the custom-events row of §25.
- **action** — §9.
- **registration** — §4, under **Registrations, routines and cadences**.
- **routine** — §4, under **Registrations, routines and cadences**.
- **cadence** — §4, under **Registrations, routines and cadences**.
- **declared setting** — §9.
- **annex** — §9.
- **turn order** — §9.
- **turn strategy** — §9, under **turn pool** · **turn orderer** · **turn strategy**.
- **widget** — §9.
- **component** — §9.
- **host element** — §9.
- **conformance** — no entry of its own yet. The kit's words are in §25 (_package conformance
  words_, 2026-09-26) and under **verdict** (§4).

## 28. Rulesets in the interface 🚧

Proposed 2026-10-16 with the rulesets vocabulary (§24). **The client never shows an SDK noun**
— _ruleset_, _mechanics_, _rigour_, _repertoire_, _piece_, _compendium_, _bridge_, _parked_,
_bestow_, _render depth_, _primer_, _own book_, _table channel_. Players see the plain
words below; ids and SDK nouns appear only where an administrator reads a pipeline's internals
(the Pipelines view, the run inspector), which already show node ids, and in **Admin › Rulesets**
(the row below). A label here may differ
from its SDK noun but never contradicts it (§24 step 6). Copy follows STYLE-GUIDE §10.

### The vocabulary test (written 2026-10-22)

`src/lib/client/rulesetVocabulary.test.ts` (Vitest, node environment), in the style of the SDK's
`sdk-tests/vocabulary.test.ts`:

1. **Files.** Every `src/lib/client/**/*.svelte`, read as text. Excluded by path, each with its
   reason in the test: the Pipelines view and run inspector (`components/pipelines/**`,
   `admin/sections/pipelines/**`), which show spec internals to administrators, and Admin ›
   Rulesets (`admin/sections/rulesets/**`), whose name is the admin exception above and whose
   ids are shown to administrators.
2. **User-visible strings.** Remove `<script>` and `<style>` blocks and HTML comments; take the
   text between tags with `{…}` expressions removed, and the values of `title`, `aria-label`,
   `placeholder`, `alt`, `label` and `description` attributes when they are literal strings.
   String literals inside `<script>` are out of scope for the first version.
3. **Words.** Two lists, both case-insensitive and whole-word, plurals included:
   - **banned** — `ruleset`, `rigour`, `repertoire`, `compendium`, `primer`, `bestow`,
     `render depth`, `phantom`, `table channel`: any hit fails;
   - **watched** — `piece`, `bridge`, `parked`, `mechanics`: common English, so each hit must
     match an entry in an allowlist kept beside the test (`{ file, text }`, with the reason), and
     a new hit fails until it is reviewed.
   A string that is an id (`core:ruleset/vis-itineris@1`, matched by the identifier grammar of §2) is
   skipped.
4. **Message.** One line per hit: `‹file›:‹line› shows "‹word›" — the interface says ‹plain word›
   (NOMENCLATURE §28)`, the plain word read from this table's list in the test.
5. **Proof.** A fixture string per list (one banned hit, one watched hit not allowlisted, one
   allowlisted hit, one id) proves the extractor and the matcher before the real files run.
6. **As written** (PLAN-ruleset-editor P3, 2026-10-22). `mechanic` is listed singular, so §28's
   _mechanics_ is its plural; a quoted attribute's literal parts count, its `{…}` does not. A last
   test holds Admin › Rulesets to every word of both lists but its own. ⏳ `REPORTED` lets through
   the banned hits the first run found in a file the programme did not touch —
   `RulesFitAuditDialog.svelte`: _any ruleset fits_, _Also in the ruleset, unused here_, _every
   ruleset fits as it is_ — until their copy is fixed; an allowlist or reported entry that stops
   matching fails. ★ The **parked** row's sentence (_From another ruleset; kept, not used here._
   under **Other rulesets**) says a banned word: built as written, it fails this test. The owner
   rewords it or rules it an exception.
7. **The catalogue half** (lane G0, 2026-10-23, PLAN-genres-seams S7):
   `sdk-tests/catalogueVocabulary.test.ts` holds the core catalogue's member-facing strings — genres
   (name, description, `about`, player label, handbook, envoys, shape hints, fields), presets,
   actions, step statuses and member-set cards with their switches — to the banned list above plus
   _piece_, _binding_, _config_, _reckoning_ and _sweep_, with _bridge_, _parked_ and _mechanic_
   watched; and a routine's duties card is titled by its routine's name.
- **2026-10-28 (speech, per-level switches).** Added **silent timbre** and **spoken playback** (§10 Speech vocabulary): three levels, three meanings — session makes audio (Read aloud), character is spoken (Spoken aloud), person hears it (Spoken lines).
- **2026-10-29 (speech, voice try-out + pin).** Added **voice try-out** and **voice seed** (§10 Speech vocabulary): a try speaks one line and stores nothing; the seed is the entry's or, when the card sets one, the card's. Neither is the voice's `previewUrl`, the run seed, the seed line or a seed key.
- **2026-10-29 (voice loadouts).** Added **voice form** (§10 Speech vocabulary); amended **voicebank** (entries live on a loadout: one pair per voice, through its loadout; `connection_model_id` dropped, 0135 adds `loadout_id`, 0136 drops the model), **timbre** and **narration voice** (the card picks an override narrator from the voicebank; no narration prose). **`timbre.narrationDescription` retired** (§23). The Narration loadout is no longer the one place voices live.
- **2026-10-29 (speech follow-ups).** Added **message settled**, **spoken pending**, **envoy voice**, **narration voice**, **narration default** (§10 Speech vocabulary); **speech tail** retired (§23). Collisions: **message settled** ⚠ not `message-completed@1`, not the **settle line** / **settled** / `history-settled@1`; **narration voice** is one word at four scopes (card · envoy · session · pub), always qualified; **narration default** ⚠ not the Narration loadout; **spoken pending** ⚠ not a run's generating state. No other new meanings.
- **2026-10-30 (narration fallback).** Added **loadout voice**, **other speakers**, **auto voice pick** (§10 Speech vocabulary); amended **voicebank** (no stars), **envoy voice** (no description fields), **narration voice** (pub scope becomes the loadout voice; new `VoiceFrom` set and resolution order). Retired **narration default**, the voicebank stars and the envoy description fields (§23). Collisions: **loadout voice** ⚠ not the loadout's sampling `voice`; **other speakers** ⚠ not the cast; **auto voice pick** is always qualified, since **Auto** is also a UI word and a `VoiceFrom` value. `EnvoyDecl.casting` (SDK, one optional field) ⚠ collides with spell**casting** — recorded on the **auto voice pick** row, rename open (★).

A port held by a process that is not ours fails the start with the **port-in-use** sentence (`portInUseMessage`: _Port N is already in use by a program Serene Pub didn't start. Stop it, or change the port in …_); our own leftover (pid file + binary match) is killed and replaced; `checkForOrphanOnBoot` keeps its name and only reaps. Managed-mode preflight starts when `isRunning()` is false, never because the port is quiet. New 🚧 **process watchdog** (`managed/watchdog.ts`: `spawnWatchdog` · `WatchdogSpawn` · `WATCHDOG_SOURCE` · `WATCHDOG_FILE_NAME` = `serene-pub-watchdog.mjs`, written beside the pid file; `TreeSignal` in `processTree.ts`): a detached Node sidecar per managed child that ends the child's tree when this process dies by any means. Always qualified (R3): ⚠ not the **idle watchdog** (`createIdleWatchdog`, `connectionAdapters/idleTimeout.ts`), which times out a quiet streamed reply. ⚠ *External mode* (`koboldCppManagedMode = "external"`, the admin's own KoboldCPP reached by address) is a setting, not adoption, and is unchanged.
